## 27 November 2026, v0.223: the glass engine draws the docked panels (task GS1, glass step 1)
> Plan `docs/glass-engine-plan.md`, sections 3.1 to 3.5 (the user's Mac tests are binding): "the engine draws its own backdrop on the GPU", levels Glass / Light / Solid, "backdrop-filter is not used for these surfaces at all", defaults lens Wide 45 px and blur Light, "on this Mac at this window size it must deliver 100 % of frames with room to spare".

Started after task D1 (v0.222, commit 527b6d5) and task G2b (engine 2.0, commit 6765edd) were on main. While this run worked, tasks G2c, G2d and G2e put engine 2.1.0, 2.2.0 and 2.3.0 on main, with the user's Mac runs of the test page (plan 3.6 to 3.8: with 2.1 every row holds 240 fps there; square panels showed a rounded band in their corners, fixed in 2.2; 2.3 changes rounded panels only). The app got the newest engine (see below), so no separate port ("GS1b") is needed for that. The audio path is not touched; no desktop shell file changed (no desktop build needed).

**Not proven here: the frame rate.** The cloud machine has no graphics card (Chromium's software renderer). Every time below says only that less work is asked for, not what the Mac will show. The user's check on the Mac (3840x2027 at 240 Hz) decides whether step 1 is good.

### What was there before
- Track headers (`#hglass`) and transport (`#tr`): `backdrop-filter` with the SVG lens (`feImage` map) and a live blur. Device panel (`#fxglass`): a blurred picture of the arrangement (`#arrBlur`, made by `abDraw` on a 2D canvas after every arrangement change). Behind live glass a half-size copy of the arrangement (`#arrBack`, `gbCopy`, up to 120 copies a second).
- A frame in which only the playhead moved copied the whole arrangement canvas back from a snapshot and drew the playhead on it; the snapshot was a full canvas copy after every full drawing. With Follow centre no snapshot was kept, so every playing frame was a full drawing.

### Built (edit script `tools/edits/taskGS1.py`, app code `tools/edits/taskGS1_block.js`, every replacement asserted unique)
- **The engine in the app**: `tools/glass-lab/glass-engine.js` (2.3.0 from task G2e, with one method added for the app, `setBackdropColor`; the version number is not raised because the module's own checks ask for it) is pasted unchanged into the block "v0.223 (task GS1, glass step 1)" before `askChoice`. One WebGL2 canvas `#glassCv`, first child of `#main`, under `#arr`. Faces for `#hglass`, `#tr`, `#fxglass` and `#fxband` (the tab band is switched off by the app's CSS since an earlier version, so it has no face today; it gets one by itself if it is shown again).
- **Backdrop drawn on the graphics card** (rule 1): `gleBuild` makes the rectangle list from the values `drawArr` and `drawClip` use (lane backgrounds, per clip a body and a title band in the track colour, selected and muted clips as `drawClip` paints them, the darker area below the last track and after the song's end, the playhead as one rectangle). `gleSig` is one number over all of it; after a full `drawArr` the list is sent again only when that number changed. Scroll and horizontal zoom are one uniform, the playhead is one uniform (in 2 px steps, 4 px at Light: under frost a finer step cannot be seen). **No canvas is copied or uploaded on this path**: `#arrBack` is an empty 2 x 2 layer that only passes clicks on, `#arrBlur` is not made, `gbCopy` and `abDraw` copy nothing.
- **Levels** (rule 2): Glass = engine with lens; Light = the same engine, lens off, an eighth-size backdrop refreshed 30 times a second; Solid = no engine at all (canvas and context freed), solid panels. Solid is also what a computer without WebGL2 gets. `#hglass, #tr, #fxglass, #fxband` have `backdrop-filter: none !important` at every level; `rfUpdate` returns at once for them, so the old lens makes no map and no filter for them. `rfAttach` / `rfBuild` / `rfMap` / `rfStyle` and the `feImage` lens stay for windows, sheets and menus (step 3 removes them).
- **Settings > Performance, "Docked panels"**: Glass level (Glass / Light / Solid), Lens (Off / Fine / Apple / Wide), Frosting (Light / Regular / Heavy), plain buttons with tooltips, no sliders. Defaults Wide and Light (rule 3). The level follows the Light mode slider (Full effects and Optimised = Glass, Lighter = Light, Lightest = Solid, which is also how existing choices are carried over) until one is picked here; moving the slider puts it back on the slider. Saved in `UI.gl`. The texts of the slider stops say what they mean now; the old effect switches are headed "Windows, sheets and menus".
- The docked panels keep their own see-through tint on top of the engine's picture (the Transparency slider still works); it has its own value `--gad`, so they are glass at Lighter too, where everything else is solid. A panel with nothing of the arrangement behind it (Solid, no WebGL2, the piano roll in full screen, the transport in a layout where it sits above the map) is solid (`glsol`).
- **Playhead as its own layer** (`#arrPhW`, G1): a thin canvas with the line and the Follow button, painted only when its look changes and moved with a transform in whole screen pixels; the small arrow at the edge is a second tiny canvas. The arrangement canvas no longer contains the playhead, so a playhead-only frame does not touch it and no snapshot is made after a full drawing. The overview keeps its old way.
- **Follow centre** (G1): frames in which the view did not move a pixel are now playhead-only frames (nothing drawn). A full drawing still happens for every pixel the view moves; at a deep zoom that is still every frame (see "Not done").
- **Transport** (G1): the logo glow, the meters, the time text and the CPU graph no longer sit inside a filtered element, because the transport has no filter any more: its glass is the engine's canvas, a separate layer under it. Nothing had to be moved in the page for that.
- **Window drags** (G1): a floating window's title bar keeps the pointer once the drag has really started (`setPointerCapture`), and a cancelled pointer ends the drag.
- **Edge light of windows and menus** used to read the blurred picture; it now reads a 384 x 216 copy of the arrangement, only while such a panel is open, at most 11 times a second.
- **Background freeze** (task AO): the engine is drawn at the end of `frame0`, so held-back frames stop it.
- Engine module: `setBackdropColor` added (the colour outside the track rows follows the theme). Everything else is task G2e's 2.3.0 as it is; the app does not use `setOrigin`, `setBackdropRate` or `setBounds` (plan 3.7: not needed). The app has one engine canvas.
- **Corners and edges** (engine 2.2 and 2.3, plan 3.7 and 3.8): the docked panels are square, so they get the square lens (no rounded band in the corners). The app names the free edges itself (`gleEdges`), because its panels lie against things that are not glass: the track headers bend only on the edge towards the arrangement, the device panel only on its top edge under the track tabs, the transport only while no device panel lies against it (devices folded or popped out).

### Measured (`tools/glass-lab/bench.py --capped --reps 2 --win 3 --scen a,b,e`, software renderer, 1600x1000, 60 Hz cap; compositor time per presented frame = viz + gpu thread)
| Scene, "Full effects" | v0.222 | v0.223 (the app code as released, with engine 2.2 in it) |
|---|---|---|
| idle, stopped | 0.33 + 0.47 = 0.80 ms | 0.15 + 0.14 = 0.29 ms |
| playing | 0.41 + 0.66 = 1.07 ms | 0.15 + 0.27 = 0.42 ms |
| scrolling and zooming the arrangement | 0.43 + 0.52 = 0.95 ms | 0.27 + 0.29 = 0.56 ms |

Two earlier runs of the same app code with engine 2.0 and 2.1 in it gave 0.28 / 0.41 / 0.30 and 0.30 / 0.32 / 0.32 ms, so the spread between runs on this machine is about as large as the last row shows. "Optimised" (picture blur before, the engine now): idle 0.28 to 0.34 ms, playing 0.46 to 0.38 ms, scrolling 0.35 to 0.30 ms (no real difference). "Lighter" (solid before, the engine at Light now): idle 0.22 to 0.24 ms; its playing row stalled for seconds in all three runs of the new build while the trace was recorded and cannot be used. Checked apart, without a trace, 5 s playing at Lighter, three runs each: 184, 216 and 238 frames shown on v0.222, 169, 178 and 202 on v0.223, the longest gap under 100 ms in both. So **on this machine, which has no graphics card, Lighter got about a tenth slower while playing**: Lighter used to be solid, and the engine at Light is worked out by the processor here. On a computer with a graphics card that work goes to the card; where the browser itself reports software WebGL the engine is refused and the panels are Solid, as before. At Full effects the same check gives 113 and 121 frames in 4 s on v0.222 and 171 and 172 on v0.223. bench.py now accepts a build with the engine (it used to stop when the header had no SVG lens).

The app's own work per frame (`FPS.js`, same machine, Fractals song): playing without Follow 4.3 to 2.0 ms; playing with Follow centre at the start-up zoom 9.6 to 4.6 ms (full drawings 95 of 95 frames before, 15 of 116 now); Follow centre zoomed in to 40 px a beat 12.6 to 9.2 ms (still a full drawing on every frame, without the snapshot and the copies).

## 27 November 2026, desktop app: the Mac icon stays blue under the Dark icon style (task IC1)

Reading: on the user's Mac in dark mode the app icon had a black background (white rings, yellow dots). Wanted: always the blue square with the Ocean Yellow W7 logo. `index.html` is not touched; only `desktop/`, `.github/workflows/`, `tools/` and `docs/`. Full write-up with sources: `docs/app-icon-mac-styles.md`.

### Found
- The black icon is drawn by macOS 26 itself. Under System Settings > Appearance > Icon & widget style > Dark it makes its own dark version of every app icon that has none: background colour out, black tile in, light parts kept. The app shipped only `icon.icns`, so it got that. **Reproduced** on GitHub's macOS 26.7.2 machine with the released desktop app (DMG 0.219, the newest one): kept in the Dock and closed, style Dark, the tile is black (`docs/app-icon-mac-styles/dock-macos26.png`, first row).
- The released app while it is **open** is blue under Dark: the picture the app sets on the Dock (`dock-icon.png`) is left alone by macOS (second row). So the black one is what shows in Finder, Launchpad, Spotlight and on the Dock tile of the closed app.
- No old build and no wrong file is involved: `icon.icns`, `dock-icon.png` and the picker pictures are as the scheduling chat said.

### Built
- An Icon Composer icon, written by hand: `desktop/icon-assets/mac-icon/AppIcon.icon` (`icon.json` + `Assets/mark.png`, made by `make_icon.py` from the W7 source). Fill = Ocean blue for the default, the dark and the tinted appearance; one layer with the white rings and the yellow dots; glass, shine, shadow and translucency off.
- `desktop/scripts/build-mac-icon.sh` compiles it with `actool` (picks the newest Xcode 26 or later; the release runner `macos-15-intel` has one beside its default Xcode 16.4) into `build/Assets.car`. `package.json`: `CFBundleIconName = AppIcon` and `Assets.car` into `Contents/Resources`. `icon.icns` and `CFBundleIconFile` stay as they were. `afterPack.js` stops a release build before the DMG if either icon or either key is missing.
- `desktop/main.js`: on macOS 26 and later with `Assets.car` in the bundle the default icon sets no Dock picture any more (the bundle icon shows, blue in Default and Dark); coming back from one of the other 48 icons hands the Dock back with `setIcon(null)`. The other 48 icons, and macOS 15 and older, work as before.
- `.github/workflows/desktop.yml`: the Mac build compiles the icon first; new job "Mac icon proof" on `macos-26` takes the finished DMG, checks Info.plist, `icon.icns` byte for byte and `Assets.car` (the three appearances, each with the blue tile), lets macOS draw the icon in the four styles, photographs the Dock, uploads the pictures (artifact `mac-icon-proof`) and fails if Default or Dark is not blue. `.github/workflows/mac-icon-check.yml`: the same look without a build, run by hand.
- Two traps, both seen on the build machine and written into the doc: a plain `fill` key beside `fill-specializations` makes the dark entry ignored (black again); and the first answer of the icon service for a new app can be the old automatic picture.

### Proof (on GitHub's macOS 26.7.2 machine, no Mac here)
- `assetutil --info Assets.car`: the layered AppIcon for `NSAppearanceNameAqua`, `NSAppearanceNameDarkAqua` and `ISAppearanceTintable`, the tile of each the colour 0.078, 0.314, 0.659.
- macOS drawing the icon of the really built app (`NSWorkspace`, style set with `AppleIconAppearanceTheme`): Default blue, **Dark blue, 0.00 difference to Default** at 512 px, tile colour 21, 80, 168 (wanted 20, 80, 168). The app with `icon.icns` only: Dark black. Picture: `docs/app-icon-mac-styles/styles-macos26.png`.
- A real Dock under Dark, both apps kept in it: released 0.219 black, new build blue, closed and open (`dock-macos26.png`, rows 3 and 4).
- Default against today's `dock-icon.png` at 512 px: the tile box is the same (50 to 461 px, so no grey plate, same margin); mean difference inside the tile 1.6 of 255, 1.4 % of pixels off by more than 24, on ring edges and the thin light rim macOS 26 adds. The old `.icns` as macOS 26 draws it is further from the reference (3.2).
- `tools/ui-tests/taskAH_electron.js`: 21 checks, all pass (4 new: macOS 26 start sets no Dock picture, another icon sets its picture, back to Ocean Yellow gives null, no page errors).
- Windows: `desktop/build/icon.ico` not touched (sha256 62cbbba8..., the same as in v0.219); `icon.icns` not touched (23beac77...); the Windows part of `package.json` and the Windows path in `main.js` unchanged.

### What macOS decides (cannot be blue)
- **Tinted** and **Clear**: macOS removes every app's colours by design (one tint colour, or grey glass). The shape stays W7.
- macOS 26 draws an Icon Composer icon at every size from the same layers, so the hand-drawn small versions in `icon.icns` (simple logo at 16 to 20 px) are not used there any more; small icons show W7 scaled down.
- macOS 15 and older take flat pictures that `actool` also puts into `Assets.car` instead of `icon.icns` (seen on the macOS 15 machine: the same W7 with a faint light rim). The switch that should leave them out did nothing with Xcode 26.6.

### Not verified without a real Mac
- The user's Mac itself (Finder, Launchpad, Spotlight, Dock) and its icon cache after replacing the app.
- `setIcon(null)` against a real Dock (tested against a recording stand-in; if Electron refused it the code sets the old blue picture).
- Tinted and Clear in a real Dock.

### For the user to check
1. Install the newest DMG. With the style on Dark (or Automatic in dark mode) the icon in Applications, Launchpad and the Dock (app closed and open) is the blue square.
2. Still black right after installing: log out and in once (icon cache).
3. Settings > App icon: another icon, then Ocean Yellow again: the Dock is blue again.

### Release
- Commit d4f8378 on main (no version change, `index.html` untouched, `update-notes.txt` left alone: the note belongs to the program version and there is no new one).
- Desktop build run 45933179423 dispatched with the GitHub tools at 03:16 UTC (the last release commit, v0.223, was 22 minutes old; no other build was running). All four jobs passed: release, Mac build (the icon compiled on `macos-15-intel`), Windows build, and "Mac icon proof" on macOS 26. It made the release **v0.223.0** (the newest desktop app before it was 0.219.0): `AudioLab-Pro-0.223.0-arm64.dmg` and the Windows installer.
- The proof job on the published DMG: `CFBundleIconName = AppIcon`, `icon.icns` byte for byte the file in the repository, `Assets.car` with the three appearances and the blue tile in each, signature valid, and the icon macOS draws for the app is blue in Default and in Dark (checked by the tile colour; its pictures are in the run's artifact `mac-icon-proof` and were not looked at by eye, the pictures in `docs/app-icon-mac-styles/` are from the same code built an hour earlier on the test branch).
- The test branches `ic1-test` and `ic1-proof` are left over if this session may not delete branches; nothing on them is needed.

No app changes: `index.html` and `desktop/` were not touched, no version. Plan: `docs/native-mac-plan.md`. Pick page: https://claude.ai/artifact/17AwgeWUCCTaDX1Ct3mmcn . Test app: https://github.com/Audio-lab-DAW/Audio-Lab-Pro-Alpha/releases/tag/native-lab-1 .

### Written
- **`docs/native-mac-plan.md`**: what was read in the app with numbers (31 worklet processors, 42 devices of which 19 are worklets and 16 are built on the browser's own nodes, 32 instruments, 1,238 presets, about 17 windows, 124 settings); four routes with cost in tasks and sources (Swift rewrite 230 to 370; shared C++ engine with native interface 245 to 400; the same engine with the present interface kept, 95 to 150 for the engine; JUCE and its prices); a plug-in hosting chapter (VST3 SDK is MIT since 3.8, a host's duties, folders, Intel-only plug-ins, crash protection and its cost, the device strip, state in the project file, why exports with a plug-in cannot be promised bit-identical, Audio Units, CLAP, and VST2 with its legal limits); the recommendation (route C as the road, B as the destination, C++, no framework for now); five stages that each work on the Mac, with the test that proves the sound at each; what can and cannot be checked without a Mac; distribution without an Apple account.

- **Test B**: `alvst3`, a command line VST3 host on Steinberg's SDK 3.8.1 behind a format-neutral interface (`native/host/plugin_api.h`), with scanning in a child process.
- **Test C**: "AudioLab VST3 test", a small AppKit app (list, load, the plug-in's own window, keys or a test pattern, output device and buffer, a report file).

The Mac's own `pow` and `exp` gave the same numbers as the browser for this device. Building with fused multiply-add allowed made no difference for this device.
- A: devices listed; default output opened; buffer set to 64 frames; device switched to 96 kHz and back; exclusive use taken and given back. Also on the virtual device BlackHole.
- B: 6 bundles scanned in child processes, one made to crash on purpose, host alive; Surge XT, Surge XT Effects, mda JX10, Note Expression Synth, ADelay and AGain loaded, played, state saved and restored, export mode, 96 kHz and 32 frames, 0 failed blocks. Surge XT: 19 microseconds per 128-frame block on average. Two fresh copies of Surge XT differ by up to -7.6 dB sample against sample: the measured reason exports with plug-ins cannot be promised identical.

### Built
- **Five pictures, one per start, drawn in code on the one canvas of the splash** (`SPLBG`, a script right after the splash at the top of `<body>`, about 11 kB; it has to sit there, before the app's code, so the picture is on screen at the first paint):
  - **Moons in resonance (S2)**: Io, Europa and Ganymede at 4, 2 and 1 orbits in the same time. New against the pick page: Jupiter stands in the centre where the logo was, as a fine circle with three faint bands, and the orbits and the planet are to scale (5.9, 9.4 and 15 Jupiter radii). The names ride on the moons.
  - **Harmonograph (S5)**: a pen on two slowing pendulums; one of 3:2, 4:3, 5:4 or 2:1 on each start, the next one after 13 s if the splash stays up. It starts with a third of the figure drawn and finishes in 4.5 s, because the splash is short.
  - **Dipole field (S1)**: field lines r = L sin²θ, tilted 10 degrees, with a small planet in line work in the centre; the lines begin at its surface. The charges now bounce between their two mirror points along their line (as trapped particles do), where the pick page let them run through. The lines fade out behind the name.
  - **Orbit chart (S7)**: H1, H2 and H3 circling at 1, 2 and 3 times the same rate around a small nucleus, tick ring, grid.
  - **Spectrogram (S6)**: the made-up 145 BPM pattern, rolling, in the upper 64 % of the card, fading into the card above the name.
- **Chance**: the four line drawings equal, the spectrogram a third of each of them (`SPEC_CHANCE = 1/3`, one constant in `SPLBG`). Never the same one twice in a row (the last one is kept in `localStorage` `audiolab-splash-last`). Because of that rule the long-run shares are 22.7 % for each of the four and 9.1 % for the spectrogram.
- **No logo, no text at the edges.** The atom is no longer drawn on the loading splash (the About window keeps it). Gone from the pick page versions: the captions in the corners, the date stamp, the Hz scale, "V 0.219 · READY". Kept: H1, H2, H3 and the moon names with their 4, 2, 1, which ride on the bodies. The line under the bar that named the loading step ("Starting the audio engine" ...) is no longer shown (it is still there for screen readers).

Moons cyan to blue with an amber end; harmonograph periwinkle to lilac; dipole blue with an amber end; orbit chart amber; spectrogram cyan to yellow (its own colour scale). The two small lines are lighter than before (contrast about 6 : 1; the version line was about 3 : 1).

The figure has the upper two thirds; the name, "Digital audio workstation", the version and the bar sit at the bottom; under them the hint line. All sizes follow the card. The card lies above the "Demo song loaded" message, which used to sit lower than the old small card.
- **Timing** (block "v0.224 (task SP1)" before `askChoice`, names `SP1`, `sp1Ready`, `sp1Close`): loading is unchanged (`bootRun` of v0.195: interface, audio engine, fonts, first picture, the page settled; the bar follows them). In that stretch "Click to continue" shows at the bottom; a click anywhere or any key closes it at once. A click on the card and a plain key are not passed on to the app (Space does not start the song); a click beside the card does what it does and also closes the splash; shortcuts with Ctrl or Cmd pass. **Before loading is done nothing closes it**: Esc used to close the loading splash at any time, it no longer does.

## 27 November 2026: task NB-N1 (native audio output and device control, as a helper)

No app changes: `index.html` and `desktop/` were not touched, no version. Running list: `docs/native-mac-build.md`. Test app 0.2: https://github.com/Audio-lab-DAW/Audio-Lab-Pro-Alpha/releases/tag/native-lab-2 .

Started in the NM1 session after the user's tests on their Mac and their words "yes continue ... do it without my input". Logged under task NB's name so that NB goes on from N2.

### Built
- **`alengine`** (`native/engine/`): owns the audio output, driven by JSON lines: devices and formats, open with rate, buffer, format and exclusive use, move to another device while playing, volume and mute, status; changes from outside come as events (volume, rate, buffer, exclusive, devices, default output). Sound comes in through a local socket and goes to the device untouched; a ring corrects itself when it runs empty or too full and counts it. Integer formats that the system does not mix are written by the engine itself (16, 24, 32 bit).
- **`native/bridge/engine-bridge.js`**: the desktop app's side as a plain Node module.
- **Test app 0.2**: Rate menu, "Exclusive use of the device", "Device volume" both ways, a device list that follows plugging, a clear line when the test pattern has nothing to play.
- Workflow `native-lab.yml`: engine checks, the hand-over test through the loop-back device, the Node bridge test, a picture of the app's main window.

### Tested (build machine, virtual M1, run 45939789700)
- Hand-over: 287,998 of 287,998 samples identical at the device, fed by a test program and fed by Node through the bridge. One earlier run had one gap of 1,456 samples in the Node test, together with one overload reported by the machine.
- Open 48 to 73 ms, switch while playing 64 to 124 ms, rate 48 to 96 kHz in 124 ms and noticed by the engine, buffers 256, 64 and 32 accepted, volume set and read back, a change by another program reported at once, exclusive use keeps a second program out (error 35).
- Arithmetic of the integer formats and of the ring: all checks pass on macOS and Linux.

## 27 November 2026: task NB-N2a (the road from the desktop shell to the native engine, proven outside the app)

No app changes: `index.html` and `desktop/` were not touched. Details and the table: `docs/native-mac-build.md`.

- **Built:** `tools/native-lab/electron-tap/` (a test program on the real shell, Electron 45.4.1): an AudioWorklet hands each 128-frame block through a message port from the audio thread straight to the shell's main process, which feeds `alengine` through `native/bridge/engine-bridge.js`. `tools/native-lab/stream_compare.py` compares what was sent with what the loop-back device recorded, bit for bit, and finds its place again after gaps.
- **Tested (build machine, run 45942655178, 20 s):** all 7,500 blocks arrived in both runs, nothing lost. Page clock from no device (`sinkId: none`): the page ran at 0.59 of real time, the ring ran empty 79 times, and every one of 1,920,000 samples that reached the device was identical. Page clock from a real device playing silence: 0.998 of real time, 1,917,384 of 1,920,000 identical, 5 gaps with 4 overloads reported by the machine.
- **Decided from it (changeable):** in N2 the page keeps a real device as its clock and plays silence into it; with exclusive use on the DAC that clock device must be another one. Blocks are sent as copies (transferred buffers arrive empty in the main process). N2 needs the smooth drift correction.
- **Not verified:** nothing inside AudioLab, no real DAC, nothing longer than 20 seconds, nothing on the M4.
- **Stopped here on purpose:** the next step needs a hook in `index.html` and changes in `desktop/`. Only one task may edit `index.html` at a time, the design chain is working there, and the user's order is design first, then the native engine. Task NB continues from N2 when it is fired in its turn.

## 27 November 2026, v0.225: the new About window, Earth with its radiation belts and the fine atom (task AB1)
> "I like E2. I like E3. Actually, E7 is better than E3. So let's have E7 and E2 randomized. One or the other opens. And let's make the animated logo on the top a little larger and more anatomically correct with more particles, more fidelity and resolution. Wanted to really fit in to the whole splash screen based on design rules. I want it to be really fine and subtle with small little particles and dots with high fidelity that would work on high resolution screens. I want it to look cool and subtle."

Started from the drawing code of the pick page of task SR7 (`docs/about-round-2.md`, read from the artifact). No other task had work in progress on `index.html` (the `NB-N1` wip commits touch only the native lab).

### How the picks were read
- Two pictures, **one at random each time About opens** (an even chance, no restart needed, the same one can come twice): **corner** = E2 "Corner chart" (large Earth low right, cut by the edge, soft glowing belts, 9 shells, 93 dots) and **sheet** = E7 "Chart sheet" (Earth on the left edge, 15 shells of thin contour lines, 100 dots). Each keeps its own placement and belt style.
- Shared by both, from the mix line: the Earth drawn as **S3** (drafted: heavier outline, graticule every 15 degrees, coastlines, night side shaded, axis ticks, turning), the content as **C3** (spec list), the logo as **L2** (the animated atom stays). E7 was S3 and C3 already; E2 becomes exactly the mix line.

### Built
- **The window** (`AB1`, block "v0.225 (task AB1)" before `askChoice`; CSS before `.dacv`, class `ab2` on `#splash.ab`). `showSplash(true)` now opens it (`showSplash` and `hideSplash` are wrapped once more; the loading splash, its preview and the old atom code are untouched, and the old `aboutHtml` is no longer called). Same window size as before (780 wide, 92 % of the height up to 860).
- **The picture**: one canvas behind everything; it stays in place while the list scrolls. No text in it. Field lines are dipole lines r = L cos²(latitude) around an axis leaning 9.2 degrees toward 80.8 N, 72.8 W; every dot sits on a drawn line and bounces between its two mirror points with the real speed profile (tables as in round 2); outer-belt lines with their electrons drift eastward, inner-belt lines with their protons westward; the Earth turns once in 4 minutes. New against the pick page: the Earth follows the real window (corner: 66 and 74 points from the right and bottom edge; sheet: on the left edge at 42.5 % of the height), lines beyond L 3 are drawn with 80 points instead of 40 (the large arcs showed corners), and the dark veil behind the text is measured from the page (the text column, the name, a soft round patch behind the atom) instead of fixed numbers. Dots inside the veil are drawn at about a fifth of their strength, as in round 2.
- **Colours from the picture** (round 2 table): ground #05080e to #0b1322, rules and outlines in the field-line blue #7aaaff, values and "Under the hood" in the outer belt's cyan #6ed0ee, text in blue-tinted greys #e8eef9, #a3b3cd, #8fa0bb, the "Lab" gradient cyan to blue. The warm tone of the inner belt (#f0a878) is used by the atom only. The amber heading, the purple in the name, the coloured icon tiles and the hint line at the bottom are gone.
- **Content, C3**: logo, name, "Digital audio workstation · Version", designed by Ilja V. Jakovliev, the eight values (version, build, audio engine, running at, instruments, effects, platform, cores) and the six highlighted features as a spec list with a hairline at the left of each entry, then "All 35 features" and "Check for updates", then the copyright line. Same facts as before, all from `AHF`; the six short value lines are the pick page's wording (`AB1` `SHORT`). "All 35 features" opens the full list in the same quiet style (six groups, name, measured value, one sentence; no icons, no cards) and the veil then covers the whole column; "Show less" closes it. Hovering a feature shows its sentence, as before.
- **The fine atom** (`FATOM`, one small piece: `FATOM.paint(g,cx,cy,size,t,o)` draws into any canvas context, `FATOM.canvas(cv,size,t,o)` sizes a canvas for the screen and draws). The AudioLab mark as particles: three orbits at 30, 90 and 150 degrees, each a circle seen so that it shows as an ellipse 0.42 wide (the proportions of `mark-colour.svg`), a small nucleus, one warm electron as in the mark. 384 fine dots on the three orbits (each on its own circle, slightly spread in radius and tilt), 80 fainter ones on other circles further in, a nucleus of 52 dots (half warm, half pale), three electrons with a short tail: 519 in all. Every particle runs on a proper circle around the nucleus at the speed Kepler's rule gives for its radius (one turn in 11 s on the main orbits, faster closer in); particles behind the nucleus are hidden, the far half of each orbit is dimmer and smaller, the near half brighter; the whole atom sways a few degrees so the depth shows. Hairline orbits (0.6 points), dots 0.4 to 0.7 points. 116 points across (the pick page's atom was 72). Drawn at the device pixel ratio (and the app's zoom) up to 3, at sub-pixel positions, no scaling of a ready picture, no blur. Nothing outside About uses it yet (the nav logo and the old atom code are unchanged); it is meant for the orbit loader of task MD1 later.

### Cost
- One canvas for the picture, one small one for the atom. The picture at most 30 times a second, the atom at most 60, both from one frame request. Picture canvas at most 2 pixels per point. No blur, no shadows. Nothing is worked out before About is opened for the first time (tables, coastlines and particles are built then).

## 27 November 2026, v0.227: windows, sheets and menus on the glass engine, backdrop-filter nowhere (task GS2, glass step 2)
> Plan `docs/glass-engine-plan.md`, section 3.1 "Step 2" and 2.4 option a, under the binding Mac rules of 3.2 to 3.5: the engine draws its own backdrop on the graphics card and never copies the full-size arrangement canvas; levels Glass, Light, Solid; "backdrop-filter is used nowhere, not even as a fallback"; defaults lens Wide 45 px and blur Light; "Moving a window costs one quad redraw, no scene or pyramid rebuild".

Started after task D3 was released (v0.226, commit 30cd5e5); "task GS2" was not in this log. Main moved only by the CLAUDE.md commit of task HR1 before the start; nobody else touched `index.html` during the run. The audio path is not touched; no desktop shell file changed (no desktop build).

**Not proven here: the frame rate.** The cloud machine has no graphics card (SwiftShader) and two cores that this renderer keeps busy; the times below only say how much work is asked for. The user's check on the Mac decides.

### What was there before
- 18 elements with `backdrop-filter` when the mixer was open (605,000 px of live blur): the mixer window at 27 px blur over the arrangement with its tab `.fwh` and every pan handle `.ck` (1.6 px) as glass on glass; sheets, menus, pop-ups, the update window, spectrum windows and some small things inside devices with their own blurs; the SVG lens (`rfAttach`) on menus, sheets and the master pop-up.

### Built (edit script `tools/edits/taskGS2.py`, app code `tools/edits/taskGS2_block.js`, every replacement asserted unique)
- **`backdrop-filter` nowhere**, at any level: one CSS rule for every element and pseudo element. The nested blurs in the mixer (tab, pan handles) are gone with it. The few small things that had a blur of their own got a slightly more opaque background (toast, layout presets inside Settings, visualizer pane, EQ overlay, device header buttons, export overlay).
- **Floating glass on the engine**: floating windows (mixer, devices, envelopes, grid, Venom, bounce, audio devices, visualizer), the sidechain window, spectrum windows, pinned devices, the mixer's tab, sheets (Settings, askChoice, the audio to MIDI pop-up and every other dialog), the update window, menus and pop-ups. Each is one face; the element keeps its own tint, border, CSS shadow and content.
- **Layers, not a face per window** (measured below): up to three more engines, each on one full-window canvas put into the page's stacking order directly before the lowest element it serves, with its z-index. An element that overlaps another floating element goes one layer up. A layer with nothing to show is hidden and draws nothing. A fourth level of overlap is solid.
- **Backdrop on the graphics card**: the docked engine's rectangle list (sent to a layer only when it changed), view and playhead as uniforms. **0 uploads.** Overview and full-screen piano roll: small copies (capped), as the docked engine does.
- **Glass never samples glass** (plan 2.4 option a): what a face covers that is not the arrangement is fed as flat pictures: the docked panels in the theme's panel colour, the device displays and the piano roll as small copies (at most the 12 largest; refreshed only where a face covers them, at most 20 times a second while playing and twice a second when stopped), and floating elements of a lower layer in their own colour. No flat source is an engine canvas.
- **Moving a window** is one face redraw: no list, no backdrop, no blur pyramid. The mixer's tab face reaches under the window, so the window's square top right corner is glass too.
- **Levels** follow the docked panels: Glass (lens), Light (no lens, 30 backdrops a second), Solid and no WebGL2 and Lightest: no layer at all, the floating elements solid.
- **Settings, Performance**: the glass block is now "Glass: docked panels, windows, sheets and menus"; the old Refraction, Blur and "Softer blur while playing" rows say that they change nothing now (kept so saved choices and tests still work); slider stop texts updated.
- **Old lens code** kept but unused: `rfAttach` makes nothing, `rfUpdate` only clears; `rfBuild`, `rfMap`, `rfStyle` and the `feImage` lens are still in the file for step 3.
- `bench.py`: the drag scenario now grabs a free spot of the mixer's tab (it aimed at the hidden title, so before this its "dragging" row moved nothing); new row `glf_face`.

### Measured (`tools/glass-lab/bench.py --capped --reps 2 --win 3 --scen c,d`, Fractals song, 1600x1000, software renderer; two runs each; compositor = gpu + viz thread time per presented frame)
| Scene | v0.226 | v0.227, layers (released) | v0.227, a face per window (`glf_face`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| playing, mixer open: frames per second | 8.4, 6.5 | 7.2, 5.7 | 8.1, 12.5 |
| playing, mixer open: compositor ms per frame | 1.22, 1.39 | 0.66, 0.72 | 0.68, 0.66 |
| dragging the mixer: frames per second | 13.5, 6.7 | 12.6, 13.9 | 6.8, 12.8 |
| dragging the mixer: compositor ms per frame | 2.53, 2.62 | 0.47, 0.42 | 0.86, 0.42 |
| elements with backdrop-filter / px | 18 / 605,000 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Reading: the compositor work per frame is about half while playing and a fifth while dragging. The frame rates on this machine are noise: both cores are saturated by the software renderer in every row (1,750 to 1,920 ms of CPU per second), so they say nothing for the Mac. **Layers or a face per window**: the face mode draws fewer pixels when nothing moves (its canvas is only as large as the window), which is why it can look as good or better while playing here, but each move of the window draws the backdrop and the blur again (counted in the test), it needs one more graphics context per open window, and the Mac test page (plan 3.7) showed two full-window engine layers over the arrangement holding 240 fps. The task's rule "moving a window costs one quad redraw, no scene or pyramid rebuild" decides it: **layers**. If the Mac shows a cost for the floating layer's full-window canvas, the fitted canvas is the fallback that is already built.

## 27 November 2026, v0.228: glass step 3, the old lens code removed, and where the app's own drawing spends its frames (task GS3)
> Plan `docs/glass-engine-plan.md` section 3.1 "Step 3" (delete `rfAttach`, `rfBuild`, `rfMap`, `rfStyle`, the `feImage` lens), held back by the user "until I confirm the frame rate on my Mac". The user's report on v0.223 in the real app (Mac mini M4, 240 Hz): "The glass is running at like 180 frames a second when you don't touch anything, and when you start moving the arrangement panel around and the settings are on top with the glass effect, it still stays around 100, 120 ... The lowest I've seen was 90 FPS, so that's a big improvement. Very good. And it looks good." The engine test page on the same Mac held 240 fps with 100 % of frames in every row (engine 2.3.0, 2194x1139 at 1.75x), so the gap comes from the rest of the app's drawing.

Started after task GS2 was released (v0.227, commit 326e89b, and the docs commit 9cd4f83); "task GS3" was not in this log and nobody else had `index.html` work in progress. The audio path is not touched; no desktop shell file changed (no desktop build). The local clone held the history from before task HR1 on its `main`; per CLAUDE.md it was not used: the work was done on a branch made from `origin/main`.

**Not proven here: the frame rate on the Mac.** The cloud machine has two cores and no graphics card (SwiftShader); every frame rate below is set by that software renderer. What carries over to the Mac are the counts: how often something is drawn, and how many frames the compositor really puts together.

### 1. The old lens code is gone (edit script `tools/edits/taskGS3.py`, every replacement asserted unique)
- The SVG lens: `rfMap`, `rfBuild`, `rfStyle`, `rfAttach`'s body, the `feImage` map, the `RFX` table and its ResizeObserver. `rfAttach`, `rfUpdate`, `rfAll` stay as empty calls because older code still calls them. The overrides GS1 and GS2 had put on top of them are gone too.
- The blurred picture: `#arrBlur` and its CSS, `abDraw`, `fxBlurPic`, the `ABL` table, the device-band wrapper of `abDraw`. The half-size copy behind live glass (`gbCopy`'s copy): `gbCopy` and `gbTick` are now one definition each (the click layer `#arrBack` stays 2 x 2). The edge light's old reader of the blurred picture: `elTick` is now only the version from glass step 1 (a 384 x 216 copy of the arrangement, only while a window or menu is open).
- `backdrop-filter`: 90 declarations removed from the CSS and inline styles; the one guard rule from GS2 (`*,*::before,*::after{backdrop-filter:none!important}`) stays, so none can come back by accident.
- The Glass preview on Settings > Glass and light (a picture that imitated the old levels: refraction bands, blur from a picture, live blur), with its chips and its loop. The page keeps Transparency and Edge light. **Visible change**: the preview is gone, as are the Blur and Refraction cards.
- Settings that changed nothing any more: Blur and Refraction on Glass and light; on Performance the rows Refraction, Blur, Softer blur while playing and Half-size picture behind glass ("changes nothing now" since GS2). "Softer blur while playing" also stopped calling `applyTrans` at every start and stop. The remaining rows are headed "Other effects" (Edge light, Animations). The texts of the Light mode stops say what they do now (glass with or without the lens on panels, windows and menus).
- Stored choices: `UI.blur`, `UI.glPlay`, `UI.glBack` are dropped once at start (checked with a profile that had them); `UI.refr` and `UI.fx` stay (the first start of an older version reads them; `fx.edge` and `fx.anim` are still used).

### 2. Where the frames go (`tools/ui-tests/frametime.py`)
The harness runs the real app at the user's size (2194 x 1139 CSS px at 1.75x, 3840 x 1993 device px), Fractals song open (31 tracks, 364 clips), Full effects, glass engine at Glass on SwiftShader WebGL2. Scenes: idle; the arrangement scrolled sideways on every frame (the same `V.x` / `dirty` path the wheel uses); the same with Settings open over it; playing from beat 128; playing with the mixer open. One part switched off at a time: the 2D arrangement (`drawArr`, `drawMap`), meters, clip waveforms and notes (`drawClipC`), the Settings window (its logo loop and the sheet), the glass canvases (`render` of every engine), the repeating timers that only update the screen (the ones the background freeze stops), the mixer's drawing. Per row: frames per second (rAF), frames the compositor really put together per second (trace, "presented"), main-thread time per frame (Chromium's own counters), script time, style and layout, kept % (frames within 1.5 times the median), the slowest frame.

**What costs, v0.227** (frames per second with one part switched off; uncapped, one run of 3 s each; the machine is saturated in every row, so only large differences mean something):

| Part switched off | idle | scrolling | scrolling, Settings open | playing | playing, mixer open |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| nothing | 56.8 | 6.0 | 4.2 | 37.6 | 7.4 |
| 2D arrangement | 58.9 | **78.9** | **30.2** | 42.2 | **18.7** |
| meters | 48.8 | 6.9 | 3.8 | 34.7 | 9.2 |
| clip waveforms and notes | 62.8 | 8.2 | 4.4 | 29.4 | 5.1 |
| the Settings window | | | **7.6** | | |
| glass canvases | 54.6 | **34.9** | **25.2** | 35.2 | **13.3** |
| screen timers | 57.8 | 7.3 | 4.3 | 38.5 | 7.8 |
| the mixer's drawing | | | | | 8.1 |

Reading: while scrolling, the full drawing of the arrangement canvas on every frame is the largest cost by far, then the glass canvases that are drawn again for the new view, then (with Settings open) the Settings window. CPU profile of the slowest scene (scrolling with Settings open, v0.227): 76 % "(program)" (the renderer's own canvas and compositing work, not script), 10 % `drawImage` (the arrangement canvas being finished when its header column is copied to `#arrCol`), 3 % the atom painters of the Settings logo, 1.3 % `querySelectorAll`. Script in the app is small in every scene.

**What changed every frame while nothing moved** (counted, not timed): with nothing playing the master meter in the top bar was drawn 120 times a second (1,625 canvas calls in 3 s, also in silence); the dot of the capture button pulsed through an opacity animation, which the compositor runs on every screen frame, so an idle window was put together again on every frame (on a 240 Hz screen: 240 times a second); the logo in Settings drew up to 160 pictures a second (about 1,500 canvas calls each). The top-bar logo draws 30 pictures a second (asked for by the user, task AO).

### 3. The fixes (none touches the audio path)
- **Capture dot**: the same pulse (1.6 s) changes the dot's colour in 12 steps instead of its opacity, so it is a few repaints of a 6 px dot a second and no longer a compositor animation. Measured: frames the compositor put together while idle went from 57 to 30 a second at 60 Hz (on a 240 Hz screen the pulse alone made 240). **Visible change**: the pulse is stepped (about 7 steps a second) instead of smooth.
- **Master meter**: draws only when what it shows changed (positions to a quarter pixel, peak hold, size). 1,625 calls in 3 s idle before, 0 now; while playing it moves as before.
- **Settings logo**: at most 60 pictures a second (was up to 160). On this machine Settings runs at about 21 frames a second, under the cap, so the count is the same here (104,721 and 103,158 calls in 3 s); on the Mac it is at most three eighths of what it was.
- **Layout reads in `drawArr`**: where the "add track" row sits and how tall the header column is are kept until the header column is given new row heights or classes, an edit happens or the window changes (each was a forced layout on every full drawing). Layouts per frame while scrolling: 1.88 to 1.87; the forced reads are gone, the rest is the page's own.

**Before and after, all parts on** (same harness, same machine; uncapped run first, then two runs at the 60 Hz limit):

| playing, mixer open (uncapped) | 7.4 | 8.6 | 15.8 | 6.7 | 157 | 134 | 59 | 65 | 348 / 293 |

Reading: **idle now draws only what changes**: about 30 compositor frames a second (the logo) instead of one per screen frame, and on this machine the idle rate rose from 57 to 78 frames a second uncapped. In the moving scenes the frames the app asks for are the same (the content really changes every frame), but the compositor no longer puts the window together a second time in between for the capture dot: at 60 Hz it made 55 frames a second while the app drew 4 to 7; now it makes as many as the app draws. On the Mac that is the work of a full 3840 x 2027 window per extra frame, up to 240 a second, taken away from scrolling and playing. The app's own rates in the moving scenes are within this machine's noise (both cores busy in every row).

### 4. Tried and left out: scrolling by shifting the picture
The table says the full drawing of the arrangement is what scrolling costs, so the obvious fix was tried: when only the view moved, shift the old picture by whole screen pixels and draw only the strips that changed (the new edge, the part next to the track headers where names stay put, the ruler band, the master lane, the right edge), the view put on the screen's pixel grid so the result is the same picture. It was built and checked pixel for pixel against a full drawing (identical except the last column, which also differs between two full drawings in a row), with safety nets (a full drawing after 48 shifted ones, a second, or 6 frames after the view stops; any other change draws in full). **Measured, one drawing of the arrangement with a 1-pixel read-back so the raster work is counted** (median of 40): full 35 to 41 ms, shifted 40 to 57 ms with one clip made of several rectangles, about the same with each strip drawn as its own pass through a second canvas. Why, from profiles: drawing the canvas onto itself makes the browser copy it first (22 ms here, 5 ms through a second canvas); a clip made of several rectangles is not cheaper than the whole drawing for this renderer; and copying a full-window picture costs this software renderer about as much as drawing it. On a graphics card those copies are nearly free, so it might pay there, but that cannot be measured here, so it is **not in the app**. The first version is kept, unused, as `tools/edits/taskGS3_shift_experiment.js`.

### 5. The frame-rate read-out
Settings > Performance, under Frame limit: "Frame-rate read-out on screen" (off by default, saved in `UI.fpsHud`). A small badge in the bottom right corner on top of everything, never taking a click: the frames per second now (green at 95 % of the screen rate or more, yellow at 70 %, red below) and the **slowest single frame of the last 5 seconds** in milliseconds, updated twice a second, in its own layer so its text changing repaints nothing else. The Performance tab's own frame-rate graph (only while the tab is open) is unchanged.

## 27 November 2026: task NB-N2b (the clock follower, and the bridge's shell and page pieces, ready for the hook)

No app changes: `index.html` was not touched (task AB2 had work in progress there when this run started, and the design chain comes first by the user's order). `desktop/` got only the bridge, idle until the page asks; no version, no desktop build. Running list: `docs/native-mac-build.md`.

### Built
- **The clock follower** (`native/engine/follow.h`, `ring.h`): N2a showed that the page's clock and the DAC's clock drift. A second reading mode for the engine's ring, `follow`: a 48-tap Kaiser-windowed sinc (4,096 phases) reads between the samples at a speed steered by how full the ring is (PI control in seconds of fill, critically damped, settles in about a minute, limited to 2,000 ppm unless the source asks for more). `exact` stays the default and is unchanged: every sample handed over untouched, rare counted corrections. Chosen per sound source (`"clock":"exact"|"follow"`) or switched with the new `clock` command; status shows the speed (`ppm`, `ppmMin`, `ppmMax`). `alengine 0.2`.
- **The desktop shell's side** (`desktop/native-engine.js`, registered in `main.js` in a try like the AI voices): finds `alengine` (packaged `Resources/bin`, `desktop/bin`, `native/build`, or `AL_ENGINE`), starts it only when the page asks, forwards the engine's events, takes the far end of the page's worklet port and feeds the engine. **Crash recovery** (research RN1, point 10): an engine that stops unasked is started again with the last device and sound settings, at most 3 times a minute, then `gave-up` tells the page to play through the web engine again. Added to the files list in `desktop/package.json`.
- **`preload.js`**: `audiolabDesktop.nativeEngine` on the Mac (`available`, `start`, `stop`, `cmd`, `sound`, `silence`, `on`) and the hand-over of the worklet port (`{ alNativePort: true }` posted to the window).
- **The page's side as one function** (`native/bridge/page-tap.js`, `alNativeTap(ctx, master)`): the worklet that copies each 128-frame block of the master and posts it from the audio thread; N2c copies it into `index.html` unchanged.
- **The test with the real pieces** (`tools/native-lab/electron-bridge/`: the real `desktop/native-engine.js`, the real `desktop/preload.js`, `page-tap.js`; cases A one clock exact noise bit for bit, B two clocks follow 997 Hz, C two clocks exact as the contrast, D the engine killed while playing), `tools/native-lab/sine_check.py` (clicks and gaps in a recorded sine, the speed it settled on), workflow `.github/workflows/native-engine.yml` (new; started by hand, runner label as an input).

### Proven (Linux, `alengine selftest`, all pass)
- At speed 1 the follower is bit for bit.
- Against the ideal (100 ppm fast): error -111.7 dB at 997 Hz, -116.8 dB at 15 kHz.
- 5 simulated minutes, sender in 128-frame blocks, device in 256: off by +250 ppm, steered to 253.9 ppm (mean of the last minute); -250 to -255.1; +1000 to 1019.5; -1000 to -1020.6 (still settling at 5 minutes); in all four 0 times empty, 0 drops, fill within 20 ms of the 50 ms target after two minutes.
- The JavaScript files pass Node's syntax check; `native-engine.js` loads in plain Node.

### Not proven
- **Nothing ran on a Mac this run.** From about 12:36 UTC no macOS run in the repository got a machine: two runs of the new workflow on `macos-15` waited 15 minutes and were cancelled, one on `macos-14` was cancelled at once (no reason shown), the same happened to other tasks' runs (native-lab, ui-bench), one dispatch got a 502 from GitHub, and a fourth run (46005232344, 13:13 UTC) was again cancelled after exactly 15 minutes in the queue. Every queued macOS job is cancelled at 15 minutes; the cause is not visible from here (a GitHub capacity problem, or a limit on the account's macOS minutes). The Core Audio side of the change (the `clock` command and status fields) is therefore not compiled on macOS yet; the next run must dispatch `native-engine.yml` first and fix anything it shows before going on. Cases A to D are written and waiting.
- Real clocks: how far the page's device and the Gryphon drift on the M4. Nothing here ran on the user's Mac.

### Assumptions
- `exact` stays the default; the bridge (N2c) picks `follow` only when the page's clock device is not the engine's device (with exclusive use on the DAC it cannot be). Page and engine on the same device without exclusive use share one clock, so `exact` is bit-perfect there.
- The follower is a bridge measure until N3: once the native engine makes the sound itself there is nothing to follow.
- Recovery restarts up to 3 times a minute; after that the page goes back to the web engine.
- The research RN1 suggestions taken in this stage: no locks on the audio path (the ring is lock-free), crash recovery. Left for later stages: meters through shared memory (N2c), App Nap guard (N2c), workgroups and block-size rule (N3).

### Next
- Dispatch `native-engine.yml` and read cases A to D (fix the Mac build first if it fails).
- N2c, when the design chain allows `index.html` work: the hook (copy `alNativeTap`, the "Native output" settings: device, rate, buffer, exclusive use, device volume both ways, switch back to the web engine), and shipping `alengine` in the desktop build (`desktop.yml` builds `alvol` the same way; that workflow may only be changed with the user's leave or through `afterPack`).

## 27 November 2026: task NB-N3b (the mixer from Chromium's arithmetic, bit for bit)

No app changes: `index.html` and `desktop/` untouched, no version. Running list: `docs/native-mac-build.md`.

**Two runs of task NB ran at the same time.** This run started from the scheduler's fire at about 13:20 UTC with the N2b state on main; another run (the one logged as NB-N3a above) started in parallel and pushed the engine core's first part at 13:36. Both chose stage 3 because N2c needs `index.html`. This run built the mixer, which N3a had named as its next part, so it is logged as N3b. The rebase met one conflict (`native/CMakeLists.txt`, both had a target called `alrender`); resolved by keeping N3a's `alrender` and calling this run's renderer `almix`, in `native/engine/mix/` beside N3a's `native/engine/core/`. The scheduling chat may want to make sure only one NB run is fired at a time.

### Built
- `native/dsp/al_mix.h`: Chromium's GainNode with a fixed value and its StereoPannerNode (both paths), the summing input.
- `native/engine/mix/mix_graph.h`, `almix.cpp`: tracks (input, devices, volume, pan) into the master, whole render quanta of a chosen size (128 live, 512 as the export), the track order as a setting (project order by default). A scene is one flat JSON object per line.
- `tools/native-lab/make_mix_ref.py` (each scene built in the real app page as `renderMix` builds it, rendered twice to see whether the web engine repeats itself), `run_mix.py` (every 32-bit sample; when project order does not match, it searches the order the web render used), `ref/mix/` (inputs, web renders and scenes, 1.4 MB). `native-engine.yml` builds `almix` and runs the check on the Mac.

### Proven (Linux, headless Chromium with the app v0.229/v0.230)
- 10 of 10 scenes identical bit for bit, repeated over four fresh sets of web renders.
- Three of the rules were found by a failing comparison and each fixed it: the two panner paths (94 samples per track in the first block), `pan + 1` in float (2,755 samples in the Bitcrusher scene), whole quanta with random numbers drawn past the end (127 samples in the last block). Silence at gain 0 was written from how Chromium's GainNode behaves and was not tested without it; the scene with a track at volume 0 passes.
- The web engine repeats itself on 8 of the 10 scenes. On five tracks into one bus and on two dithering Bitcrushers it does not (10,465 and 17,912 samples differ between two renders of the same scene); in 24 renders of the second there were two outcomes, one per order of the two tracks, and the native mixer reproduces both.
- Speed on this machine: 350 to 16,000 times real time depending on the scene (one shared core).

### Not proven
- Apple Silicon: the `native-engine.yml` run dispatched at 13:39 UTC was still queued when this entry was written (earlier ones were cancelled after 15 minutes without a machine).
- Sends, groups, returns, master devices and limiter, moving values, rates other than 48 kHz.

### Assumptions
- Project order is the native engine's order. Where the web engine's export is not stable (three or more tracks into one bus, or random-drawing devices on several tracks), "the sound must not change" is judged against one of the web engine's own renders, and the difference between web renders (about -140 dB) is the yardstick. Written here so the user can disagree.
- The N3a core runs its chains at 128 frames; the export runs at 512 (`renderSizeHint`, RQOK in `index.html`). The worklet bundle's skip-on-silence and every-16-blocks flush count blocks, so an export at 512 and a native render at 128 can differ. N3c should make the quantum a setting of the core.

### Next
- N3c: the mixer's tracks run N3a's `Chain`, quantum as a setting; sends, groups and returns; then the master chain.
- Read the Mac results of `native-engine.yml` (N2b cases A to D, N3b mixer) and of `native-core.yml` (N3a) when a machine is given.

## 27 November 2026, v0.232: task NI-1a, "Why is this clipping?" part 1: the engine (lane D, idea I3)

No visible change yet: this step is the measuring engine; the card with the fixes is NI-1b. Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ni/ni_1a.py` (anchored, re-run after the rebase onto v0.231), test `tools/ui-tests/taskNI_1a.py` (36 checks, all pass).

### Built
- **Clip event log** (`NI_clipSeen`, `NI_clipLog`, `NI_clipClear`, `NI.clips`): one call from `meters()` (master, readings above -6 dB) and one from `trackMeters()` (each strip, readings over 0 dB), only while the song plays; repeats within 1.5 s and 2 beats merge into one event (song position of the highest reading, level, the open project). Capped at 200 events. It only reads the numbers the meters already have: nothing is added to the audio path. `NI_HOOKS.clipEvent(e)` is called for each new event (for the card in NI-1b and for other lanes).
- **The master meter reads after the safety limiter.** Found while testing: the live safety limiter is a soft curve up to its ceiling (-1 dB) whose table spans twice the input range, so it also gives back the 6 dB of master headroom (`masterGain()` has `UI.headroom` -6 dB). With the limiter on (the default) the master meter never reaches 0 dB and the clip light never lights. The log therefore reads the level going into the limiter back through the inverse of its curve; that is the same level an offline render of the mix has. Where the curve is flat (the limiter at its ceiling) only a lower bound is known: such events are marked `sat` ("the limiter is squashing peaks here", at least -3.1 dB going in at the default ceiling) and the offline explanation measures them exactly. With the limiter off the reading is used as it is (`lim:false`).
- **`NI_clipExplain(t, o)`** (also `NI.clipExplain`): for a song position, a logged event, or nothing (the last event). Renders 0.25 s each side of the moment offline (`renderMixChunked`, the mix, then each audible track alone, two at a time), finds the master's peak sample, and returns: bar and beat, the channel, the peak and the overshoot in dB, the **inter-sample peak** (4x oversampling, windowed sinc with 16 zero crossings, kept 16 samples away from the ends of the render), each track's **signed contribution** at that sample and its share of it (cancelling tracks are negative), the rest (what sends, groups and master effects add; zero when there are none), and the chain in words (`NI_clipWords`): "Kick + Bass add up here: +1.6 dB over 0 dBFS at bar 9, beat 1. Biggest share: Kick (67%), Bass (42%). Pulling the other way: Anti (-8%). Inter-sample peak: +2.3 dB." For a strip event it also gives the track's own peak (master gain taken out; marked approximate when the master has effects) and the clips playing there. Cached per moment and project content (the work timer left out of the key), 40 entries; a result measured while the song changed is thrown away ("Try again"); refuses while an export runs. About 0.5 s for three tracks.

### Checked
- Test project from known signals (stereo audio clips, Kick + Bass + a phase-inverted copy of the bass, 120 BPM, master at +6 dB so the master gain is 1 with the default headroom): played live with the safety limiter off, one master event at beat 32 (bar 9) with a level over 0 dB; with the limiter on, one event there marked `sat` with a lower bound under the real +1.6 dB; no strip events. The explanation finds bar 9, beat 1, names Kick and Bass first, the peak sample equals the signals' sum within 0.1%, each share within 2% of the direct calculation (here exact to 4 decimals), the inverted track negative, nothing left over, the overshoot right, the words right; a second call comes from the cache (0.1 ms); after an edit (Bass at half) it is measured again.
- Same project with a quiet kick: nothing logged while playing (limiter on), the explanation says "No clip here", no last event.
- Inter-sample peak: a sine at a quarter of the sample rate, 45 degrees, amplitude 1.2: sample peak -1.41 dB, inter-sample peak +1.60 dB (true +1.58 dB).
- **Fractals levels unchanged** (measured with `tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`, same hashes as before): Kick -19.05560 dB, Bass -35.48685 dB (beats 64 to 96, master -10 dB as it opens); -9.75669 and -25.48699 dB with the master at 0 dB. The other lines of that script (Plant, Sampler, Drum kit) differ between two runs of the same old file too (the test project gets a new random seed each build), so they say nothing about this change.
- UI tests: `mixstrip.py` and `taskAB2.py` (207 of 207) pass; after the rebase `taskNI_1a.py` and `taskST_S2.py` again. No console errors. Nothing visible changed, so no screenshots this step.

### Limits
- The live log samples the meter once a frame: an over shorter than about a frame can be missed, and the level read live is lower than the real peak (in the test +0.6 dB read for a +1.6 dB over). The log only says where to look; the explanation measures offline and is exact.
- Live MIDI playing while the song is stopped is not logged (there is no song position to explain).
- The live safety limiter's curve giving back the 6 dB headroom also means that turning the limiter off makes the live output 6 dB quieter (export unchanged). This was already so before this step; noted here, not changed.

### Left
NI-1b: the card (click a clip light or the peak read-out, or the command `ni.clipExplain`), the bar chart of shares, and the three fixes (lower the top contributor by the overshoot plus 0.5 dB, master limiter on, play the moment). Then NI-2a.

## 27 November 2026, v0.233: the controller layer (task FT-C1a, lane C)
Step FT-C1a of `docs/features-build.md` (the user's pick: MIDI controller support, Push 1 first; F38 extended). This step is the layer every controller step builds on; Push 1's own profile is FT-C2a.

### Built
- **One MIDI service** (`CTL`, block "v0.233 (task FT-C1a)" right after the commands map `SCM`): Web MIDI asked **with SysEx**, and again without it when the browser refuses (plain MIDI then works, SysEx is never sent). Devices are found at the start and followed when plugged in or out (toast "Controller connected" / "unplugged"); each input is paired with its output by name (also the Windows names "MIDIIN2 (x)" and "MIDIOUT2 (x)"). In the desktop app MIDI starts with AudioLab (the shell already allows `midi` and `midiSysex`); in a browser it starts on the first MIDI learn, arm or Controllers window, and at later starts by itself once it was allowed.
- **Profiles**: each device's messages go to its profile (`ctlProf({id,name,match,attach,detach,msg,bye})`, FT-C2 adds Push 1). Every device today is **Generic MIDI**, which behaves as before: notes play the armed or selected track (same keys `m<note>`, sustain pedal as before), controller moves and pitch bend go to the recorded controller lanes, and to the mappings.
- **Mappings** `{id, dev, type cc/note/pb, ch, num, target, min, max, take, enc, fb, scope}`: for every project in `UI.ctl` (v1), for one project in `S.ctl` (v1, written only when a project mapping is made; undo covers it). The old `UI.midiMap` ("channel:cc" to a control) is read once into global mappings for any device with takeover Jump, as it behaved; it is left in place so an older build still finds its links. For the same message a project mapping wins over a global one.
- **MIDI learn** (Mod+L, the menu entry, the Controllers window): click a control, then move a knob, fader or button; Shift-click keeps the link in this project only, Alt-click removes it. Learns CC, notes and pitch bend (notes and pitch bend only after a control was clicked, so playing still plays). A learned note switches its control between its two ends and no longer plays. The toast names message, device and control ("Linked CC 21 (channel 1) on Fake Keys to Compressor: Ratio."). **Pinned device windows**: learn works there and the mapping names the device's own control, so it keeps working when the device is unpinned or pinned again; both copies are redrawn.
- **Takeover** for absolute knobs: Pick up (the default for new mappings: nothing moves until the knob passes the control; moving the control with the mouse or another mapping makes the knob catch it again), Scale (the control moves toward the knob's end as the knob moves and they meet there), Jump (as before). **Range** min and max per mapping, a reversed range turns a knob around.
- **Endless knobs** (relative encoders): two's complement (1 to 63 up, 65 to 127 down), sign bit (65 and up down) and offset 64; the first moves after learning tell which kind it is (Push 1's encoders are two's complement), and each step moves the control from where it is.
- **Feedback**: when a mapped control changes (mouse, another mapping), its value goes back to the controller (CC, note on or off, 14-bit pitch bend), only on change, at most 30 messages a second, never an echo of the controller's own move. Nothing runs while no MIDI arrives and nothing changes (no timer, no frame work).
- **Controllers window** (menu "Controllers…", command `ctl.mappings`): the connected devices with their profile and a switch each, and every mapping (device, message, what it moves, takeover, project or everywhere, delete). FT-C1b grows it into the full mappings page.
- **Commands**: `ctl.learn` (Mod+L; the old id `learn` is an alias), `ctl.mappings`. The learn banner lost its em dash.
- **Hooks for lane B** (Settings): `FT_HOOKS.controllersPage(host)` draws the same page into a Settings page body; `FT_HOOKS.controllersPaint`, `FT_HOOKS.controllersChanged`, `FT_HOOKS.controllerMessage`. Settings rows in the S4 shape are in `docs/features-build.md` section 6 (`ctl.take`, `ctl.scope`, `ctl.off`).
- Code: edit script `tools/feature-lab/ft/ftC1a.py` with `ftC1a_block.js` (every anchor asserted unique): `initMidi`, `mlMark`, `midiCC`, the learn click, the learn toast and banner, the menu entry, two `SCA` entries, and the block.

### Tested (`tools/ui-tests/taskFT_C1a.py`, headless Chromium, a fake MIDI system injected before the page loads, 55 checks, all pass)
- Nothing asks for MIDI at the start of a browser that never allowed it. SysEx asked; device found, generic profile, output paired; a second device plugged in later (Windows names) and unplugged, with toasts.
- As before: note 60 plays the selected track and stops; CC 64 holds and lets go (sustain); pitch bend reaches the lanes; the migrated old link moves its knob.
- Learn by clicking a knob and moving CC 21; marked; Pick up (knob below does nothing, then follows after passing; caught again after a mouse move); Scale (moves up more slowly, meets at the top, then follows); Jump with a range and reversed; endless knobs recognised as two's complement and sign bit; learned note switches and does not play, other notes still play; Shift-click into the project (S.ctl v1), project wins, saved with the project, undo takes it back; device switched off ignored; learn in a pinned window and the pinned knob redrawn.

- The Controllers window lists the device and every mapping, tooltips on every control, no em dash, delete and takeover from the list, the command opens it. Screenshots looked at (learn mode, the window in the normal and the Light level, a pinned window).
- SysEx refused: asked again without it, the device works, SysEx is not sent. No console errors in either run.
- **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`, beats 64 to 96): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; -9.75669 and -25.48699 dB at 0 dB; Saw, Pad, Acid, Wavetable and Venom the same checksums as v0.229 (Plant, Sampler, Sampler grains and Drum kit differ between runs of the same file, as logged in v0.229). ## 27 November 2026, v0.234: task NI-1b, "Why is this clipping?" part 2: the card (lane D, idea I3)

Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ni/ni_1b.py` (anchored; needs NI-1a; re-run after the rebase onto v0.233), test `tools/ui-tests/taskNI_1b.py` (36 checks, all pass; `taskNI_1a.py` 36 of 36 again).

### Built
- **Where it opens.** In the compact transport the master peak read-out is hidden, so a small **Clip** button (orange dot) appears next to the mixer button while the song has clip events, and hides again when they are cleared. The card also opens from the master peak read-out (which gets an orange dot), the mixer's master clip dot, the master pop's clip dot (when the song has master events), a strip's peak read-out in the mixer (when that strip has events), and the command **`ni.clipExplain`** "Why is this clipping? (explain the last clip)" in the commands list. Without events the old clicks work as before (reset).
- **The card** (`#niClip`, a `.pop`, so the glass engine draws it; dark and the Light level): a list of the song's clip events (newest first, positions to the nearest half beat), "Measuring this moment offline…" while `NI_clipExplain` runs, the chain in words, three read-outs with units (Where bar.beat, Peak dBFS, Inter-sample dBTP, red when over), a signed bar per track (its colour, zero line and quarter lines, sends, groups and master effects as a grey bar when they add 2% or more), notes (heard through the safety limiter; master effects; samples under 0 dBFS but inter-sample peak over). A strip event also gives the strip's own level and the clips playing.
- **Fixes**, each one undo step, and the card measures again afterwards: **Lower <top track> by X dB** (so the peak sample lands at -0.5 dBFS, at least the overshoot plus 0.5 dB as the research proposed; the research's rule alone was not enough when the top track has 67% of the peak, so the needed amount is computed from its share); for a strip event, that strip by its own overshoot plus 0.5 dB. **Limiter on the master** (AudioLab's Limiter at the end of the master chain, Safety net settings: no gain, ceiling -1 dB, true peak; or turns an existing one on). **Play the moment** (loops the bar before and the bar of the peak and plays). **Clear** (forgets the song's events, resets the clip lights).
- Escape or a click outside closes it. Nothing is drawn per frame; no audio nodes.

### Checked
- Test project from known signals (Kick + Bass + inverted copy, clipping at bar 9), played live with the limiter off and on: the Clip button and the dot appear; the card names bar 9 (9.1), "Kick + Bass add up here: +1.6 dB over 0 dBFS", +1.6 dBFS and +2.3 dBTP, bars Kick 67%, Bass 42%, Anti -8%; Lower Kick by 3.4 dB is one undo step, changes only Kick's volume and the re-render says "No clip here: the peak is -0.5 dB"; Undo puts it back; the master limiter is one undo step and the re-render peaks at -1.0 dBFS; Undo removes it; Play the moment loops beats 28 to 36 and plays; the command and the mixer's master dot open it; a strip event shows the strip's level; Escape closes; every control has a tooltip; no em dashes; no redraws while open; Clear works and the old reset click is unchanged. Screenshots of the card (normal and Light level) and the Clip button looked at.
- Fractals levels unchanged (measured): Kick -19.05560 dB, Bass -35.48685 dB (master -10 dB), -9.75669 and -25.48699 dB at 0 dB, same hashes. Lane C's `taskFT_C1a.py` passes on this file. No console errors.

### For the user to try
Play a loud part of a song with the safety limiter on: if the limiter hits its ceiling, the orange **Clip** button appears next to the mixer button. Click it and check that the tracks it names are the ones you would have guessed, and whether "Lower ... by X dB" sounds right. After lowering the top track the inter-sample peak can still be a little over 0 dB; the master limiter (true peak) catches that.

Task I3 done. Next: NI-2a, the kick and bass analysis (shared with lane C's FT-F18).

A second NB run did N3b (the mixer) at the same time; this part is N3c, and the mixer's sends, groups and returns become N3d.

### Built
- `native/engine/core/dev_modulation.h`: Chorus (`al-chorus`), Stereo imager (`al-imager`), Frequency shifter (`al-fshift`), Vocoder (`al-voc`), Tape stop (`al-tstop`), ported statement by statement. Devices native: 10 of 42; instruments 0 of 32.
- `native/third_party/llvm-libc/` (143 header files, Apache 2.0 with LLVM exception, commit 19b71e03): the browser's `sin`, `cos`, `exp`, `log10`. `js::pow` follows V8 (its own `x**2`, `x**0.5`, otherwise the system's `pow`). All devices call `js::` maths only.
- `WorkletShell` keeps the worklet bundle's rules on the web engine's quantum grid in sample time at any call size (silence per quantum with catch-up, the tiny-value guard every 16 quanta, `currentTime` of the quantum); `RenderContext::quantum` (128 playing, 512 export); `Processor::init` (settings made with) apart from `set` (settings by message, counts `pv`).
- Float rules: `-ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math` for the whole native tree; every chain sets round-to-nearest with tiny numbers kept and restores the caller's state.
- `alrender cases ... [block]`; targets `alrender_sysmath` (control), `almathprobe`; `tools/native-lab/math_probe.py`, `wl_node.js` (the app's worklet bundle run in Node); `make_ref_core.py` with ten device types, 4 chains and any quantum; `native-core.yml` with the maths probe, call sizes 32 and 64, and the controls.

### Proven (Linux; headless Chromium 158; app v0.230)
- **240 of 240 cases bit for bit** at quantum 128 (every preset of the ten devices, extra settings for every mode, four chains). With the system's maths library instead: 231.
- The same on GitHub's Linux machine, run 46014683118 (Chromium 159): 240 of 240; maths probe 0; 239 of 240 at 32 and 64 frames; system maths 231.
- The browser's maths: over 400,000 arguments, the engine's functions 0 differences for sin, cos, exp, log10, pow; glibc differs for sin 596, cos 579, exp 262, log10 84,586; pow 0 (it is glibc's own in the browser on Linux).
- Call sizes 1, 7, 32, 64, 100, 512, 4096 on the 128 grid: 239 of 240 each; the exception is two random-drawing devices in one chain (one shared stream in the web engine, review A2).
- Quantum 512 (the export's): 156 of 240 web renders differ from 128; native at 512 in 512s 240 of 240; in pieces of 128 or 32, 209 of 240, all differences (but the random chain) in the frames between a quantum's start and the return of sound after more than 3 s of silence, at most 1.5e-12.
- Wrong guess ruled out on the way: the browser does not flush tiny numbers to zero (with flushing every device differed).

### Not proven
- **Apple Silicon.** No macOS machine again: the `native-core.yml` runs (macos-15 and macos-14) and the N2b run stayed queued. On the Mac the browser's `pow` is Apple's; the probe step will show it when a machine comes.
- Electron's own V8 (the app ships Electron 45, Chromium 156) against Chromium 158's: the review's D3; the engine side is ready.

### Assumptions
- The parallel run's mixer (N3b) and this core stay separate directories until N3d joins them; neither run edited the other's files.
- The scheduling chat's note to use the repository's new name was followed for reading; pushing works only through the old name (`Audio-lab-DAW/audio-lab-beta`, which redirects), because this session is authorised for that name only.
- Research and review folded as written in the running list; the decisions D2, D3, D6, D7, D9 stay with the user.

### Next
- N3d (sends, groups, returns, the master's chain; joining the mixer and the core), or the FFT family (pitch shifter, pitch corrector, resonance suppressor: `atan2`, `hypot`, the FFT), whichever run comes first; N2c when the design chain allows `index.html` work.
