## 27 November 2026, v0.237: task NI-2a, kick and bass tuning lab part 1: the analysis (lane D, idea I2)

No visible change yet: this step is the analysis; the ruler view with the two fixes is NI-2b. Shared with lane C: FT-F18 builds on `NI_HOOKS.kickBass` and adds only what I2 does not have (low-band correlation, phase rotation, shorten tail). Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ni/ni_2a.py` (anchored, re-run after the rebases onto v0.235 and lane B's v0.236), test `tools/ui-tests/taskNI_2a.py` (56 checks, all pass).

### Built
- **`NI_kickBass(o)`** (also `NI.kickBass`, `NI_HOOKS.kickBass`): o = {t (song beat, default the playhead), kick, bass (track ids, default found), sr}. Finds the kick (Kick designer, a drum machine playing a kick pad, or a track named Kick or BD) and the bass (named Bass, Sub or 808, a Bass preset, notes mostly under E3; never a drum track). Takes the bar under the playhead (or the first bar the kick plays, if it is silent there).
- **The kick, from its settings** (exact): Kick designer instruments (with key tracking) and drum machine pads (Kick designer pad, kit kick, with the pad's Tune and Decay), using the same pitch formula as `kickRender`: the falling curve every 2 ms with its level, start and end frequency, the end note, the life in ms. `NI.kickModel(track, note)` gives this without any render.
- **The kick, measured** (audio kick, sampler, anything else): that one track rendered offline for the bar (`renderMixChunked` with `only`), low-passed and taken down to about 12 kHz, hits found from the level, YIN every 5 ms on the hit that rings longest; the end note is the median of the tail, given as a range (10th to 90th percentile), at least 40 cents each side under 40 Hz and marked `low` there, as the research asked.
- **Bass notes of the bar** (MIDI clips): note, frequency, in key or not, and against the kick's end: the interval folded to the nearest octave, the **beat rate** (between the kick's octave harmonic and the bass, or the reverse when the bass is lower), and the state: tuned (under 30 cents), clash (0.3 to 2.5 semitones, the beating range), apart.
- **Overlap** for the rolling-bass strip: each kick hit of the bar with the bass notes sounding during the kick's life and the gap in ms to the next bass note.
- **The key** (`NI_key`): lane C's project key when `FT_HOOKS.projectKey()` exists (FT-F11), else the piano roll's scale and root (`S.prKey`). **"Tune the kick to the root"**: the root note nearest to where the kick settles and the semitones to get there (NI-2b's fix).
- The result in words ("The kick settles on F♯1 (46.2 Hz, Kick designer settings). Key: F♯ minor. Bar 3 bass: F♯1 in tune with the kick; G1 beating at 2.8 Hz; ..."). Cached per kick track, bass track, bar, key and tempo map; thrown away if the song changes during a render; refused during an export.

### Checked
- Synthetic audio kicks (sweep from 260 Hz, drive, 380 ms) ending at 49.0, 41.2, 56.3, 36.7 and 32.7 Hz: found within 1.8, 4.6, 3.2, 6.9 and 7.6 cents; the range holds the true note every time; the two under 40 Hz flagged; the four hits of the bar found on the beats.
- Kick designer at tune 30, 26 and 34.5: read exactly from its settings, and its own render measured with the audio path agrees within 7.8, 13.8 and 10.1 cents (the drive and the short tail pull the measurement slightly sharp). Key tracking: note 48 reads 12 semitones up. Drum machine: the kit kick with pad tune -2 and a Kick designer pad with tune +1 read right.
- A song with Kick (F♯1), a Lead and a Bass: the Bass (not the Lead) found; bar 3's six bass notes and none from bar 4; every interval, beat rate and state equal to a direct calculation (G1 beating at 2.75 Hz, G2 at 5.51 Hz against the kick's octave, F♯1 and F♯2 in tune, C♯2 and B1 apart); key F♯ minor from the piano roll, G out of key; tune to root 0 semitones, and A1 +3 in A minor; gaps 125 ms; the kick's 320 ms life overlaps the notes at 8.25 and 8.5 only. The analysis leaves the project unchanged (saved JSON equal), the second call comes from the cache, an edit gives a new result; a stubbed lane C project key is used.
- **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`, measured): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; -9.75669 and -25.48699 dB at 0 dB; Saw, Pad, Acid, Wavetable and Venom the same checksums. No audio code was touched: the block makes no audio nodes.
- After the rebase onto lane C's v0.235 (and again on lane B's v0.236; lane B's `taskST_S3.py` 60 of 62, the two misses its own check that the version is 0.236): `taskNI_2a.py` 56 of 56, `taskNI_1a.py` and `taskNI_1b.py` 36 of 36 each, lane C's `taskFT_C1b.py` 29 of 29 (once, run beside another test, one feedback-timing check missed; alone it passes). No console errors. Nothing visible changed, so no screenshots this step.

### Limits
- An audio bass (a bass recorded or bounced to audio) is not read yet: its notes would need pitch tracking per note; the result says so. Notes are read as written; a transposing device after the instrument is not followed.
- Measured kicks: a kick with a lot of drive or a very short tail reads up to about 15 cents sharp; under 40 Hz it is shown as a range. Psytrance kicks that never settle on one note show a wide range; that is honest, not a fault.
- What only the ears can judge: whether "in tune" by this reading also sounds right on the user's kicks; to try in NI-2b.

### Left
NI-2b: the view (note ruler C0 to C3 with the key lit, the kick's falling curve with its end note, bass notes as bars, the clash glow with the beat rate, the rolling-bass gap strip), the fixes "tune kick to root" and "bass down an octave" (one undo step each), the command `ni.kickBass`, `NI_HOOKS.kickBassView` for FT-F18's rows. Then NI-3.


## 27 November 2026, v0.238: Ableton Push 1, part 1: connect, display, pads (task FT-C2a, lane C)
Step FT-C2a of `docs/features-build.md` (the user's pick: MIDI controller support, their Push 1 first). Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ft/ftC2a.py` with `ftC2a_block.js` (one asserted anchor, after FT-C1b's block), test `tools/ui-tests/taskFT_C2a.py` (46 checks, a fake Push 1).

### Built
- **A Push 1 profile** (`push1`, "Ableton Push 1") for the Push's Live port: names with "Ableton Push", not "User", not "MIDIIN2 (...)" (the Windows name of the User port), not Push 2 or 3. The User port stays Generic MIDI, so User mode is left to the user.
- **Hello** (when it is plugged in, AudioLab starts or the device is switched on again): Live mode `F0 47 7F 15 62 00 01 00 F7`, pressure mode `F0 47 7F 15 5C 00 01 <0 per pad, 1 whole grid> F7`, touch strip mode `F0 47 7F 15 63 00 01 <6 pitch bend, 10 mod wheel> F7`, then the display, the pads and the buttons it uses. **Goodbye** (page hidden or AudioLab quits, device switched off on the Controllers page, unplugged): the 4 lines cleared (`F0 47 7F 15 1C..1F 00 00 F7`), every pad and lit button dark, held notes stopped.
- **The display**: 4 lines of 68 characters, `F0 47 7F 15 <18..1B> 00 45 00 <68 ASCII> F7`; only lines that changed are sent. Note mode shows AudioLab and the track's name, the key, layout, octave and velocity curve, and a hint; the Scales page shows the 8 settings over the 8 encoders.
- **Pads as a note grid** in the project key (`PR.root`, `PR.scale`, the same key as the piano roll; "none" plays chromatic): In key (every pad a note of the scale) or Chromatic (every note; notes outside the key dark), rows in fourths (3 scale steps or 5 semitones), thirds (2 or 4) or in a row (8), **octave up and down** (CC 54, 55; lit while there is room). Pads play the armed instrument tracks, or the selected instrument track when none is armed (as Live does with Push), recorded like a keyboard.
- **Pad colours** (note on to the pad, velocity = Push palette index): root pads in the nearest palette colour to the track's colour (the 14 full colours 5, 9 ... 57; white 3 for grey colours), other notes of the key white (3), outside the key off (0), held pads green (21), also every other pad with the same note. Only changed pads are sent. They follow the selected track, its colour and the key (selectTrack, changed).
- **Velocity curves** Linear, Soft, Hard, Fixed (100). **Pressure** Off, Per pad, Whole grid: values go to `FT_HOOKS.pressure(note or null, 0..1)` for FT-F14 (AudioLab's instruments do not take pressure yet). **Touch strip** as pitch bend or the mod wheel lane (ccLive 'pb' or '1', as keyboards do). Encoder and strip touches (notes 0 to 12) never play.
- **Scales** (CC 58): the 8 encoders (CC 71 to 78, two's complement, 3 ticks a step) change root, scale, layout, rows, velocity, pressure, strip, octave. Outside Scales the encoders and buttons go to MIDI learn and mappings (an encoder is found as an endless knob), and are not recorded into controller lanes. FT-C2b puts them on the selected device.
- **Controllers page**: while a Push 1 is connected, an "Ableton Push 1" block with Layout, Rows, Velocity, Pressure, Touch strip and Octave (tooltips on each; kept in `UI.p1`, for every project) and the project key. Hooks: `FT_HOOKS.pressure`, `FT_HOOKS.push1Paint`; settings rows in the S4 shape in `docs/features-build.md` section 6.
- Nothing runs while the Push is still (event driven; a 60 ms repaint after a change only while a device is connected). Audio path untouched; no project fields added.

### Sources
- pushmod, "The Ableton Push" (reverse-engineered SysEx on Live 9.1.2: display write and clear, Live and User mode, key or channel pressure, touch strip modes, pad notes y*8+36+x, pad colour by note velocity, button LED values): https://pushmod.blogspot.com/
- Ableton, Using Push 1 (Live 12 manual): https://www.ableton.com/en/manual/using-push-1/ ; Push User Mode for custom MIDI mappings: https://help.ableton.com/hc/en-us/articles/209071249
- hardpush (Push 1 hardware notes): https://github.com/cbmainz/hardpush
- Button and encoder numbers (Octave 54 and 55, Scales 58, Note 50, encoders 71 to 78, encoder touches notes 0 to 10, strip touch note 12) come from the open-source Push 1 scripts (DrivenByMoss, Live's remote scripts), as listed in the plan; the pushmod note and CC table and its palette table could not be read in this run. The palette colours past 0 (off) and 3 (white) follow Live's pad palette and are **not yet confirmed on a real Push 1**.

### Tested (`tools/ui-tests/taskFT_C2a.py`, headless Chromium, fake Push 1, 46 checks, all pass)
- Profile matching (Live port, User port, "Live Port", MIDIIN2, Push 2); hello bytes; display lines 77 bytes each with 00 45 00; display text; all 64 pads coloured, root red for a red track, white in key, octave above red again; buttons lit; nothing sent to the User port or the Push 2.
- Pads in A minor, octave 2: pad 36 plays A (MIDI 45), 37 B, 44 D (fourths), on the selected unarmed track; linear velocity; held pads and same notes green; note off and note on 0 stop them; only changed pads sent. Encoder and strip touches do not play; the strip bends; Push buttons not recorded.
- Octave up: octave 3, only the changed display line sent, pad 36 plays A2. Scales: display shows the settings (68 characters); root up a semitone; chromatic (A# dark, B white); one row up 5 semitones; velocity curves Hard and Fixed (plays 100); strip mode 10 and pressure 1 sent; pressure reaches the hook; strip moves the mod wheel lane. An encoder learned as an endless knob outside Scales. Track colour blue: root pads 45.
- Controllers page block with tooltips, no em dash; a change there reaches the Push. Nothing runs while still. Switched off: lines cleared and 64 pads dark; on again: hello again; page hidden: goodbye. SysEx refused: pads play and are coloured, no SysEx sent. No console errors.
- Screenshots looked at: the Controllers page with the Push 1 block (normal and Light level).
- `taskFT_C1a.py` 55 of 55, `taskFT_C1b.py` 29 of 29. **Fractals levels unchanged**: Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; -9.75669 and -25.48699 dB at 0 dB.

### Only the user can test (the real Push 1)
- Plug in the Push 1 and open AudioLab (desktop app; in a browser press MIDI learn once and allow MIDI with SysEx). Expected: the display shows "AudioLab", the selected track, "Key A minor" (or your project key), "Octave 2"; the pads light with the track's colour on the root notes and white on the others.
- Select an instrument track and play the pads: notes in the key, a row up is a fourth. Press Octave up and down. Press Scales and turn the 8 encoders: root, scale, layout (try Chromatic), rows, velocity, pressure, touch strip, octave; press Scales again to go back.
- Please report: does the display show text (if it stays blank, the Live mode or display bytes differ); are the pad colours right (red track: red roots; held pads green); do the Octave, Scales and Note buttons light; does the touch strip bend notes (and act as mod wheel when set). Quitting AudioLab should clear the display and darken the pads.

### Left
- FT-C2b: encoders on the selected device's parameters with names and values on the display, banks, track select and arm/mute/solo rows, transport, tempo, swing, master, metronome, undo, drum-rack 4x4 mode. Pressure reaches no instrument yet (FT-F14). Next: FT-C2b.

## 27 November 2026: task NB-R1 (native CI on every push; review RN5's first fix task)

Why this part and not the next N stage: when this run started, another NB run had pushed two N3c commits a minute earlier and was still writing its docs (the two-runs-at-once problem logged under NB-N3b). N2c needs `index.html` and waits for the design chain. So this run took the review's first fix task, NB-R1, which touches different files (`native/tests/`, `.github/workflows/`, the bridge). `index.html` untouched; the app is unchanged.

### Built
- **`.github/workflows/native-ci.yml`**, on every push to main touching `native/**`, `desktop/native-engine.js`, `desktop/preload.js`, `tools/native-lab/**` (Linux only, so it starts at once), and by hand with a `mac` box for the Apple Silicon job. Jobs: `linux` (Release and ASan + UBSan builds of every target; selftest; ring stress; mixer 10 scenes; all 240 device cases against the web engine rendered fresh in headless Chromium, Release at 128 frames, sanitizers at 128 and 7), `tsan` (ring stress under ThreadSanitizer), `node` (syntax of every bridge file, bridge unit tests), `mac` (on demand).

Written on v0.234, rebased onto v0.235 to v0.240 by re-running the edit script on the fresh file.

### Built (block "lane E (task IN-A)" before `askChoice`, one object `INS`; nothing drawn by it yet)
- **Look values** `INS_LOOK0`: the user's DR3 details as named constants until task LK: G3 drafting grid (three line levels), W1 hairlines (0.5 CSS px, curves 1 px), L2 amber units `#ffb547`, A1 yellow selection `#f5c84c`, label greys and the mono font. `INS.look()` takes LK's values of the same names when LK's object exists. **For lane A (LK):** the name `LOOK` is already used by the Settings look sliders (`const LOOK=[...]`, an array); `INS._src()` ignores an array, so LK either renames that one or points `INS._src` at its own object (one line).
- **One number formatter** (for MD1 and X9 to reuse; MD1 was not out yet): `INS.fmt(v,unit)`, `INS.parts(v,unit)` (number and unit apart, for the amber unit label), `INS.num`, `INS.hz(f,{note:true})` (X8: "440 Hz  A4 +0 ct"), `INS.note(f)`, `INS.ucap(unit)` (capitals that keep the micro sign). A real minus sign, a thin space before the unit, one decimal for dB, dBFS, dBTP, LUFS and LU (LU signed), SI prefixes with three significant figures (12400 Hz gives 12.4 kHz, 0.0005 s gives 500 µs, 48000 Hz gives 48.0 kHz). X9's text says three figures while its examples show four (12.40 kHz); the formatter follows the rule and the pick page (12.4 kHz), and `{n:4}` gives four.
- **Colour maps** as 256-step lookup tables: magma, inferno, viridis (matplotlib's, within 2 levels at every step) and today's heat (the app's `heatCol0` stops); `INS.rgb(map,t)` and `INS.cbar(...)` (a colour bar made once per map, then copied).
- **Scale drawers** on whole device pixels: `INS.scaleTaper` (the fader taper, +6 to -60 dB: a mark per dB to -12, every 3 dB to -24, then every 6; numbers where they fit), `INS.fAxis` (log frequency: long marks and grid at decades, mid at 2 and 5, short elsewhere; labels only where they fit), `INS.dbGrid` (heavier every major step), `INS.graticule` (oscilloscope: 10 by 8 divisions, five minor marks on the centre axes, the fine drafting level left out at the Light level), `INS.corner` (settings in a corner). `INS.due(st,now)` gives the half-rate variant at the Light level.
- **Ballistics** from the standards: `INS.peak` (digital peak, instant rise, falls 20 dB in 1.7 s, hold 2 s then falls, maximum latched), `INS.vu` (IEC 60268-17, second order, aligned so a sine reads its peak level), `INS.ppm` (type IIb: a 10 ms burst reads 2 dB below the steady tone; the charge time constant, 2.75 ms on the rectified signal, is set by that rule; falls 24 dB in 2.8 s), `INS.rms` (sliding window, AES17 +3.01 dB), `INS.kms` (K-weighted mean square over 400 ms, ITU-R BS.1770, the filters keep their state between blocks).
- **One analyser read per analyser per frame**: `INS.fft`, `INS.fftB`, `INS.td`. Every frequency read in the app (13 places: the mixer spec and spectrogram views, the Spectrum device, the spectrum overlay and its modules, the Visualizer, the EQ device's analysers, `fqOf`) now goes through the cache (Chromium already reuses its FFT within one audio block, so nothing looks different; the point is that IN-S and later share one read). `INS.fresh` finds the samples that are new since a reader's last look (the last four samples found again on the 128-sample block grid), so per-sample ballistics neither miss nor count twice.
- **The meter's "Loudness" reading is now K-weighted.** It was plain mean square with -0.691 added. Now: the two BS.1770 filters (`kBiquads`, as the loudness map uses) over only the new samples, a 400 ms window, plus 3.01 dB so a sound in both channels reads the LUFS the loudness box shows. Peak, RMS and VU readings are untouched (same code as before). The hint in Settings says what it is.
- **The double `vizSide`:** the Visualizer's layout helper (the later one, which replaced the first) is now `vizDockSide`; the **Sidechain device shows its picture again** (it had been blank).

### Tested (`tools/ui-tests/taskIN_A.py`, known signals made in the page and played live)
- Formatter: units, prefixes, minus sign, thin space, notes and cents, unit capitals.
- Colour maps against matplotlib (within 2 levels at all 256 steps); lightness rises steadily in magma, inferno and viridis; heat matches the app's colours.
- Digital peak: -20.0 dB after 1.7 s; hold 2 s then falls; maximum latched. VU: -18.01 for a -18 dBFS sine, 99 % in 0.301 s, overshoot 1.30 %. PPM IIb: 10 ms burst -1.99 dB, falls 24 dB in 2.8 s, a steady -6 dBFS sine reads -6.00. RMS 300 ms: -18.00.
- K-weighting at 25 Hz, 100 Hz, 1, 4 and 10 kHz equal to the standard's own 48 kHz coefficients (0.000 dB difference); one channel of a -18 dBFS 1 kHz sine reads -21.00 LUFS as BS.1770 says; the same reading when fed in odd-sized pieces.
- New-sample finding exact when the frame clock and the audio clock disagree by a block either way (200 frames).
- Cache: three reads of one analyser in a frame call it once; no native frequency read left outside the block.
- Live, 1 kHz sine at -18 dBFS in both channels (at the context's rate): peak -17.98, **Loudness -17.97 LUFS on both bars, the loudness box -17.97**, steady to 0.002 dB; anti-phase pair -17.98 on each bar; a 10 kHz sine reads higher by the K-weighting shelf, as the box does; RMS unchanged.

## 27 November 2026, v0.242: Ableton Push 1, part 2: control (task FT-C2b, lane C)
Step FT-C2b of `docs/features-build.md` (the user's pick: MIDI controller support, their Push 1 first). Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ft/ftC2b.py` with `ftC2b_block.js` (one asserted anchor, after FT-C2a's block; re-run on the fresh file after rebases over ST-S4 and IN-A), test `tools/ui-tests/taskFT_C2b.py` (59 checks, the fake Push 1).

### Built
- **The 8 encoders outside Scales** (CC 71 to 78, two's complement; 1/127 of the range a step, Shift a tenth of that): **Device** (CC 110, the default) moves the selected device's parameters 8 at a time, in the order of the device panel (the instrument first; the track's own Gain, Volume, Pan, Width are the first "Track" device), names on line 1 and values on line 2 of the display; **< and >** (CC 62, 63) page through banks; **Left and Right arrows** (CC 44, 45) pick the device; **Up and Down** (CC 46, 47) the track. **Volume** (CC 114) and **Pan & Send** (CC 115): the encoders move the volume or pan of the 8 tracks over the upper row (< and > page by 8 tracks). One undo step per run of turns of one control (a pause of 1.5 s starts a new one).
- **Display**: line 3 the track, the device (number of devices), the bank, and the key and octave (on a drum kit, the chosen pad); line 4 the 8 tracks over the upper row, the selected one marked with ">". In Volume and Pan mode lines 1 and 2 show the 8 tracks and their values, line 3 the mode, the tracks shown and what the lower row does.
- **Two rows of buttons under the display**: the upper row (CC 20 to 27) selects a track (selected bright orange, others dim); the lower row (CC 102 to 109) arms it (red, dark red when not armed); **Mute** (CC 60) and **Solo** (CC 61) switch the lower row to mute (yellow) or solo (blue); pressing the lit one again goes back to arm. The bank follows the selected track.
- **Transport and editing**: Play (CC 85; Shift+Play: loop on or off; lit while playing), Record (86, lit while recording), Stop (29), Metronome (9, lit when on), Tap tempo (3, the average of up to 5 taps), the tempo encoder (CC 14, 1 BPM a step, one undo step a turn), the master encoder (CC 79, master level), Undo (119; Shift+Undo: redo), New (87: new instrument track, the instrument browser), Duplicate (88: the selected clip, else the selected track), Delete (118: the selected clip), Quantize (116: the selected clip to 1/16). They call the same `SCA` commands as the keyboard. The swing encoder (CC 15) is left to MIDI learn: AudioLab has no song swing.
- **Drum kit track selected** (Drum kit instrument): the lower left 4x4 pads are its 16 pads (36 bottom left, rows of 4), in the track colour, the chosen pad white, muted pads dim, held pads green; pressing a pad plays it on that track (recorded like a keyboard) and chooses it (the device panel shows its settings). The top two rows are **16 steps of the chosen pad** over the bar under the playhead (in the clip there, or a new 1-bar clip): a press adds or removes a 1/16 note (velocity 0.8), one undo step a press; empty steps dim, every 4th a little brighter, notes in the track colour. **Delete held + a pad** clears that pad in the bar. While the song plays on a drum kit the lane follows the bar (4 times a second, only while playing).
- **Learned mappings win**: a Push control learned in MIDI learn goes to its mapping, not to the device. Learning still works on every control; Scales, octave and Note keep the C2a behaviour; on an instrument track the pads are the note grid as before.
- The Controllers page has a short guide under the Push 1 settings (with a tooltip). No new settings, no project fields; audio path untouched.

## 27 November 2026: task NB-R2 (the rate contract, the source hand-shake, the engine on a null device)

Fired by the scheduler with a note from the scheduling chat (14:11 UTC): fold in the independent review (RN5) and fix its blockers before building further. Done here: the review mapped item by item to stages in `docs/native-mac-build.md`; blocker A1 fixed; blocker P1 fixed for Linux (NB-R1 and this run); C1, C2, C5 fixed; blocker A2 left for your decision D2 (it changes the web engine's sound). `index.html` untouched.

### Built
- **Rate contract** (`native/engine/engine_main.cpp`): socket sources need `pageRate`, refused unless it equals the device's rate; a device rate change while playing gives silence, a `rate` event with `soundPaused`, a `framesAtWrongRate` count, and resumes when the rate returns; `open` at another rate re-checks. `alengine 0.3`, `ready` says `rateContract: true`.
- **Source switching** (C1): socket thread stopped first, then `quiesce()` waits for the device thread to leave `render` (flags `source` and `inRender`, sequentially consistent); no sleep. Sinc table built at start (C2). `E.rate`, `E.dev` atomic; steering reset carried out by the reader (`Ring::requestSteerReset`, C5); `Ring::drain` (reader side) for the silent pause.
- **Null device** (`native/common/nulldevice.cpp`, `nulldevice.h`): the Core Audio layer's API on any machine, two pretend DACs (Gryphon-like and Zoom-like), a real-time device thread, a listener thread, `null` command to change a device from outside (rate, volume, unplug, plug, hog), `AL_NULL_RECORD` recording. `alengine` now runs on Linux, not only `selftest`.

## 27 November 2026, v0.244: Ableton Push 1, part 3: sections as scenes (task FT-C2c, lane C)
Step FT-C2c of `docs/features-build.md` (the user's pick: MIDI controller support, their Push 1 first). ### Built
- **Session** (CC 51, lit while on; Note, CC 50, goes back; Scales still works on top): the pads become a grid of **8 tracks across** (the same track bank as the button rows under the display) **by 8 sections down** (the song's sections in time order, the first at the top). A pad is lit in the track's colour when that track plays something in the section (a note starting inside it, an audio clip over it; a group track when any track in it does; muted clips do not count), **green** in the section playing now, **white** in the section queued, dark otherwise.
- **Launching**: the 8 scene buttons on the right (CC 36 to 43, top to bottom) and the pads (a pad also selects its track) launch a section. Stopped: AudioLab plays from the section's start. Playing: the jump waits for the **next bar** (the default), for the **end of the section** playing (like a scene in Live) or happens **at once**: the new setting **Launch** on the Controllers page (`UI.p1.sq`), and Shift+button is always at once. Pressing the queued section again cancels it; Stop clears the queue. The jump is the same stop and start at the new place as the section jump keys, so no new audio path.
- **Display**: line 1 the 8 tracks, line 2 their volumes (or pans after Pan & Send), line 3 the section playing, the one queued and "in N bars" (or the Launch setting), line 4 the 8 sections for the scene buttons. A song without sections says "No sections yet" and keeps the pads dark.
- **In Session**: the arrows scroll the grid (Up and Down by one section, Left and Right by one track; Shift by 8); the 8 encoders move the volume of the 8 tracks shown (Pan & Send: pan; one undo step a turn). Every other button works as in FT-C2b; a learned mapping on any Push control wins.
- **Light use**: a timer runs only while a section is queued (one, set to the bar line, checked again on arrival), and a check 4 times a second follows the section under the playhead only while the song plays in Session. Nothing runs while stopped.

Hook `FT_HOOKS.push1Launch(sectionId, now)` for a launcher on screen and for FT-C3c (Launchpad, APC); the settings row `p1.sq` for lane B's table is in the plan's section 6. No project fields; audio path untouched.

## 27 November 2026, v0.245: task NI-3, the analysis worker and the per-beat band cache (lane D, idea I1 part 1, NF3)

No visible change yet: this step is the measuring base for the frequency map (NI-4) and for the ideas that reuse it (I4 mono-loss map, I5 harmonic ruler, I6 energy arc, I7, I12 masking cables, I13, I31). Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ni/ni_3.py` (anchored, re-run on the fresh file after the rebase onto v0.243), test `tools/ui-tests/taskNI_3.py` (29 checks, all pass).

Note on this run: it first built NI-2b (the kick and bass view) in parallel with another lane D run, which released it first as v0.239; that copy was dropped unpushed, and the run claimed NI-3 in the plan (commit "step claimed") before starting it, as lane C does.

### Built
- **`NI_anWork`**, the analysis of one piece, in a Worker made from the function's own text (the `WARPQ` pattern; it runs on the page if a worker cannot start). Per beat: **61 bands of 1/6 octave** from 20 Hz to 20.5 kHz for **mid and for side** (one FFT gives both), **loudness** (BS.1770 K-weighting, LUFS of the beat), **spectral centroid**, **playing** (over -60 dBFS RMS), the **five strongest peaks** (Hz refined by a parabola, dB). FFT 8192 with a Hann window at 44.1 kHz, frames every 4096 samples inside the beat, averaged. Bands in dB where a full-scale sine reads -3 dB in its band (mean square, the window taken out), stored in 0.5 dB steps; bands under two bins wide use the spectrum's density at the band centre times the width.
- **`NI.an`**: each track (not groups or returns) in pieces of 24 beats, rendered offline on its own (`renderMixChunked` with `only`: the track's effects and the master chain are in it, with the render's usual pre-roll), one piece at a time. Each piece keyed by a hash of what its sound depends on: the track without name, colour, mute, solo or ids, the clips that reach the piece (from 24 beats before it, for tails), tempo map, master level and chain, headroom, the code version. Kept in memory and in IndexedDB (`audiolab-ni`, capped at 3,000 pieces, the oldest go first), so a reopened song is read back without a render. Pieces where the track has no clip are answered "silent" without a render.
- **Snappy and safe**: nothing runs until a view asks; never in the audio thread; waits while an export runs; while the song plays it works only when the CPU read-out stayed under 45% for the last 2 s, and then one piece every 600 ms at most; a project switch empties the queue and the waiting caller is told it was cancelled; a track edited while its piece rendered is queued again.
- **API**: `NI.an.get(track, beat)` (sync: the numbers, `{silent}` where nothing plays, or null and the piece is queued), `NI.an.ensure({tracks, b0, b1, prog})` (a Promise with done, total, renders, cancelled), `NI.an.status()` (queued, busy, why it waits, renders, read from IndexedDB, skipped, time per piece), `NI.an.cancel()`, `NI.an.bands`. Hook `NI_HOOKS.analysis` (= `NI.an`).

### Checked
- **The Fractals demo**, beats 64 to 160, all 27 tracks: 130 pieces, 78 skipped as silent, 52 rendered and analysed, about 0.6 to 0.7 s per piece on this 2-core test machine (so the whole song, about 600 pieces, would take some 7 minutes here, in the background). While the song played for 45 s the analysis held back by itself (the CPU read-out on this machine goes over 45%) and did 2 to 3 pieces; dropouts while playing: 0, the same as 45 s of playing without it. The song is not changed (saved JSON equal), the worker is a real Worker, the Kick at beat 80 shows a low peak and its loudness.
- **Known signals** (audio tracks, 120 BPM, 44.1 kHz; the render's gain of -6.00 dB, the default headroom, taken into account): a 110 Hz sine is the strongest peak within 0.3 Hz in both pieces and reads its level in its band within 0.6 dB, with no side; silence before it reads "not playing"; an anti-phase 2 kHz tone has no mid and its side band at its level; a 1 kHz tone at -20 dBFS in both channels reads -20.0 LUFS within 0.3 (scaled by the gain), centroid 1 kHz; white noise: every band from 60 Hz up equals a direct numpy calculation on the same render within 0.6 dB (beats 4, 7 and 30).
- **Cache**: a second pass renders nothing; with memory cleared (as after a reopen) all 8 pieces come from IndexedDB; a one-clip edit (the second clip of one track) re-analyses exactly one piece of that track; `get()` of a missing beat answers null, queues it and answers once done; while an export runs it waits and says why; a project switch cancels the pass.
- **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`, measured on v0.245): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; -9.75669 (0496bb147f6c) and -25.48699 dB (09e0415bec5e) at 0 dB; Saw, Pad, Acid, Wavetable and Venom the same checksums. One run of the whole test list, made straight after the heavy tests, read the Bass at 0 dB as -26.74 dB once; four runs after it (with and without this step) read the reference again, so it is counted with the known run-to-run noise of that test, not as a change. No audio code was touched: the block makes no audio nodes.
- After the rebases onto v0.243 and lane C's v0.244: `taskNI_3.py` 29 of 29, `taskNI_2b.py` 36 of 36, `taskNI_1b.py` 36 of 36 (and before it `taskNI_1a.py` 36, `taskNI_2a.py` 56), lane B's `taskST_S4.py` 33 of 33, lane C's `taskFT_C2a.py` 46 of 46 (one check missed once beside other tests, passes alone) and `taskFT_C2c.py` 36 of 36, lane A's `taskGS4.py` 42 of 42, lane E's `taskIN_A.py` 37 of 37. No console errors. Nothing visible changed, so no screenshots.

### Limits
- Per-track renders use `only`, so a track's **sends and sidechain ducking are not in its numbers** (a ducked bass reads as if not ducked; return tracks are not analysed). NI-5 (masking cables) should keep this in mind; a ducking-aware pass would render the sidechain source too.
- The key includes the master chain and level: changing the master re-analyses everything (in the background). Tails longer than 24 beats from a clip before the piece are not counted.
- On a weak machine nothing is analysed while the song plays; it catches up when stopped.
- What only the user can judge: nothing to hear or see yet; the frequency map in NI-4 is the first place to judge it.

### Left
NI-4: the frequency map view (time left to right, log frequency 20 Hz to 20 kHz, each pixel the owning track's colour, sections on top, a one-track layer switch, click to jump and select, command `ni.freqMap`), built on `NI.an`. Then NI-5a/b masking cables.


## 27 November 2026, v0.246: task NI-4, the frequency map of the whole song (lane D, idea I1 part 2, NF4)

Idea I1 is complete. Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ni/ni_4.py` (anchored; needs NI-3 and lane E's IN-A), test `tools/ui-tests/taskNI_4.py` (31 checks, all pass). The step was claimed in the plan before it started.

### Built
- **A window "Frequency map"** (command `ni.freqMap`, "Frequency map of the whole song"; the app's floating window: moves, resizes, remembers its place). Time left to right over the whole song, frequency bottom to top on a log scale from 20 Hz to 20 kHz (NI-3's 61 bands of 1/6 octave), every spot in the colour of the **track that owns the most energy there** (mid plus side), brightness by the total level (-84 to -18 dB), spots under -90 dB dark, pieces not measured yet hatched. Section names and colours along the top with lines down the map; bar numbers under it as often as they fit; frequency labels at 20, 50, 100 ... 20k with the decades brighter.
- **Colours**: Auto (by track, or by group when the song has more than 12 tracks, as the research asked), By track, By group. **Legend** of the owners, most spots first (spots over -60 dB counted), as groups when coloured by group.
- **Layer**: one track or one group glowing by its own level in its colour over the rest in grey (from the select or by clicking a legend chip; again for all).
- **Hover read-out**: bar and beat, the band's frequency with its note (lane E's `INS.hz`), the owner and the runner-up with their levels (`INS.fmt`), or "silent" / "not measured yet". **Click**: the playhead moves to that beat (while playing too) and the owner is selected (with a layer on, the layer's track, or the group's track that sounds there).
- **Snappy**: the owners are worked out once per change of the analysis from the stored bytes through a lookup table, into an image of beats by bands that is scaled into the window; drawn again only when the analysis grows (at most every 600 ms while it fills), on a resize, or when a setting changes; nothing per frame. While the song plays a thin playhead marker is moved by a 250 ms check (a CSS position, the map is not drawn again). The analysis starts when the window opens and stops when it closes; an edit is measured again after 1 s of quiet.
- NI-3's key now leaves out the track's group (`grp`): a render with `only` does not pass through the group, so putting a track in a group no longer re-measures it.
- `NI.map` (`open`, `close`, `draw`, `own(beat, band)`, `grid()`) for NI-5 and NI-11.

### Checked
- A test song (audio, 120 BPM, 8 bars, sections Intro and Drop): Kick 50 Hz in bars 1 and 2, Pad 500 Hz throughout, Hat 8 kHz from bar 5. The command opens the window and measures it ("3 tracks · 32 beats"); Kick owns beat 4 at 50 Hz, nothing at beat 20 there, Pad at 500 Hz, Hat at 8 kHz; the cells are red, blue and green as the tracks; a silent cell is dark. Hover at the kick spot reads "bar 2.1 · 50.4 Hz · G1 +49 ct · Kick −16.0 dB"; clicking it puts the playhead on beat 4 and selects Kick. Layer Pad: the kick spot grey, the pad blue. The legend lists the three owners in order of their spots; clicking the chosen chip again shows all. Kick put in a group "Drums": nothing measured again; by group the kick spot takes the group's yellow, the legend shows Drums, Hat, Pad; the Drums layer glows yellow with the pad grey, and a click there selects Kick. Bar numbers every bar at this width.
- Nothing drawn in 1.5 s with the window open and the song stopped; while playing the marker shows and moves with no redraw; stopped, it hides. An edit (Hat shortened to bar 7) is measured again in the background and beat 28 at 8 kHz turns silent. Every control has a tooltip, no em dashes, the window inside the app; closing it stops its check and the measuring. No console errors.
- **The Fractals demo** (first 96 bars measured, the rest hatched; screenshots normal and Light level, looked at): coloured by group (27 tracks): Kick & Bass own the low end under about 150 Hz through the drops, Music (blue) the 300 Hz to 2 kHz band, Drums the top, the vocal intro and the breaks visible as gaps.
- After the rebase onto the claims of lanes C and E (main still v0.245): `taskNI_4.py` 31 of 31, `taskNI_3.py` 29 of 29, `taskNI_2b.py` 36 of 36, `taskNI_1b.py` 36 of 36, lane E's `taskIN_A.py` 37 of 37.
- **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`, measured): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; -9.75669 (0496bb147f6c) and -25.48699 dB (09e0415bec5e) at 0 dB. No audio code was touched.

### Limits
- As NI-3: a track's numbers leave out its sends and sidechain ducking, so a ducked bass owns more of the low end on the map than you hear.
- The whole Fractals song takes several minutes to measure the first time (about 0.6 s per piece on the test machine, more while it plays); after that it opens from the browser's storage.
- With group colours, groups that share a colour (Drums and FX in the demo are both yellow) look alike; By track or the legend tells them apart.
- Docking the map like the analyser is not built; it is a floating window.
- What only the user can judge: whether owner-by-loudest reads right for the way they listen (an alternative would be "share over 50%"), and whether the brightness range (-84 to -18 dB) suits their mixes. To try: open the map on a finished song, point at the low end in a drop and at 2 to 5 kHz.

### Left
NI-5a: masking cables (the clashes between the loudest tracks from the NI-3 cache at the playhead, cables in the cable lane under a "Clashes" switch). Then NI-5b, the fixes.

## 27 November 2026, v0.247: generic MIDI controllers and templates (task FT-C3a, lane C)
Step FT-C3a of `docs/features-build.md` (the user's pick: "support for other MIDI controllers"). Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ft/ftC3a.py` with `ftC3a_block.js` (two asserted anchors: the `ctlLabel` line and the end of FT-C2c's block; re-run on the fresh file after the rebase over NI-4), test `tools/ui-tests/taskFT_C3a.py` (35 checks, fake controllers).

### Built
- **Moving targets.** A mapping's target can now start with `@` and is worked out when the message arrives: `@dev:0..7` the selected device's knobs (the device panel of the selected track, 8 at a time, the first real device unless changed; the same reading of the panel as the Push), `@vol:k` and `@pan:k` the level or pan of a bank of 8 tracks, `@ms` the master, `@pad:0..15` the drum kit's 16 pads, `@cmd:<id>` a button (Play, Stop, Record, Loop, Metronome, Undo, Redo through the `SCA` commands; previous and next device, previous and next 8 knobs, faders 8 tracks back or on, track above or below, each with a short toast). Takeover (pick up, scale, jump) and the endless-knob detection work as for any mapping; the takeover starts again when the target changes, so a knob does not jump when you select another track.
- **Pads**: when the selected track is a drum kit, a template pad plays its pad (note 36 + pad); on any other track the pad plays a note as before. Buttons act on press only.
- **Templates** (built in): Akai MPK mini (knobs CC 70 to 77, pads channel 10 from note 36), Arturia MiniLab 3 (knobs CC 74, 71, 76, 77, 93, 18, 19, 16; faders CC 82, 83, 85, 17 on 4 track levels; pads channel 10 from 36), Novation Launchkey (MIDI port only, not the DAW port: knobs CC 21 to 28, drum pads channel 10 from 36; faders and buttons by moving), Arturia MiniLab mkII, Arturia KeyLab, Komplete Kontrol in MIDI mode, "Any controller: 8 knobs and 8 faders" (with master, transport and navigation) and "Any pad controller: 16 pads and 8 knobs". The first three are applied by themselves the **first time** such a controller is plugged in, when it has no mappings yet (remembered in `UI.ctlTplSeen`, so removing it is not undone); messages already used by another mapping are left alone.
- **Set up by moving**: on the Controllers page, per connected controller, pick a template and press Set up by moving: AudioLab asks for each knob, fader, pad and button in turn ("move or press Knob 3 now, 3 of 25"); the next new message from that controller fills it (a knob still turning, or one set already, is ignored); Skip, Finish (keeps what is set), Cancel or Esc. This makes every template work whatever the controller sends.
- **Your templates**: Save as my template keeps every mapping of a controller (learned ones too) under a name in `UI.ctlTpl`; it shows under "Yours" in every controller's list, can be used on another controller and deleted. Remove deletes the mappings a template made.
- **MMC transport**: Play, Stop, Pause and Record sent as MIDI Machine Control (many keyboards' transport buttons) work with no mapping.
- Templates are global (`UI.ctl`, like other global mappings); nothing is written into projects. Template mappings appear in the mappings list with plain names ("Selected device, knob 1", "Drum kit pad 16", "Play or pause") and can be edited or deleted like any other. Hook `FT_HOOKS.controllerTemplates` (plan section 6). Audio path untouched.

### Tested (`tools/ui-tests/taskFT_C3a.py`, headless Chromium, fake controllers, 35 checks, all pass)
- An unknown keyboard gets nothing by itself; "MPK mini 3" plugged in gets 24 mappings and a toast; knob 1 follows pick up, then moves the selected device's first knob; another track selected: the same knob moves that track's device. Pad on an instrument track: plays a note as before (noteOn(12), key m36) and stops; on the drum kit: kit pad 3, stopped on note off.
- Controllers page: both controllers under Templates, the MPK's in use; Set up by moving on "Fake Keys" with the 8-knob, 8-fader template: 8 knobs (each turned three times and one turned again: ignored), 3 faders, 6 skipped, Play and Stop, Finish: 13 mappings; fader 1 moves track 1's level; Play and Stop buttons; MMC Play and Stop; Next device with its toast. Save as "Studio keys" (13 controls), used on another controller, removed. Plain names in the list, tooltips on every new control, no em dash. The Launchkey DAW port is left alone; nothing written into the project; nothing of the controller layer runs while still; no console errors.
- Screenshots looked at: the page with the guide banner and the page with two controllers and a user template (the "last message" line no longer squeezed when the page is long). Lite mode does not change this window.
- Also after the rebase: `taskFT_C1a.py` 55 of 55, `taskFT_C1b.py` 29 of 29, `taskFT_C2c.py` 36 of 36, `taskNI_4.py` 31 of 31; `taskFT_C2a.py` and `taskFT_C2b.py` pass except, at times, their idle check (5 timers against a limit of under 5): every timer counted is the glass engine's `gbTick`/`gbCopy` (lane A), none of the controller layer, and it passes on other runs. **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; -9.75669 and -25.48699 dB at 0 dB; Saw, Pad, Plant, Acid, Wavetable, Sampler, Venom, Drum kit the same.

### Sources

- Arturia, MiniLab 3 manual: https://www.fullcompass.com/common/files/85627-MINILAB3MidiControllerManual.pdf and MiniLab 3 general questions: https://support.arturia.com/hc/en-us/articles/6189475866396

## 27 November 2026, v0.248: Mackie Control and HUI (task FT-C3b, lane C)
Step FT-C3b of `docs/features-build.md` (the user's pick: "support for other MIDI controllers"). Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ft/ftC3b.py` with `ftC3b_block.js` (one asserted anchor, the end of FT-C3a's block; re-run on the fresh file after the rebase over NB-R3), test `tools/ui-tests/taskFT_C3b.py` (51 checks, a fake X-Touch, its extender and a fake HUI).

### Built
- **Which devices**: by name (Mackie Control, MCU, X-Touch except the Mini, QCon, Platform M or X: Mackie Control; HUI in the name: HUI), or set by hand per device in the new **Works as** block of the Controllers page (Automatic, Keyboard or controller, Mackie Control, HUI; `UI.ctlAs`). Changing it switches the device's profile at once.
- **Mackie Control**: faders (14-bit pitch bend, channels 1 to 8) on the levels of 8 tracks, the 9th on the master; motors follow AudioLab (after a mouse move, undo, automation while playing) and stay quiet while a fader is touched (touch notes 104 to 112; one undo step a touch). V-pots (CC 16 to 23, sign-bit steps, 1% a step, Shift fine) on pan, or after **Plug-in** on the selected device's first 8 parameters; Pan goes back; pressing a V-pot resets it; LED rings (CC 48 to 55: boost and cut for pan, a bar for parameters). Rec, Solo, Mute, Select per strip with their LEDs. Bank (8, or 16 with an extender) and Channel (1). Play, Stop (stopped: to the start), Record, Cycle, Click, Rewind and Fast forward by a bar, the jog wheel (a 16th a step, Shift: a bar; while playing the jump waits 180 ms for the wheel to stop), Undo (Shift: Redo), Save, Up and Down select the track, Left and Right the device. The **2 x 56 display**: track names (or parameter names) over pans (or values), 6 characters each; the **time code display** in bars, beats, 16ths and ticks (240 a 16th); the assignment display "PN" or "PL". An **extender** (name with Ext or XT) shows the next 8 tracks on its own display id (0x15).
- **HUI**: the ping (`90 00 00` once a second, only while a HUI is connected; it needs it to keep its faders), switches by zone and port (strips: touch, select, mute, solo, rec; zone 0A bank and channel; 0E rewind, forward, stop, play, record; 0F cycle; 0D arrows; 08 shift, undo, save), faders by high and low byte with motors, V-pots (CC 0x40 to 0x47) on pan with their rings, the jog wheel, the 4-letter strip displays (track names), the 2 x 40 display (AudioLab, the tracks shown, the selected track; pans) and the time code.
- A mapping learned on a surface control wins over all this, as on the Push. Everything is sent only when it changed; a check 15 times a second runs only while the song plays with a surface connected; page hidden or the device switched off: displays cleared, LEDs and rings off.

## 27 November 2026: task NB-R3 (the sound path out of the shell's main process; review RN5 A8)

Fired by the scheduler; the next NB item after NB-R2 was NB-R3 (review section 6: "sound path out of the main process: a utilityProcess feeder, a bounded queue, a back-pressure count, a hang watchdog; test: case A again with the main process blocked for 50 ms every second, no gap"). `index.html` untouched; the desktop app behaves as before (the shell stays idle until the page asks for the native engine, which comes with N2c).

### Built
- **`desktop/native-feeder.js`**: an Electron utilityProcess. Takes the page's worklet port (handed on by the shell as a transfer) and the engine's socket address; writes each 128-frame block into the socket. Back-pressure honoured: while the socket says wait, blocks queue up to `queueMs` (250 ms default, 20 to 2,000); beyond that new blocks are dropped whole and counted. Answers pings with its counts.
- **`desktop/native-engine.js`**: the port and the sound go to the feeder (no block in the main process); `openSound` opens the engine's socket without connecting (`engine-bridge.js` `startSound(o, { connect: false })`) and connects the feeder; a **watchdog** once a second while the engine is wanted: feeder ping and engine `status`, 3 misses replace the feeder (`feeder-restarted`, `needPort`) or kill the engine (`engine-hung`, then the crash recovery's `restarted`); 3 feeder restarts in a minute give `gave-up`. `status.tap` names the path and carries the feeder's counts. A replacement page port keeps the socket. `AL_FEED_IN_MAIN=1` keeps the old path (comparison only); without utilityProcess (plain Node) the old path is used. `AL_ENGINE_TEST=1` lets the shell and `preload.js` start the engine off the Mac (null device), for tests. `native-feeder.js` added to the desktop build's files.
- **`native/bridge/page-tap.js`**: `tap.reconnect()` (a new channel to the worklet and the shell) and `alNativeWatchFeeder(nativeEngine, tap)`.
- **`alengine` 0.4** (`tools/native-lab/edits/nb_r3_engine.py`, anchors asserted once): a source switch shuts the old sender's connection down instead of waiting for it to close (a frozen feeder held the command thread; found by this task's test).
- **Tests**: `tools/native-lab/feeder_test.py` with `electron-feeder/` and `feeder_check.py` (real Electron, real shell, feeder, preload, page tap, engine on the null device; the null device's recording compared with what the page sent); `bridge_unit.js` 45 checks (16 new, with a stand-in utilityProcess running the real feeder); `fake-alengine.js` gets `FAKE_HANG_AFTER_MS` and `FAKE_PAUSE_READ`; `engine_null_test.py` 26 checks (2 new). New CI job `electron` in `native-ci.yml`.

### Proven
- Here (2 cores, Electron 45.4.1 as in `desktop/package-lock.json`, production settings 30 ms prefill, exact clock): main process blocked 50 ms every second for 20 s: 960,000 of 960,000 frames bit for bit, no gap, ring never empty (0 gaps in 9 blocked runs); 250 ms every second: 576,000 of 576,000; spinning 50 ms: bit for bit in the strict run (2 of 8 spin runs had one short gap, from blocks reaching the feeder up to 74 ms apart, upstream of the feeder: the spin took half this machine). The old path under the same spin: 2 to 5 gaps per run, up to 152 ms. Feeder frozen (SIGSTOP) at second 4: found after 3 s, killed, replaced, the page gave a new port, the sound came back by itself and stayed bit for bit to the end, never a wrong sample.
- GitHub (run 46030650243, commit 4fdbfcb, 4 cores): `electron` job 14 of 14 (the spinning case strict there, bit for bit, blocks at most 11 ms apart at the feeder; the old path 2 gaps); `node` 45 of 45; `tsan` green. The first two runs failed on the job's own setup (Electron's binary not fetched, numpy missing), fixed in ddc5d31 and 4fdbfcb.

### Left
- The Mac (D9): the same test on Core Audio and in the app's own main process comes with N2c. Upstream jitter (the page's audio thread itself) is not the feeder's to fix; whether 30 ms prefill is enough is NB-R5's production-targets question.
- Next: NB-R4 (engine hardening: NaN/Inf scrub and protect clip, volume ramp, request ids and protocol version, client shutdown, checked conversions), NB-R5 (follower), then N2c when the design chain allows; N3d in parallel.

### Assumptions
- The commit identity and the no-attribution rule come from the repository's CLAUDE.md, as the task says.
- The feeder queue default is 250 ms: long enough for a slow socket moment, short enough that dropped sound stays bounded; the engine's own ring still decides latency.
- Linux CI with the null device stands in for the Mac for this part, because the change is in the shell's processes, not in Core Audio.
- The hold test uses a waiting block for the strict cases (the main process unavailable, which is what A8 is about) and counts the spinning case as strict only on 4 or more cores.


## 27 November 2026, v0.249: task LK, the look tokens (lane A)

Section 6 step 1 of `docs/design-languages-research.md` with the user's DR3 picks `(no direction) | G3 W1 L2 A1 M3 N3`: today's colours, buttons, icons and layout stay; the details apply everywhere. ## 27 November 2026: task NB-R4a (engine hardening, alengine 0.5; review RN5 C6, C7, C8, C10, C11, A10)

Fired by the scheduler with a note from the scheduling chat (15:35 UTC, read as data): do the next stage, review blockers first. No other NB run was working (the only NB commits in the last 20 minutes were NB-R3's own, finished). NB-R4 split: R4a here, R4b (C9's second half) left. `index.html` untouched.

### Built
- `native/engine/engine_main.cpp` (`tools/native-lab/edits/nb_r4_engine.py`): protect (NaN and infinity to 0, a clip at +-1.0, counted, legal samples untouched); the device volume in a ramp thread (0.02 per 5 ms, one event at the end) with a per-device ceiling (level at first open, confirmed levels, levels set outside), `needsConfirm` above it; a `format` event restarts the stream on its own thread under a device lock; dither from `open`'s `dither` (off by default); `deviceLatencyFrames`, `ringLatencyFrames`, `latencyNote`; `numArg` checks every number from the page; `protocol: 1` in ready; `req` echoed in every answer, also on a parse error. `alengine 0.5`.
- `native/common/` (`nb_r4_common.py`): the Core Audio watcher also listens to the output stream's virtual and physical format; dither16 off by default; the null device offers 16 and 24-bit integer formats the system does not mix, writes them through `sample_convert.h` and records what the bytes decode to; `null change=format`; `minijson.h` reads `\u` escapes and surrogate pairs as UTF-8; `wav.h` bounds checks.
- `native/bridge/engine-bridge.js`: request numbers, matching by number, the protocol check at start, `volume(value, confirm)`, SIGKILL 3 s after an ignored stop. The fake engine echoes request numbers and can speak another protocol or answer late.

### Proven
- Here: `engine_null_test.py` 43 of 43 in Release, ASan + UBSan and TSan (new: protocol and request numbers, a parse error answered with its number, 7 kinds of bad number refused by name, bad ring sizes and volumes refused, the ceiling refuses 0.9 until confirmed, the ramp takes 56 ms and is at 0.77 half way, one event, 0.95 needs a confirmation again, quieter needs none, NaN, +-infinity counted (3) and 2.0, -3.0, 1e30 held (3), peak at most 1.0; a format change restarts the stream in 24-bit integer; 24-bit samples through the integer path bit for bit, 96,000 of 96,000; dither only when asked; a broken WAV refused). The older checks unchanged, the hand-over still 192,000 of 192,000. Selftest: `\u` escapes and a surrogate pair. Bridge unit tests 50 of 50. Feeder test 13 of 13. Ring stress ok.
- GitHub (commit 67a1158): push run 46033808827 green on every job; run 46033821125 (Apple Silicon box ticked) green on Linux, its Mac job still waiting for a machine after 7 minutes (D9), left queued.

### Left
- NB-R4b: C9's second half (the socket thread's messages through a queue so they can never wait on the output pipe).
- The Mac: the Core Audio format listener has not been compiled by any machine (D9).
- Then NB-R5 (follower quality), N2c when the design chain allows, N3d.

### Assumptions
- The volume ceiling is "the loudest level the device has had" (first open, confirmed, set outside), not the last level: lowering the volume and raising it back to where it was needs no confirmation; only louder than ever does.
- A volume change from outside during the engine's own ramp is overwritten by the ramp's next step; the event at the end says where it ended.
- Protect is always on (no switch): it changes no legal sample.
- Dither stays a choice made at `open` (the engine does not know the source's bit depth yet); the settings page decides it in N2c.

## 27 November 2026, v0.254: task DS-A4, audio clips in three bands (design round 2, lane A)

Step 2 of the lane order for design round 2 (picks `A5 P4 B3 T3 | AC3 AW3 ...`): the waveform detail **AW3** (and look A5): lows, mids and highs in three muted colours, as the pick page's `arrWave` with `w:3`. Edit script `tools/design-lab/ds/ds_a4.py` (needs DS-A3; every anchor asserted; written on v0.252, re-run on the fresh v0.253 file), test `tools/ui-tests/taskDS_A4.py` (17 checks; `--shots DIR` saves the Dark and Light pictures).

### What changed
- **Three bands**: per audio buffer, the peak of each band per bin: lows through a 2-pole low-pass at 200 Hz, mids through a 2-pole high-pass at 200 Hz and a 2-pole low-pass at 2.5 kHz, highs through a 2-pole high-pass at 2.5 kHz (three separate filters; a first try that took mids as the difference of two low-passes let a kick leak into the mids through their different phase, the test caught it). Drawn from the clip's centre line, lows in `rgba(88,120,200,.62)`, mids in `rgba(206,156,84,.66)`, highs on top in `rgba(236,236,241,.75)` (the pick page's colours; blue only as a fill, never a hairline), a faint one-device-pixel centre line, stereo files in their two halves as before, clip gain applied, each pixel column the largest value of the bins under it.
- **Cost**: the analysis runs once per buffer (and per warped buffer: it is keyed by the buffer's peaks object in a WeakMap and freed with it), at the peaks' resolution (2000 bins), in slices of about 6 ms with `setTimeout` between them, never inside a drawing; when it is done the clip pictures are redrawn once. Drawing goes into the existing per-clip cache (`drawClipC`, keyed by size and zoom), so a zoom or a clip edit redraws from the stored bands and nothing runs per frame. The test's 6.6 s stereo clip took 3 slices.
- **Kept**: today's waveform is drawn until the bands are ready, in the other looks (Live, FL, Cubase, Logic, Bitwig and the rest) and for audio that is not loaded; fades, gain line and label, warp markers, envelopes and the DS-A3 clip body are unchanged. No audio nodes: playback and exports do not change.
- What it looks like on Fractals' vocal: mostly amber and white (voice and air), gaps clear; the outline sits a little inside today's, because each band carries only part of the signal (the bands are not stacked).
- Helpers `dsBands(view)`, `dsBandJob`, `dsBandCols`, `dsWaveDraw`, `dsBandMap()` (before `askChoice`). Lane D's NI analysis (frequency map) is a different thing (rendered tracks per beat, 61 bands) and is not used or duplicated here.

### Tested

## 27 November 2026, v0.255: linked clips (task FT-F1, lane C)
Step FT-F1 of `docs/features-build.md` (starred card F1 of `docs/research-features-gap.md`, section 4 "RF-F1 Linked clips"). Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ft/ftF1.py` with `ftF1_block.js` (two asserted anchors: the end of FT-C3c's block, and the `dup` entry of `SCA` for the two commands; re-run on the fresh file after the rebase over DS-A4), test `tools/ui-tests/taskFT_F1.py` (29 checks).

### Built
- **The model**: `clip.link`, an optional id shared by linked copies (older songs have none and load as before). Shared: for MIDI clips the notes, controller lanes (`cc`), bend range (`pbr`) and envelopes; for audio clips the gain, warp markers and envelopes. Each copy keeps its own place, length, start offset, fades, name and mute.
- **How an edit spreads**: every linked clip has a baseline of what it holds. After an edit (`changed()`), a linked clip that differs from its baseline is the one edited, and its content is copied into the other copies **in the same undo step** (the snapshot was taken before the edit). The selected clips and the piano roll's clip are checked at once; every linked clip is checked a quarter second after an edit (catches edits made elsewhere, such as a whole-track transpose) and a link left with one clip is dropped. Nothing runs while idle. Note selection in the piano roll is not shared.
- **Envelopes in content time**: a copy that starts later in the content has its points shifted, so an envelope stays in step with the notes. A move, a resize or a split changes a clip's placement and is never shared (a left resize of one copy changes no other); a split keeps both halves linked (same notes).
- **Making and breaking**: **Alt+Shift-drag** makes linked copies (one or a selection; Shift-drag stays a plain copy, and a plain copy of a linked clip is unique); clip menu **Duplicate as linked copy** (also the command `clip.linkedDup`), and on a linked clip **Make unique** (`clip.unique`, also for a selection) and **Select linked copies**. Plain Duplicate (Mod+D) and copy and paste of a linked clip keep it linked. Toasts say what happened.
- **Chain mark**: a small chain on a dark pill right after the clip name (or in the middle on thin tracks), part of the clip's cached picture.
- **Fractals**: its repeated Kick and Bass clips are linked when the song is built (2 groups of 12 on each track: same notes and envelopes); the start-up check that tells a stored Fractals tab from an edited one ignores links, so an old stored tab is not kept as "(edited)".
- **File**: every copy keeps its full content, so an older AudioLab opens the song as plain clips; the links add under 1 % (531,221 against 530,252 characters for Fractals) and the file is gzipped.
- Hook `FT_HOOKS.clipLinks`; no settings rows. Audio path untouched.

### Tested (`tools/ui-tests/taskFT_F1.py`, headless Chromium, 29 checks, all pass)
- Fractals: Kick and Bass 24 linked clips each in 2 groups, no other track linked; the chain mark in the clip picture's key. An edit to one Kick clip changes all 12 at once in one undo step; undo and redo every copy. Clip menu has the three new entries, no em dash; Transpose +1 octave from the menu reaches every copy; Select linked copies selects 12. A left resize of one copy changes no other; an envelope point at beat 2 of that copy shows at beat 6 of the others; a note edit on it reaches the others. Make unique (command) and its edits stay its own. Duplicate as linked copy (command) on a Lead clip, a note added to the copy shows in the original. Real mouse: Shift-drag of a linked clip gives a plain copy, Alt+Shift-drag a linked copy, the original stays. Audio: gain shared, fade not. The other copy deleted: the last is a plain clip. File under 1 % bigger. A reloaded song keeps working links; a song without links opens with none. Nothing runs while still. No console errors.
- Screenshots looked at: the clip menu, and Kick clips with the chain mark beside the name (the plain Shift-drag copy has none).
- Also: `taskAJ.py` all OK, `taskDS_A3.py` 19 of 19, `taskDS_A4.py` 17 of 17, `taskAI.py` all pass (the Fractals boot and kept tabs), `taskFT_C2c.py` 36, `taskFT_C3b.py` 51, `taskFT_C3c.py` 57. **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; -9.75669 and -25.48699 dB at 0 dB; Saw, Pad, Acid, Wavetable, Venom the same. Plant, Sampler, Sampler grains and Drum kit give other numbers on every run, on the untouched v0.253 too (they are seeded at random in that check), so they say nothing about this step.

### Only the user can test

### What changed
- **CSS tokens** (before `.dacv`): `--ov-row` 26 px, `--ov-r` 10 px (R2 menus, D3 popovers), `--ov-r-item` 6, `--ov-r-tip` 8 (T3 callout), `--ov-r-card` 9 (N1), `--ov-r-pal` 12 (K1), `--ov-hi` the focused row (R2 keeps today's blue fill, `--blf`), `--ov-tint` the soft blue tint (drop targets, palette rows), `--ov-ln` the hairline, `--ov-mut`, `--ov-amb` (LOOK's amber `--unit`: T3 leader, Advanced), `--ov-lab` mono capitals 9.5 px with `--ov-labsp` .12em, `--ov-key` mono 11 px. Motion: `--ov-in` 90 ms, `--ov-out` 60 ms, `--ov-sheet` 140 ms, `--ov-tip` 80 ms, `--ov-card` 140 ms, `--ov-ease`, all times `--ov-mo`, which is 0 with the system's reduced motion and with Motion set to "Signal only" (LOOK, `body.lkm1`).
- **The same numbers as a LOOK entry** (`lkT().ov`, made by `ovLook()`): sizes, the label font, and `ms` (in, out, sheet, tip, card, sub 120, typeahead 600, tipDelay 500, tipWarm 300, drain 6000, log 8000) and `cards` 3, from the pick page's timing table. `ovMs(k)` gives a time (0 for the transitions when motion is off), `ovStill()` says whether motion is off. The later steps read these.
- **The one visible change**: the right-click menu (`#ctxm`) fades in over 90 ms from 3 px above and fades out over 60 ms. For the code the menu is closed at once (`hidden` is set straight away, focus leaves it, it is `inert` and lets clicks through while it fades), so every check of `ctxm.hidden` behaves as before. A MutationObserver on the menu does it, so every way of closing (Esc, a click outside, an entry, `closeMenu()`, window blur) fades. No fade for the three-column menus (their layout changes on close), the drop-up menus keep their own 140 ms animation, none in Light mode (it has no animations: the fade-in rule is off there, as with reduced motion and "Signal only").
- **Glass engine**: `glfShown` lets a hidden element with class `ovout` through, so the engine keeps the menu's glass face during the 60 ms fade-out; it already follows the element's opacity. No `backdrop-filter`.

## 27 November 2026, v0.257: task IN-M, the level meters (lane E, instruments)

Step IN-M of `docs/design-round-4-instruments.md`, the user's pick **M2** (peak and RMS in one bar). Edit script `tools/design-lab/in/in_m.py` with `in_m_block.js` (every anchor asserted unique), test `tools/ui-tests/taskIN_M.py` (26 checks, all pass). Written on v0.245, rebased onto v0.254, v0.255 and v0.256 by re-running the edit script on the fresh file.

### Built (block "lane E (task IN-M)" before `askChoice`)
- **The RMS core in every level meter.** The bar keeps its look (Flat bars and every other fader design, colours, the hold line) and gets a bright core: the RMS over 300 ms (AES17, so a sine reads its peak level); the part of the bar above the core, up to the peak, is faint (DIGICheck style). In: the mixer's fader meters (strips and master), the track headers, the device panel's track meter, the transport meter, the mixer's meter view and the big meter in Settings.
- **Nothing new is read from the audio.** The meter engine (`mtrPeak`) already reads each analyser's new samples once per frame; the same samples now also feed `INS.pr`, a 300 ms window in 10 ms pieces (sum of squares and the highest sample).
- **Read-outs: peak, RMS, crest factor.** Crest = the highest sample over 300 ms against the true RMS of the same 300 ms (a sine reads 3.0 dB, a square 0 dB). The master strip in the mixer shows RMS (dBFS) and Crest (dB) above the true peak box; the channel peak read-outs (`.mxpkr`) and the transport's peak box give peak, RMS and crest in their tooltips (twice a second); the big meter in Settings shows RMS and Crest under its Peak. Real minus sign, thin space before the unit (the IN-A formatter).
- **Scale:** the mixer's meter view and the Settings meter now follow the fader taper (they were linear, so they did not match the fader meters) with the M1 tick scale (`INS.scaleTaper`: a mark per dB to −12, every 3 dB to −24, then every 6). The Settings meter's numbers were cut off at its 50 px width; it shows the ticks only.
- **Kept as the user has them:** the speed, reading, colours and hold settings. The core shows with the Peak reading (the default); with RMS, VU or Loudness the bar is an average already, so there is no core, and the read-outs stay. M1's standard digital-peak fall (20 dB in 1.7 s, `INS.peak`) is not forced on the bar, since the Speed setting decides that; it could become a Speed choice if wanted.
- **Shared:** `INS.mbar(g,x,y,w,h,peak,rms,fill,horizontal)` is the one canvas bar drawer (transport, meter view, Settings). **For DS-T2 (lane A):** TM1 reuses it, with `INM.rfr(analyser,map)` for the core. The look comes from `LOOK` through `INS.look()` (task LK, v0.249); the two new values, `INM.faint` (0.38, canvas) and `INM.VEIL` (`rgba(7,8,11,.6)`, page elements), are named for LK to take over.
- **Page-element meters** get the core as an inset shadow along the top of the bar itself (paint only, no extra element): a first version with a `::after` box per bar doubled the style work that `miniMeter` forces each meter frame (CPU profile: 65 to 163 ms in 6 s). Header veils update 30 times a second, as the header glass does; strip positions are cached (read again every 60 frames), the scroll position comes from the scroll event.
- **Overlaps named:** idea I3's Clip button and card near the meters (v0.234) and the `NI_clipSeen` calls are untouched; the true peak in the master box is task IN-L's area (unchanged).

### Tested (`tools/ui-tests/taskIN_M.py`, at 2194x1139, signals made in the page or played through the app)
- Window: 1 kHz sine at −18 dBFS reads RMS −18.00, peak −18.00, crest 3.01 dB; a square at −6 dBFS crest 0.00 dB; pink noise at −20 dBFS RMS reads −17.0 (AES17) with crest 10.9 dB; 150 ms after a stop the reading is 3.0 dB lower (half the window) and gone at 300 ms; odd-sized pieces give the same numbers. The bar drawer: core opaque, the part above it faint, nothing above the peak.
- Live: the sine in both channels reads master RMS −17.98, crest 3.01, both channels equal and steady to 0.005 dB; an anti-phase pair −17.98 on each channel; a log sweep 20 Hz to 20 kHz at −12 dBFS stays within −12.03 and −11.94; pink noise RMS −17.06, crest 10.9. Master strip read-outs "−18.0" and "3.0", tooltips with units. Flat bars (design 7) kept with the core; the core is visible on the transport meter, the mixer's meter view and the track headers with pink noise; with the RMS reading the core is off and the read-outs stay. Mixer closed: no mixer pass; background freeze (the frame gate shut): no frames and no veil writes. Settings meter (since lane B's S5 on the Mixer page): RMS and Crest read-outs. No console errors, no audio nodes, no em dashes.
- **Track meters:** a track's taps (`N.aL`, `N.aR`) hold 256 samples (5.8 ms), so its RMS is built from the snapshots the meters read, not every sample; the test track reads within 0.1 dB of the master in most runs, once 0.58 dB lower (the check allows 0.75). The master's taps hold 2048 and see every sample. The track peak reading has the same limit today. IN-S, which moves analyser sizes into the IN-A cache, is the place to enlarge them (the mixer's spectrum views read the same taps).
