## 27 November 2026: task NB-R4b (the engine never waits on the app; alengine 0.6; review RN5 C9, and gaps in C6 and C7)

Fired by the scheduler. This run started on NB-R4 while a parallel NB run was doing the same stage; that run pushed NB-R4a first (alengine 0.5, the bulk of R4). This run's own version of R4 (branch `nb-r4-mine`, not pushed) was dropped rather than merged, and the run did NB-R4b on top of R4a, carrying over only what R4a lacked. `index.html` untouched.

### Built
- **Output through one writer thread (C9).** `say()` puts the line in a queue; one thread writes and flushes. The socket thread, the system's listener and the volume ramp never wait on the pipe. Answers are never dropped; events beyond 4,096 waiting lines are dropped and counted (`status.output`: `waiting`, `waitingMax`, `eventsDropped`). The queue is drained before the engine exits.
- **`std::cin.tie(nullptr)`.** Found by the new test: `std::cin` is tied to `std::cout`, so each `getline` flushed stdout, and with the shell not reading, the command thread waited on the stdio lock and stopped reading commands.
- **Format restart through a worker.** The listener only sets a request (`fmtReq`) and returns; `formatWorker` restarts under the device lock. In 0.5 the listener joined the previous restart thread, which waited on the device lock the command thread may hold (a possible hang on the Mac, where removing a listener may wait for the listener in flight).
- **A race fixed.** `isOpen` is atomic and `status` reads under the device lock (ThreadSanitizer: the restart wrote `isOpen` and the stream's format text while `status` read them; present since 0.5).
- **Files at another rate than the device are refused** (both rates named), unless `anyRate: true`.
- **The shell (`desktop/native-engine.js`)**: drops `confirm` and `req` from what the page sends; on `needsConfirm` asks the person in its own dialog (Electron's `dialog.showMessageBox`, "Make it louder" / "Keep it") and only then sends `confirm: true`; no dialog means no. `format` events reach the page. `setup()` takes an optional `dialog` (tests).
- Tests: `engine_null_test.py` (a reader that can stop reading: `Engine.hold`), `bridge_unit.js`, `fake-alengine.js` (volume ceiling, `FAKE_FORMAT_EVENT_MS`).

### Proven
- Here: `engine_null_test.py` 50 of 50 in Release, ASan + UBSan and TSan (each twice). New: the engine still takes 3,000 commands while its output is unread; a new sender connects and 1.5 s of sound goes in at its own pace (1.40 s); every frame reached the ring (72,064, nothing dropped); all 3,000 answers arrive once read again (4,205 lines waited, 248 events dropped and counted); 40 format changes during 40 opens, all answered (0.7 s); a 44.1 kHz file on a 48 kHz device refused. Against alengine 0.5 the same test fails 6 checks: commands stop being read, only 12,032 of 72,064 frames go in within 6 s.
- `bridge_unit.js` 55 of 55 (5 new): the dialog says yes (sent with confirm, 80 % set), no (refused, level kept), or there is none (refused); the page's own confirm never reaches the engine (4 sends of 0.8, one with confirm); the format event reaches the page. Electron feeder test 13 of 13 (real Electron 45.4.1, real shell, engine 0.6). Mixer 10 of 10 identical.
- GitHub: the push run for 542df25 (46038865376) was cancelled after 50 s by the workflow's own rule (a newer push, the user's fifth test-app report c882e6d, touched `tools/native-lab`); that newer run, 46038950323, contains this commit and is **green on every Linux job** (linux with sanitizers and the 240 device cases, tsan, node, electron). A run with the Apple Silicon box ticked was started afterwards; as in every run since NB-R1 a Mac machine is not expected to start (D9).

### Left
- The Mac (D9): no macOS runner has started a job since NB-R1; the Core Audio format listener and the writer thread on macOS are compiled by no machine yet.
- Next: NB-R5 (follower quality: per-rate kernel, bypass at speed 1, 19 to 21 kHz test points, production targets, a bursty sender), then N2c when the design chain allows; N3d in parallel.

### Assumptions
- Two NB runs at once: the first to push owns the stage name; the later one does the next part on top and drops its duplicate.
- Events (not answers) may be dropped past 4,096 waiting lines: the page reads state again with `status` anyway, and a queue without limit would grow while the shell is hung.
- The confirmation dialog belongs to the shell, not the page, because the page comes through an update channel that is not signed (RN6 1.4); the words of the dialog can change with the settings page (S11).
- A file source must match the device's rate, like the page (NB-R2); `anyRate` exists for tests.

## 27 November 2026, v0.258: task NI-5a, masking cables part 1: the clashes (lane D, idea I12, NF5)

Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ni/ni_5a.py` (anchored; needs NI-3 and NI-4), test `tools/ui-tests/taskNI_5a.py` (34 checks, all pass). The step was claimed in the plan before it started.

### Built
- **Clashes at the playhead, from NI-3's cache** (`NI_clashAt(beat)`, no live analysis, nothing in the audio path): per track the energy (mid plus side) of that beat in **1/3-octave bands** (two of NI-3's 1/6-octave bands each). The **12 loudest tracks** that play at that beat are compared in pairs; with the cable lane's **Selected only**, the selected track against every other (none when it is silent there). A band clashes when both tracks are over the **floor** (36 dB under the loudest band at that beat, kept between -80 and -50 dB, so a quiet mix is judged like a loud one) and **within 12 dB** of each other. The strength of a pair is its strongest band: how far the quieter track is over the floor, less for a bigger gap; the band range around it ("95 to 120 Hz") is every neighbouring band with at least half that strength. At most **8 cables**, strongest first.
- **A "Clashes" switch in the mixer's cable legend** (`UI.mxs.niClash`, with the count at the playhead, "…" while still measuring). With it on, each clash is a **magenta cable** between the two strips (its own colour, not a track colour, never red against green), **thicker for a bigger clash**, labelled "Bass vs Kick, 95 to 120 Hz" under its curve (labels that would cover each other are left to the tooltip), tooltip with both levels and the gap. Hover lights it; **click**: a small card with the band, bar and beat, both levels, and Select (the covered, quieter channel). With Clashes on the lane asks for two more rows of room, only out of the room the channels leave (a height dragged by hand wins).
- **Command `ni.clashes`** ("Show clashes between tracks in the mixer"): opens the mixer, the cable lane and Clashes.
- **Snappy**: a 250 ms check runs only while the mixer is open with the cable lane and Clashes on; it works only when the beat, the project or the analysis changed, and draws only when the list of clashes changed. A piece not measured yet is measured in the background (`NI.an.ensure`), and while playing the next piece ahead. Closing the mixer or switching Clashes off stops it.
- `NI.clash` (`at`, `draw`, `pop`) and `NI_HOOKS.clashPop(c, card)` for NI-5b's fixes.
- **Fix for NI-1b**: since v0.257 lane E's meters (IN-M) rewrite the transport peak box's tooltip twice a second, which wiped NI-1b's clip note ("Click to see why"; the orange dot still showed). Lane D's block now puts the note in front of their text while a clip event is flagged, and leaves their text alone otherwise; lane E's code is not touched. `taskNI_1b.py` failed on main v0.257 for this and passes again (36 of 36); lane E's `taskIN_M.py` 26 of 26.

### Checked
- A test song (audio, 120 BPM, 8 bars): Bass 100 Hz all through; Kick 106 Hz in bars 1 to 4, then 3 kHz; Pad 1 kHz; Hat 8 kHz; a send from Pad to a return (a normal cable). At beat 4: **exactly one clash, Bass and Kick, 95 to 120 Hz** (-19.4 and -19.6 dB), one magenta cable with that label, the legend says 1; the strength matches the formula from the levels and the floor. At beat 20 (the kick moved to 3 kHz): **no clash**, no cable, the legend says 0. Selected only: Pad selected, none; Kick selected, Bass and Kick. While playing from bar 4 the list follows the playhead (gone after bar 5). An edit (the bass moved to bar 5) is measured again and the clash at beat 4 goes; undo brings it back from the cache.
- The normal cables: the same cables in the same colours with Clashes on (the lane is taller, so their paths sit lower: 52 to 84 px here), the exact same paths with it off, the legend's own buttons unchanged. Nothing worked out or drawn in 1.5 s with the playhead still; the song is not changed (no undo step, same tracks); closing the mixer stops the check. Tooltips on the switch and every cable, no em dashes, no console errors.
- Screenshots looked at: the mixer with the clash (normal and Light level), the card. The Fractals demo: at beat 160 (Drop 1) "Toms vs Kick, 38 to 60 Hz" and "Toms vs Bass"; at 130 "Bass vs Impact"; in the kick-and-bass part (beat 100) none, since the demo's bass sits about 20 dB under its kick.
- **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`, measured on this version and on main): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB, in every run; -9.75669 (0496bb147f6c) and -25.48699 dB (09e0415bec5e) at 0 dB on the run after the rebase onto v0.256. Earlier runs of both this build and main sometimes read the Bass at 0 dB as -26.74483 dB (a6774faed0a9), the flip NI-3 already logged (main gave it once in four runs, the same hash); Plant, the Sampler and the Drum kit also differ between two runs of main itself, so they are run-to-run noise; Saw, Pad, Acid, Wavetable and Venom the same checksums. No audio code was touched: the block makes no audio nodes.
- Also: after the rebases onto v0.256 and v0.257: `taskNI_5a.py` 34 of 34, `taskNI_4.py` 31 of 31, `taskNI_2b.py` 36 of 36, `taskNI_1b.py` 36 of 36, lane F's `taskOV1.py` 25 of 25, lane E's `taskIN_M.py` 26 of 26; before them lane B's `taskST_S5.py` 84 of 84 and lane A's `taskLK.py` 32 of 32. `cables3.py` (the mixer cables at three heights, 2, 8 and 34 cables) gives the same layout as main (lane height, rows, labels); a first build lost one cable label in a small window because the Clashes button widened the legend, so the button now takes its room from the hint text at the end of the legend.

### Limits
- As NI-3: a track's numbers leave out its sends and sidechain ducking, so a bass ducked by the kick still shows its full overlap with the kick (a ducking-aware measure would render the sidechain source too; NI-5b's fixes should say so).
- One beat at a time (a beat's average): a kick and a bass that alternate inside the beat count as overlapping. Groups and returns are not compared (not analysed).
- What only the user can judge: whether the floor (36 dB under the loudest band) and the 12 dB gap catch the clashes they hear, and whether magenta reads well next to their track colours. To try: open a drop of a finished song, run "Show clashes between tracks in the mixer" from the commands, play, and watch which pairs light up; click one and solo the two.

NI-5b: click a clash cable for the fixes (a band-limited duck of one under the other with the Ducker, or a 2 dB EQ notch), each one undo step, through `NI_HOOKS.clashPop`.


## 27 November 2026: task NB-R5 (the clock follower's quality; review RN5 C3, C4)

Fired by the scheduler with a note from the scheduling chat (16:27 UTC, read as data): do the next stage; stop if another NB run committed in the last 20 minutes. The only NB commits in the 20 minutes before were this session's own NB-R4b (finished); the note predates R4a and R4b. To avoid a second overlap like R4's, the step was claimed in the running list first (commit c0485b0). `index.html` untouched.

### Built
- `native/engine/follow.h`: `SincTable` 128 taps, cutoff 1.0 (the top frequency), Kaiser beta 13 (was 48, 0.92, 11); rows at whole samples exact (now the kernel's own limit, no jump). `Steer` kp 0.1, ki 0.0025 (was 0.04, 0.0004), acquisition: x3 (kp x3, ki x9) for 30 s after a reset, integral rescaled at the handover so the speed does not jump; `holdIntegral()`.
- `native/engine/ring.h`: speed exactly 1 on a whole sample copies the sample (bit for bit, -0.0 kept); the steering is no longer reset when the ring primes again after running empty, and only the fill's smoothing restarts after a drop; `HISTORY` 160 frames (the kernel looks back 63); `fillMin` with a reset request (`noteFill`).
- `native/engine/engine_main.cpp`: default `prefillMs` 40; the socket thread measures the longest wait between arrivals; status `ring.targetMs`, `fillMinMs`, `worstGapMs`; `reset` clears them; the selftest's follower part rewritten (bit for bit with -0.0, a response table at 44.1 kHz from 997 Hz to 21 kHz, four bursty senders at the 40 ms target, the cost).
- Shell and bridge default `prefillMs` 40 (`desktop/native-engine.js`, `native/bridge/engine-bridge.js`).
- The model and the simulation used to choose these: a numpy model of the kernel (it reproduces the review's table for the old one: -4.23 dB at 20 kHz) and a C++ simulation of `ring.h` with a sender whose blocks are delayed by 0 to 4 ms and held 10 or 25 ms about once a second, at targets 30, 40, 50 ms (scratch files, not committed; their results are in the running list).

### Proven
- Selftest (Release here): 20 kHz at 44.1 kHz 0.000 dB with error -120 dB (needed: within 0.5 dB); 21 kHz -0.018 dB; senders off by +50, -250, +1000, -1000 ppm, bursty, 40 ms target, 4 minutes: never empty, never a drop, steered to 52.1, -249.9, 1000.7, -999.9 ppm, fill 8 to 41 ms after the first minute; cost 16 to 18 us per 128-frame block at 48 kHz (0.6 to 0.7 %). Under ASan + UBSan the selftest passes in 49 s.
- `engine_null_test.py` 52 of 52 in Release, ASan + UBSan and TSan (new: the default target is 40 ms; a feeder-like sender with one 20 ms stall: worst wait 20.3 ms and lowest fill 26 ms in the status, never empty). Ring stress (two threads) ok in both modes. `bridge_unit.js` 55 (its default check now expects 40). Electron feeder test 13 of 13. Mixer identical.
- GitHub: push run 46042034200 (commit e7163f7, which also carries test app 0.5's commit 0e3bb3a whose own run it replaced) **green on every Linux job**: linux (Release and ASan+UBSan selftest with the new follower checks, the null-device test, the mixer, all device cases against the web engine), tsan, node, electron. The Mac job was not asked for; the dispatch with the Mac ticked after NB-R4b (run 46040068132) ended without a Mac machine (D9, as every run since NB-R1).

### Left
- The real clocks: how many ppm the Gryphon and the Zoom are off from the page's device, and the real gaps on the M4 (status `worstGapMs`), come with N2c on the user's Mac; the 1-hour run is NB-R10.

### Assumptions
- 40 ms is the default because it is the smallest of the tested targets that held through the worst gaps measured at the feeder (25 ms); lower latency is for the settings page to offer from what `worstGapMs` and `fillMinMs` show on the user's Mac, and for N3 (native playback has no ring).
- The acquisition phase (30 s, three times faster) is chosen so that a sender 1,000 ppm off never sinks the fill below the margin; its extra wobble (about 3 times, still under 0.1 cent) lasts only those 30 s.
- Real crystals are usually under 100 ppm; ±1,000 ppm is tested as the far case.

No app changes: `index.html`, `desktop/` and `native/engine/` were not touched, no version. Touched: `native/host/` (host layer, new `diag.cpp`), `native/testapp/` (the app, new `strictsynth/`), the test-app part of `native/CMakeLists.txt`, `tools/native-lab/READ-ME-FIRST.txt`, `.github/workflows/native-lab.yml`, `docs/native-mac-build.md`, this log. Ran in parallel with task NB.

### From the user's fifth report (0.4, 18:04 Brussels)
- Search worked (Phase Plant found and loaded); 1,428 knob moves from Phase Plant's window reached the host (gestures 4 and 4).
- Phase Plant SILENT (peak 0.000) on the Gryphon at 48 kHz and 44.1 kHz with 63, 80 and 113 notes sent; Pigments was silent the same way in report 4. The 16 kHz explanation of NL4 is wrong for Phase Plant.
- The Gryphon appeared during the scan; the app switched to it but wrote no [device] line for it.
- 32 Intel-only bundles (Output's Arcade, Black, Boost, Brass, Clone, Duck, Hatz, Infiltrator, Minipol, PitchMonster, Shaper2, Tantrum, Tapex2, Texture, Transient Master, Vybz, Midnight Mirage; the 14 RX 9 plug-ins), one broken (helisert_6.0).
- Mojibake ("12‚ÄØ%", "‚àí3.26‚ÄØdB"): UTF-8 read as Mac Roman.

### Cause found (code read against the SDK and JUCE's VST3 host; mechanism proven with a test instrument; the user's Mac still to confirm)
- The SDK's `PlugProvider`, used by 0.1 to 0.4, never calls `IEditController::setComponentState` with the processor's state (JUCE: `synchroniseStates`), and connects processor and controller through `ConnectionProxy`, which drops every message not sent from the main thread (JUCE connects directly). Plug-ins with separate processor and controller that pass the patch between them (Kilohearts, Arturia) can stay silent; JUCE-built ones (Surge XT, Serum 2) share one object and never noticed.
- The rest of the checklist (bus arrangements and activation, setupProcessing, setActive and setProcessing order, buffers for every output bus, events, process context, sample size, run loop) was already right in 0.4 except the order and stereo forcing of the bus set-up and only the first event input on; changed to the validator's and JUCE's way, not a cause found.

### Built (0.5)
See `docs/native-mac-build.md`, section on report 5 and test app 0.5: own set-up instead of PlugProvider (state to the controller, messages from any thread, counted), validator order with the plug-in's preferred arrangements, `HostOptions` to switch each 0.4 behaviour back; `[diag]` lines; "Why silent?" probe in a child process with nine set-ups and a conclusion line (also automatic once per silent instrument; `alvst3 diag` on the command line); factory presets (program list, .vstpreset) and a `[state]` line; `[device] appeared:` for hot-plugged devices; `[rosetta]` and `[broken]` lists at the end; `[clap]` and `[au]` listings for D5; report in ASCII with a BOM only if needed; AL Strict Synth, a test instrument that only sounds with both fixes.

### Tested
Build machine: GitHub's `macos-latest` runner (virtual Apple M2 Pro, macOS 26.7.2), run 46041572291 on commit 141af31 (main with this task's commit 0e3bb3a): this is the published build. ## 27 November 2026, v0.260: task NI-5b, masking cables part 2: the fixes (lane D, idea I12, NF5)

Idea I12 is complete. Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ni/ni_5b.py` (anchored; needs NI-5a), test `tools/ui-tests/taskNI_5b.py` (22 checks, all pass). The step was claimed in the plan before it started. (This run's trigger still said NI-4 was the last release; the plan's rule is the next step not yet logged, so this run did NI-5b.)

### Built
- **Two fixes in the clash card**, each one undo step, for the covered (quieter) channel:
  - **Duck it under the louder one in this band**: a Ducker on the covered track, triggered by the louder track, listening to that band (Listen to: Band, Focus at the band centre), ducking **only that band**, 50% (about 6 dB at the centre) while the louder one plays there; trigger level 9 dB under the louder track's band level.
  - **Notch it by 2 dB**: a -2 dB bell at the band centre on the covered track's first Pro EQ (the unused bell band nearest in frequency; a new Pro EQ when it has none or no free bell), Q from the width of the clash range (1/3 octave: Q 4.3).
- **The Ducker's band mode** (`p.bd`, width `p.bq` as Q): no existing device could duck a single band (the Ducker ducks all of a sound and its Focus only chooses what it listens to; the Pro EQ's dynamic bands react to their own track and work live only). In the Ducker's worklet the band mode computes `out = x - (1 - gain) * band(x)` with a zero-phase state-variable band-pass around the Focus frequency, so the centre is ducked by the full amount and the rest of the sound is untouched. Without `p.bd` the per-sample code is the old one. The band is twice as wide as the clash range, so its edges are ducked too.
- **The Ducker window**: with Listen to "Band" (or the mode on), a button **Only this band** next to Hear it, one undo step (`NI_HOOKS.duckBandRow`; it wraps both the window's builder `agBuild` and `abxBuild`, as the window calls itself by name).
- **A handled clash**: NI-3 measures one track at a time, so it cannot hear ducking. A clash whose covered track already ducks under the louder one in that band is drawn **dimmed and dashed**, labelled "Bass ducks under Kick, 95 to 120 Hz", and not counted in the legend; its card offers **Open the Ducker**. The notch is measured: the bass is measured again with its EQ and the clash gets weaker.

### Checked
- Test song: Kick 106 Hz (louder), Bass 100 Hz plus 1 kHz, Pad 3 kHz. One clash, Kick and Bass, 95 to 120 Hz; the card offers both fixes with tooltips.
- **Notch**: one undo step; a bell at 107 Hz, -2 dB, Q 4.32 on the bass's Pro EQ; the bass measured again and the clash strength fell from 32.8 to 29.3; undo restores the bass's effects exactly.
- **Duck**: one undo step; a Ducker on Bass, trigger Kick, Band at 107 Hz, Q 2.16, 50%. Rendered with the bass heard and the kick built as its trigger: **100 Hz down 5.1 dB, 1 kHz unchanged (-0.01 dB)**; with "Only this band" turned off in the window (one undo step) the 1 kHz drops 6 dB too, as a normal Ducker. The cable turns dimmed with "ducks under", the legend says 0, the card offers Open the Ducker, which opens the window with Only this band lit.
- **Untouched tracks**: the Pad renders bit-identical through both fixes. **Existing Duckers**: a Ducker without the new fields renders the same as with the band mode off, and a song with a default Ducker (Listen to All, Lows, Band) renders with the same checksums on this build and on main v0.258 (efbd3caefccf, bd2652e678e3, e0073ca6571a).
- **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`, measured): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; -9.75669 (0496bb147f6c) and -25.48699 dB (09e0415bec5e) at 0 dB. The Ducker's worklet changed only behind the new switch; no other audio code was touched.
- Also: `taskNI_5a.py` 34 of 34, `taskNI_4.py` 31 of 31, `taskNI_1b.py` 36 of 36; the Ducker window tests `taskAB.py` and `taskAG.py` run clean (no failures, no console errors) on this build as on main; after the rebase onto lane E's v0.259 `taskNI_5b.py` 22 of 22, `taskNI_5a.py` 34 of 34 and `taskNI_1b.py` 36 of 36 again.

## 27 November 2026, v0.261: task HF1, the v0.250 start-up glitch and the release gate (top priority)

The user (18:13 Brussels, M4 Mac mini, 240 Hz, desktop app) opened v0.250 and it "starts glitching all over the place as if someone's clicking all over the place": tracks selected, the playhead and play/stop running several times a second, the instrument browser opening, EQ points moving, mutes and solos on, a "Kick & Bass copy" track, quitting froze; also in an empty project. The update window's long notes also pushed its buttons out of reach.

### The cause
- **The user's Mac has the IAC Driver online with two ports made for Cubase: "Ableton Push to Cubase" and "nanoKey2 to Cubase"** (their Audio MIDI Setup screenshots, 19:07). The user has no Push or other MIDI device plugged in.
- Since v0.233 the desktop app opens every MIDI port at start. The Push 1 profile (`p1Match`, v0.238) takes any input whose name contains "Ableton Push" (not "User", not Push 2 or 3), so it took the IAC port. It sent its Live-mode SysEx, display lines, pad and button LEDs to the matching output, the same IAC port. IAC is a loop-back, so every message came straight back in.
- In v0.238 to v0.241 the echoes only toggled Scales and repainted (614 echoes in 10 s, nothing visible).
- From **v0.242 (task FT-C2b, Push part 2: buttons run commands)** the button LED values came back as presses. Note-on/CC with a non-zero value is a press, so:
  - Play (CC 85) toggled play
  - Stop and Record ran
  - New (CC 87) ran `newmidi`, which opens the instrument browser
  - Duplicate (CC 88) duplicated the selected track: "Kick & Bass copy"
  - the upper and lower rows (CC 20 to 27, 102 to 109) selected tracks and switched mute, solo and arm
  - the arrows moved the selection
  - Undo ran
  - every change relit the buttons, which echoed again
- **Line:** `p1bCc` (Push 1 part 2, the button handler), reached through `ctlMsg` with no echo guard; the match is `p1Match` in part 1.
- The user confirmed it: with the IAC Driver switched offline, v0.250 opens calmly.

### Bisect (the start-up harness, scenario `iac-push`: those two IAC ports, echoing)
| Version | Result |
|---|---|
| v0.237 | clean, nothing sent |
| v0.238 | loop starts (634 sent, 614 back), no visible change |
| v0.241 | the same |
| **v0.242** | synthetic clicks on Record, Metronome, Stop and Loop; frame time p50 50 ms (60 ms per frame and worse) |
| v0.250 | the same |
| v0.261 | clean, nothing sent to the port |

- Idle with no MIDI, with a plain keyboard, with ports named like the user's audio software, and with a port sending random messages: clean in every release from v0.228 to v0.260, also with the mouse moving over the window.

### Fixed (edit script `tools/release-gate/hf1_edit.py`, anchored, refuses a second run)
- **Control surfaces only when turned on.**
  - A surface profile (Push 1, Mackie Control, HUI, Launchpad/APC; every profile but the generic one, also ones added later) takes a port only after the user ticks **Control surface** for it on the Controllers page (`UI.ctlOn`), or picks it under Works as.
  - Until then the port is plain: its notes play, mappings work, nothing is sent to it, and a notice says once that it looks like a surface.
  - Mapping feedback goes only to ports turned on as surfaces (`ctlDevOf`).
- **Echoes ignored.**
  - Every message sent is remembered (`ctlEcho`, in `ctlSend` and the four goodbye senders), and the same message back within 50 ms is ignored (`ctlGuard` in `ctlMsg`).
  - Never dropped: note-offs (a stuck note otherwise), Mackie pitch-bend faders, HUI fader CCs.
- **Loops and floods stopped.**
  - A port whose messages are at least 24 a second and at least 60 % echoes of what was sent in the last second is stopped for the session with a notice (`d.halt='loop'`), and its profile says goodbye.
  - So is a port sending over 1500 a second.
  - Ticking Use this device again retries it.
- **Stop all controllers** (Controllers page, command `ctl.stopAll`):
  - nothing is read or sent, kept across restarts (`UI.ctlStop`)
  - MIDI does not even start at launch while it is on
- **The two `lkSel` functions** (v0.255, found by the scheduling chat): FT-F1's linked-clips helper is now `ftLinkSel` (2 callers); LK's `lkSel(a)` is the selection colour again everywhere.
- **`peakOf`** was declared twice with the same body; the second declaration is removed.
- **Duplicate element ids.** The lint finds none written twice in the HTML or in one piece of markup. The running app shows no duplicate ids in the start-up test or after opening every window (abUpd, dawRecol, ibPlane and master appear in different templates that are never in the page together).
- **The update window:**
  - the notes scroll in a fixed area (at most 640 px tall); the buttons sit under a hairline, always in view
  - "What is new" is one line per release, newest first, 8 shown and "and N earlier changes"
- The FT tests turn their fake devices on as surfaces (one line in each `F.plug`).

### The release gate (new): `tools/release-gate/gate.py`, `docs/release-gate.md`
It tests a fresh worktree of origin/main against the build installed apps have:
- a) lint, `lint.js` (acorn): a top-level function name declared twice, a function sharing a const's name, an id written twice
- b) every UI test, with failures re-run on the reference to tell regressions from old failures (`ui-skip.json` lists 8 non-pass/fail tools)
- c) `smoke_electron.js`, the real Electron app at 2194 × 1139 × 1.75 with the Fractals song (14 scenarios):
  - 60 s idle, then the mouse over the whole window
  - the MIDI scenarios (none; keyboard; Push 1 plain, echoing, turned on; IAC loop; the user's IAC ports; Mac names; Mackie echoing; IAC with old learned mappings; random messages)
  - fails on any state change, synthetic event, command, `changed()` call, console error, duplicate id, or a loop left running
  - frame times against the reference
- d) every main window opened and closed; the update window with 40 long lines at three sizes
- e) `export_same.py`: the Fractals levels and every export line against the reference

Only the gate promotes (`AL_PROMOTE=1 node desktop/scripts/sync-app.js`, notes trimmed to the ten newest).

### Tested
- `tools/ui-tests/taskHF1.py`: 19 of 19.
- FT tests C1a to C3c and F1 pass with the change (C3b 51 of 51 after the fader exception).
- `smoke_electron.js`:
  - the push1, push1-loop, mackie-loop and keyboard scenarios are clean
  - push1-loop-on and mackie-loop-on stop the looping device with no state change
  - iac-push is clean (nothing sent)

### What the user can do with v0.250 now
Switch the IAC Driver offline in Audio MIDI Setup, or rename its "Ableton Push to Cubase" port so it does not contain "Ableton Push". Either works until v0.261 is installed. With v0.261 the IAC port can stay on.

## 27 November 2026, v0.263: task IN-S, the spectrum: the analyzer front panel (lane E, instruments)

Step IN-S of `docs/design-round-4-instruments.md`, the user's pick **S2** (the analyzer front panel). Edit script `tools/design-lab/in/in_s.py` with `in_s_block.js` (every anchor asserted unique), test `tools/ui-tests/taskIN_S.py` (34 checks, all pass). Written on v0.261, re-applied by the edit script on v0.262 (lane A's DS-P1) and tested again there.

### Built (block "lane E (task IN-S)" before `askChoice`)
- **One drawer, `INS.spec`**, laid out as on the pick page (Keysight and Rohde & Schwarz style): IN-A's graticule 10 by 10 (centre axes with minor marks, the G3 levels and W1 hairlines from `LOOK`), the **reference level on the top line** with its dB/div (the range divided by ten: 10 dB/div in the Visualizer, the device's Top and Floor, 7.2 for the overlay's 72 dB), START and STOP frequency, LOG, **RBW** (the window's noise bandwidth: Web Audio's analyser uses a Blackman window, 1.73 bins, so 1.73 x rate / FFT size), **AVG** (the averaging time constant), **DET PEAK**, the tilt when there is one; **trace 1** live in yellow ("1 CLRW"), **trace 2** max hold in cyan ("2 MAXH", or "2 PK HOLD" when it falls); **marker 1** on the strongest peak and the **delta marker** on the next local maximum (at least 3 % of the width away), with MKR1 frequency, note and level in the header and ΔMKR2 Δf and ΔdB in the footer. Frequency marks inside the bottom line (decades long, 2 and 5 short, numbers at the decades). Three sizes: full (two footer rows), mid (one), mini (settings in the top corners). Numbers ink, units amber (L2), real minus signs; no em dashes.
- **The detector** is positive peak, as the device had: a pixel column takes the highest bin in its span, or the level between the two nearest bins where bins are wider than a pixel. **Averaging is by time** (a time constant, the same at 60 or 120 frames a second and at the Light level's half rate), including the analyser's own smoothing where a caller keeps one (`INS.avgOf`). The hold falls in dB per second.
- **Levels are now dBFS.** The analyser reads a sine 13.56 dB under its peak (the Blackman window's coherent gain 0.42, one side); `INS.SPCAL` adds it back so a sine reads its peak level, as on the pick page (measured: a 1 kHz sine at −18 dBFS read −31.8 dB before). **Marker read-outs** come from a parabola through the highest bin and its neighbours (in dB), so they are free of the window's scalloping (up to 1.1 dB): the same sine reads 999.97 Hz, −17.97 dBFS.
- **`INS.an`** sets an analyser's FFT size and smoothing in one place, only when they change: the Spectrum device's FFT choice, the overlay's and the Visualizer's analysers.
- **Spectrum device** (`ND('spec')`): draws through the drawer. Top is the reference level, Floor the bottom, Slope the tilt, Smoothing the averaging time (its old per-frame share at 60 frames a second, as a time constant), Peak fall the hold's fall (dB per frame at 60, as dB/s; 0 = max hold). The dots, presets, FFT sizes, Peak hold, Hold ref and Clear ref (the orange dashed reference) stay. Because of the calibration, a saved device shows its curve 13.6 dB higher against the same Top and Floor than before (the numbers are now true dBFS).
- **Analyser overlay**, spectrum module (`ANZD.spec`): through the drawer; its sources (each in its colour, the others' traces faint, their holds dashed), the colour modes, the range menu (60, 72, 96 dB, slow automatic) and the Peak button stay. Its steady top moved by the calibration (ANZTOP + 13.6, REF −10 dBFS), so the picture sits where it was. It now shows the peak detector (it averaged the bins' power before).
- **Visualizer spectrum** (`VZD.fft`): through the drawer, REF 0 dBFS, 10 dB/div, no tilt (as on the pick page); max hold falls 3 dB/s, none at the Light level. Its Light gate is now 40 ms against 20 (it was 33 against 20, which gave the same rate on a 60 Hz screen). IN-V lays it sideways next to the spectrogram later.
- **Mixer spec view:** a strip is too narrow for a front panel, so its bars, colour maps, mirror and caps stay; decade marks (100 Hz, 1 kHz, 10 kHz) on its right edge, with numbers when the strip is wide enough.
- **Not done:** the track taps stay at 256 samples (IN-M's note): every track's meters and stereo displays read them each frame, and the stereo displays read 512 samples whatever the size, so growing them belongs with IN-O. The overlay's analyser stays at 8192 at the Light level (its spectrogram module shares the buffer size).
- **Overlaps named:** NI-3 and NI-4 (lane D, the frequency map) keep their own per-beat analysis; idea I4, I5 and I13 views are untouched; MD1 (lane G) is in progress: the drawer uses `INS.parts` and `INS.note`, MD1 can swap in its formatter. No lane's code was changed besides lane E's.

- Drawer with a made-up analyser (peaks between bins): graticule 10 by 10; REF on the top line, −50 in the middle, −100 at the bottom; the front-panel text; RBW 9.31 Hz at 44.1 kHz and 8192; marker 1 1000.0 Hz −18.00 dBFS, delta 3000 Hz −30.00, read-out +2.00 kHz −12.0 dB; trace 1 yellow, trace 2 cyan, holding −18 after the tone stops; fall 10 dB/s for 0.2 s = 2.0 dB; averaging 0.1 s after a −60 to −18 step reads −33.37 (one time constant: −33.45); tilt 4.5 dB/oct: −18 at 2 kHz reads −13.50; silence draws nothing; three sizes, all text inside the box.

## 27 November 2026: task NB-R7 (the project's state and its edit protocol; review RN5 A10)

Fired by the scheduler. Next step after NB-R5 by its own "Left" list: NB-R6 waits for decision D2 (and its other parts were done in N3c), so NB-R7. Claimed in the running list first (commit 679e83c). No NB commit in the 20 minutes before. `index.html` and `desktop/` untouched.

### Built
- `docs/native-state-protocol.md`: the design. The document is the app's project `S` as JSON (no view, transport or audio samples). The page owns it until the end of stage 3, the engine from N4; one protocol for both. Edits are the difference between `S` and the copy last sent (`set`, `del`, `ins`, `rm`, each with the old value: its own undo, checked by the engine). `seq` and `base`, stale edits refused, one edit in flight and a queue per undo step, rebase when the engine changed first (the engine wins at the same place), the whole project again on a lost line, a refusal or a restart. Undo by step in the engine, 64 MB, whole steps dropped. A half-native song: one document, the engine decides where each track sounds. Saves: atomic, five older copies, `minReader`, hash. Costs, the messages, the four-place hook for N2c.
- `native/engine/doc/doc.h`: the engine's document (its own JSON reader and writer that round-trip any JS string, also unpaired surrogates, and any double; the operations, all-or-nothing edits, undo and redo by step, the structural hash, `saveAtomic`). `native/engine/doc/aldoc.cpp`: the commands `doc.load`, `doc.edit`, `doc.undo`, `doc.redo`, `doc.hash`, `doc.snapshot`, `doc.save`, `doc.open`, `doc.stats`, and `aldoc selftest` (22 checks). CMake target `aldoc`. They go into `alengine` when the bridge carries edits (N2c).
- `native/bridge/doc-sync.js`: the page's side (diff, apply, inverse, the same hash, `DocMirror` with commit, queue, replies, `remote` and rebase, timeout).
- `tools/native-lab/doc_sync_test.js` with the three built-in songs as the app holds them (`tools/native-lab/ref/doc/*.json.gz`, taken from v0.261 in headless Chromium).
- `native-ci.yml`: the selftest and the protocol test on every push (Release 1,000 steps, sanitizers 150 steps) and in the Mac job (300 steps).

### Proven
- Here (Linux, Release): `doc_sync_test.js --steps 1000` PASS on Fractals, the Psytrance demo and Shrine Legion: phase A (page owns, about 850 edits of 34 kinds and 100 snapshot undos per song: engine hash equal after every step), B (engine undo and redo: every undo exactly the state before its step, all undone = the song as loaded), C (200 overtaken edits: refused, rebased, equal), D (lost line, stale base, wrong old value, engine restart), E (saves, crash before rename, half file, one changed number, newer `minReader`), F (3,000 shuffled arrays). Under AddressSanitizer + UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, 1,000 steps per song with another seed (3): PASS, no report.
- GitHub push run 46052350883 (the first version): green on every job (linux with the new step: Release 1,000 steps and sanitizers 150, tsan, node, electron).
- Measured on Fractals (514 KB): edits median 176 bytes, 90 % under 1.3 KB; engine hash 2 ms; page compare of an unchanged project about 10 ms (Node 22); a save 23 ms with the flush to disk.
- Found by the first sanitizer run with 1,000 steps and fixed: the 64 MB history limit dropped single edits and could leave half an undo step (now whole steps, a selftest check, and the test accepts dropped steps); moving one track made the diff resend all tracks (now the longest in-order run stays and only the moved one travels: 0.7 KB instead of 1 MB).

### Left
- N2c: the hook in `index.html` (four places, section 10 of the design), the commands inside `alengine`, the cost in the real page; the hash check at idle and before saves.
- **The Mac got a machine** (native-ci run 46052838752, `macos-latest`: macOS 26.7.2, Apple clang 21, arm64), the first since NB-R1 (D9). `alengine` built and its selftest passed on Apple Silicon (follower flat to 20 kHz, the four clock offsets steered within 2 ppm, cost 15.7 us per block), the ring under two threads passed. `alrender`, `almix` and so `aldoc` (built after them) did not build: the vendored LLVM maths had only its Intel branches (`aarch64/nearest_integer.h` missing). Fixed in this run: 13 ARM files from the same LLVM commit (found by compiling for aarch64 here until nothing was missing), and the Mac job now builds with `-k` so one target cannot hide the others. Dispatched again: run 46054867320, **Mac job green**: all targets build for arm64; alengine selftest, the ring (also TSan), the mixer's 10 scenes ALL IDENTICAL on Apple Silicon, aldoc selftest and the protocol test (300 steps per song) PASS, bridge 55 of 55. ## 27 November 2026, v0.265: settings step S7, the changed mark, reset per setting and per page, Reset all with a list and a backup (task ST-S7)
Seventh step of the settings rebuild (`docs/settings-round-1.md`, S7, depends on D2 (picked: all three) and S4, both done: "Changed mark, reset per setting and per page, 'Reset all' that lists what it resets and saves a backup first"). Written on v0.261 (HF1); main had v0.262 (DS-P1, lane A), v0.263 (IN-S, lane E) and v0.264 (IN-E, lane E) when it was ready, so the edit script was run again on the fresh file and the version is 0.265. No other task had an open wip commit on index.html, and the last release was more than 3 minutes old when the work started and when it was pushed.

### Built
- **The changed mark**: every row whose value differs from how it came gets a thin blue bar on its left and a ↺ at its end (the prototype's design). The ↺'s tooltip names the default and the value now ("Back to the default: on (now off)"); a click puts that one setting back through its own control (so it is stored and applied exactly as a click would) and a short notice says so. Read from the settings table (`STT`): only rows with a default; never the glass chain's rows (Performance and the Glass block, rebuilt in G4) and never the block lists (layout picture, mixer, meters, shortcuts, which keep their own Reset buttons).
- **The count per page**: each page button in the sidebar shows how many of its settings differ from the default (a small blue number, hidden at 0).
- **Reset this page** in the page title row, with the count ("Reset this page (2)"); disabled when nothing differs, hidden on pages that have no resettable rows (Performance). It resets only that page; for 10 s it becomes "Undo the reset", which puts the page back as it was.
- **Reset all settings…** now asks with the full list: every changed setting with page, value now and the default it goes back to ("Editing › Pick up notes that are already sounding: off, back to on"), the options outside Settings that go back too (Metronome and count-in, Capture, Transport bar layout, Track controls, Mixer view, Visualizer, Map, Piano roll, Devices panel, Instrument browser, Keyboard piano, MIDI controllers and learned mappings, window sizes: only the groups that have a stored value) with the count of other remembered choices, and what is kept (projects and their files, keyboard shortcuts). The button says "Back up and reset". It saves a backup of every setting first, then resets as before (every stored setting except the shortcuts) and reloads. If the browser has no room for the backup it says so and offers "Save as a file" or "Reset without a backup".
- **Settings backup and restore** (new card on General): the last 3 backups on this computer (newest first, with the time, why it was made and the version), Back up now, Restore… (asks; backs up the current settings first, so a restore can be undone; reloads) and Save as a file… (a JSON file `AudioLab settings backup <date> <time>.json`, kind `audiolab-settings-backup`, the whole `UI` object; S18 builds export and import with tick boxes on the same format). Search finds it ("backup", "restore").
- Marks are redrawn after any change inside the Settings window and once a second while it is open (so a change made on the master strip or elsewhere shows too); nothing runs while Settings is closed; nothing per frame.
- Code: block `STS7` "v0.265 (task ST-S7)" before `askChoice` (`ST7`: `mark`, `one`, `page`, `backup`, `backups`, `restore`, `file`, `plan`, `fill`, `all`, `build`), CSS before `.dacv`; the Reset all button's handler is replaced (same reset, now with the list and the backup); edit script `tools/edits/taskST_S7.py` with `taskST_S7_block.js` and `taskST_S7_css.txt`, every replacement asserted unique. - `native/engine/mix/albus.cpp` (CMake target `albus`): renders a scene file (JSON) as `make_bus_ref.py` writes it, `--order bus=...` to try Chromium's orders.
- `tools/native-lab/make_bus_ref.py`: 14 scenes built in the real app page the way `renderMix` routes them (devices by `mkFx`/`mkFxNode` with presets, their posted settings recorded, delay compensation from the app's own `fxLat`, muted and soloed tracks left out as `trkAudible` does), each rendered twice; references in `tools/native-lab/ref/bus/` (3.6 MB).
- `tools/native-lab/run_bus.py`: compares every sample; where a bus has three or more inputs and the scene differs, it tries that bus's orders.
- `native-ci.yml`: the bus comparison in the Linux job (Release and sanitizers); in the Mac job, Chromium is installed on the Mac and the Mac's own references are made for the 240 device cases and the 14 bus scenes (review D3), then compared.

### Proven
- Linux, Release and ASan+UBSan: **14 of 14 scenes bit for bit** (group2, groupfx, nested, send, send2, master, pdc, pdcgrp, mute, solo, mutedgroup, song, song128, wide). `wide` has every ported device on the buses at once.
- Chromium's DelayNode at a whole number of samples is an exact copy (probe at 1, 7, 96, 240, 2,048 samples, 128 and 512 frames), so delay compensation ports as a plain delay.
- The web engine differs from itself between two renders in 4 of 14 scenes (three or more inputs into the master; up to 26,328 samples, about -140 dB); one summing order reproduces each web render exactly.
- Cost: `wide` (10 devices, 7 nodes) 19 times real time on one core of this build machine, `song` 38 times.

### Left
- **Mac, run 46056395016:** the 240 device cases bit for bit against Chromium on Apple Silicon (first time). The buses differed by about -138 dB from the second quantum: Chromium's arm64 build fuses `a + b * g` in StereoPannerNode (contraction on; JavaScript devices unaffected). Fixed in `al_mix.h` (`AL_WEB_PAN_FUSED`, on for arm64, both pan paths; Linux unchanged and still 14 of 14 and N3b's 10 of 10 here). The CI gate `grep -q 'ALL IDENTICAL'` also matched 'NOT ALL IDENTICAL' (since N3b); now `grep -qx`. Rerun 46058415128 (Mac job also makes the Mac's own references for N3b's scenes): its result is read by the next run if not added here.
- Clips as sources (the export's clip chain), moving values (automation, live smoothing), the Ducker's keys, the export's output limiter, other sample rates; then the remaining devices (FFT family, delays, voice, ducker, loudness) and the instruments.
- NB-R8 when the test-app task is not working in `native/host/`; NB-R9 needs `index.html`.

### Assumptions
- The native engine sums each bus in the order the export connects it (project order), which makes its renders repeatable; the web engine's own order is not repeatable, so "the same as the export" means "the same as one of the export's renders".
- Mac references come from the Mac's Chromium (D3's direction), not Linux's; the Linux references are compared on the Mac too, for information.

## 27 November 2026, v0.269: task NI-6, the energy arc (lane D, idea I6)

Idea I6 is complete. Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ni/ni_6.py` (anchored; needs NI-3, NI-4 and NI-5b), test `tools/ui-tests/taskNI_6.py` (33 checks, all pass). The step was claimed in the plan before it started.

### Built
- **A lane under the section row** (under the tempo lane when that shows), 40 px, **off by default**. Switch: "Show the energy arc" in the section row's right-click menu (and the time signature menu, which shares the tempo lane's item), the command `ni.energyArc`. A UI setting (`UI.niArc`), not stored in the project; three rows in `NI_SETTINGS` (S4 shape) for lane B.
- **What it shows**, per beat, from NI-3's cache of every track (no live analysis, nothing in the audio path), each smoothed over 4 beats:
  - loudness: the tracks' K-weighted power added up, in LUFS (tracks are measured one at a time, so correlation between tracks is not counted)
  - tracks playing: how many of the song's tracks sound, as a share
  - brightness: the spectral centroid of all tracks together, in Hz
  - energy = 55% loudness (-36 to -6 LUFS) + 25% tracks playing + 20% brightness (150 Hz to 6 kHz, log). A fixed scale, so a quiet mix sits low in the lane.
- **The look**: the energy line in ink over a magma fill (brighter is more energy), section starts as hairlines, beats not yet measured hatched, "measuring 56%" top right while it fills. **Pointing** at it draws the three ingredients apart (cyan loudness, violet tracks, amber brightness) and a read-out: bar and beat, energy, LUFS, "4 of 4 tracks play", brightness, the comparison's value. "Always show the three ingredients" keeps them. Tooltip on the lane and its label (what energy is made of).
- **Comparison** (dashed, drawn within the song's own range, 5th to 95th percentile, so the shape compares, not the height): a typical psytrance arc. When every section has a name it knows (intro, build, drop, break, outro, verse and similar), the arc follows the sections (drop 0.95, break 0.4, build rising 0.45 to 0.85); otherwise a generic arc over the song length (intro, build, drop, break, build, second drop, outro). A reference's arc when another lane gives one: `NI.arc.setRef({name, at(fraction, beat)})`, for lane C's FT-F25a reference slots (the chip is off until then, with a tooltip saying why).
- **Click** in the lane moves the playhead (nothing selected); **right-click**: compare with (chips), always show the ingredients, hide.
- **Snappy**: drawn only inside the arrangement's normal redraw; the numbers are worked out once per change of the analysis (throttled to 0.7 s while it fills). No timer. The measuring starts 0.3 s after the lane shows, again 1.2 s after an edit settles (only what changed: one track's edit measures that track's pieces), and is cancelled when the lane is hidden (unless the frequency map or the clashes are using it). A measuring cancelled by another view is picked up again, three times at most.
- **Lane A's code**: the new CLAUDE.md gives the arrangement drawing and tempo to lane A. This step adds three one-line touches there, none changing what they did: `TMPH()` adds `NI_arcH()` (so every place that offsets the tracks by the tempo lane also makes room for the arc), `tmpGeo()` keeps the tempo lane's own 44 px, and `drawArr` calls `NI_arcDraw(g, w)` after the tempo lane. No other lane changed these lines (checked with `git log -S`). Lane A: please keep the three calls when rebuilding the arrangement.

### Checked
- Test song (audio, 120 BPM, 16 bars; sections Intro, Drop, Break, Drop 2): Pad 500 Hz throughout, Kick 55 Hz, Bass 110 Hz, Hat 8 kHz in the drops only. Energy: intro 0.26, drop 0.70, **break 0.26**, drop 2 0.70. Tracks playing 4 of 4 and 1 of 4. Loudness of a pad-only beat equals the Pad's own NI-3 loudness (-28.65 LUFS), of a drop beat the four tracks' power sum (-13.33), both within 0.05 dB; brightness of the break 508 Hz (pad at 500). Typical arc from the names: break 0.40, drop 0.95, intro rising; one unknown name gives the generic arc.
- Pointing at beat 40 redraws with the read-out and the cyan line; moving away removes them and the tooltip; a click puts the playhead on beat 24 and leaves the selection; the menu switches the comparison (Nothing, typical, a stub reference through `setRef`, back to typical when it is taken away).

- **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`, measured on this build and on main v0.261): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; -9.75669 (0496bb147f6c) and -25.48699 dB (09e0415bec5e) at 0 dB. ## 27 November 2026: task NB-N3e (the Pro EQ: Chromium's BiquadFilterNode, the first device made of browser nodes)

Fired by the scheduler. The next stage not done after N3d: the rest of stage 3's devices. Chosen by what the built-in song needs: Fractals uses the Pro EQ 35 times (33 tracks), the compressor 4, the sidechain pump 4, the tempo delay 5, the plate reverb 1 and a clipper on the master, none of them worklets; the EQ first. `index.html`, `desktop/` (also `desktop/app-version.json`) untouched; no version. A second NB run had meanwhile committed an N3d follow-up on the panner (2e165ad, b2f67da); this run rebased on it and merged the two (below).

### Built
- `native/engine/core/biquad.h`: Chromium 158.0.8127.36's BiquadFilterNode (biquad.cc, biquad_filter_handler.cc; identical on main): float AudioParams, `pow10` via `fdlibm::expf`, all eight types, coefficients at the first quantum and on change, the Linux loop (double state fed back through float) and the Mac path (`vDSP_deq22D`, 1,024-frame slices), `getFrequencyResponse` with libc++'s complex arithmetic written out.
- `native/third_party/fdlibm/`: Chromium's fdlibm (SunPro licence; only `base/` includes replaced). CMake library `al_fdlibm` (links Accelerate on the Mac), used by `alrender*`, `albus`, `almix`.
- `native/engine/core/dev_eq.h`: the Pro EQ as `mkEQ2` builds it (stages, tilt, solo, idle bands kept out until used, mid/side, auto gain, out gain). Registered as `eq`.
- `device.h`: `Processor::worklet()` (browser-node devices skip the worklet rules), `NodeFloatState` (denormals flushed, as Chromium's audio thread), mono in and out per call; `graph.h`, `bus_graph.h`: a chain keeps a mono input mono through browser-node devices.
- `al_mix.h` (merged with the other run's fix): the panner's fused form is the Mac's `vDSP_vsma` (Chromium is built with `-ffp-contract=off` everywhere, BUILD.gn; `Vsma` is `vDSP_vsma` in vector_math_mac.h), so `AL_WEB_PAN_FUSED` defaults on for the Mac only and calls `vDSP_vsma` there; the first quantum's double path unfused (`AL_WEB_PAN_SA_FUSED` switch kept); pan gains from fdlibm as stereo_panner.cc.
- `make_ref_core.py`: the EQ's 47 cases (17 settings that reach every branch, all 29 distinct EQ settings of Fractals from `ref/eq_fractals.json`) and two chains with worklet devices; chains may name an extra setting. `make_bus_ref.py`: settings merged into a device (`("eq", None, {...})`), scenes `eqbus`, `eqbus128`, and a scene filter that keeps the others' entries. CI: the Mac's device gate counts every case.

### Proven (Linux, this machine)
- Devices: **289 of 289 bit for bit** at 128 frames per call; 288 of 289 at 7, 64 and 512 (the known two-random-device chain, review A2). Under ASan+UBSan at 7 frames: the 47 EQ cases bit for bit.
- Buses: **16 of 16 identical** (with `eqbus`, `eqbus128`: EQ on a mono source, mid/side on a group and on a mono source, tilt with auto gain on a return, an EQ before the master's limiter); N3b's mixer 10 of 10 (with the fdlibm pan gains).
- Found by measurement: Chromium's own nodes run with denormals flushed (without it only the samples under 1.2e-38 differed); a GainNode at exactly 1 copies.
- Cost: four active bells 7.9 µs per 128 stereo frames; 48 dB/oct passes 14.6 µs; Fractals' EQs 0.3 to 3.8 µs.
- **Apple Silicon** (native-ci with the Mac job, against the Mac's own Chromium; the whole run 46062616472 green, Linux too with the sanitizers at 128 and 7 frames): run 46060870529: buses 16 of 16, N3b's mixer 10 of 10 with the Mac's references (vDSP_vsma and vDSP_deq22D right), devices 288 of 289: `eq-x-ms` gave +0 where Chromium gave -0. Chromium's `AudioChannel::SumFrom` copies the first connection into the silent summing bus and adds the rest; the port started from 0 (0 + -0 + -0 = +0). Fixed in the EQ and in the buses' inputs (3ce1a8c). Run 46062616472: **289 of 289, 16 of 16, 10 of 10 on Apple Silicon**, strict gates (the Mac job now prints the cases that differ).

### Left
- A connection flagged silent is skipped by Chromium's summing (a GainNode at 0, a finished source): not modelled yet; it matters with clips as sources.
- The EQ's dynamic bands (live only) and automation; a biquad's tail after silence (with clips as sources).
- Next devices for Fractals: compressor (DynamicsCompressor), sidechain pump, tempo delay, plate reverb (convolver: measured), clipper; then clips as sources and the instruments.

### Assumptions
- `UI.eqAll` (an interface option that keeps idle bands in the path) is off, its default; the port reads only the device's settings.
- An unknown band type keeps the filter's previous type, as the browser does.
- Chromium 158.0.8127.36's source stands for the Electron the app ships (Chromium 156) for these files; the comparison is against headless Chromium 158 here and the Mac's Playwright Chromium in CI.

## 27 November 2026, v0.273: task XT-DL2, the commands registry (extensions and the Workshop, lane H, second step)
Row DL2 of docs/extensions-plan.md 9.7 (part c of 9.6). Invisible groundwork: nothing looks or behaves differently, no shortcut changes.

### What was built
- **Every action has one namespaced command id** (71): the 68 rows of the shortcut list `SCA` plus three buttons without a shortcut row (`transport.countIn`, `transport.tapTempo`, `transport.capture`, kept out of the Settings list in `XT_CMD_EXTRA`). Sections: transport, project, edit, clip, track, view, help, ctl, ni, arr. (`mg.native` of task MG1 exists only in the desktop app and is noted, not listed.) List: `docs/commands.md`.
- `SCA` itself is unchanged: its old ids stay the keys of `UI.keys`, the key presets (`SCPRE`) and `SCM`, so nobody's keys change and every existing caller (`SCM.get('play').run()` in the controller code) keeps working. `XT_CMD_NS` gives each old id its namespaced id; the ids lanes A, C and D already namespaced (`ctl.*`, `ni.*`, `clip.linkedDup`, `clip.unique`, `arr.*`) are adopted as they are.
- `COMMAND_ALIAS`: old id (and later retired ids) to the namespaced id; `xtCommandId(any id)` resolves namespaced, old and retired ids.
- `xtCommands()`: the registry, a Map of `{id, name, group, defaultKey, key (the user's current key), legacy (old id), gesture, when, run}`. Built on first use and again only when `SCA` grows (rows other lanes push later join by themselves). With nothing asking for it, it is never built.
- `runCommand(id, source)`: the one door for macros (DL8), toolbars, scripts (DL13) and the Assistant (DL15). ## 27 November 2026, v0.276: task IN-G, the dynamics displays: gain reduction history, transfer curve, per-band bars (lane E, instruments)

Step IN-G of `docs/design-round-4-instruments.md`, the user's picks **G1** (gain reduction history), **G3** (transfer curve with a live point) and **G4** (per-band gain reduction). Edit script `tools/design-lab/in/in_g.py` with `in_g_block.js` (every anchor asserted unique), test `tools/ui-tests/taskIN_G.py` (31 checks, all pass), draw cost `tools/design-lab/in/draw_cost_g.py`. Written on v0.266, re-applied by the edit script on v0.273 and tested again there.

### Built (block "lane E (task IN-G)" before `askChoice`)
- **G1, one drawer `INS.grh`** (FabFilter Pro-L style, as on the pick page): 4 s of history, the input as a grey area, the output as a blue line (`#4c8dff`), the gain reduction in red hanging from the top **on the same dB scale** (1 dB down is 1 dB), the level scale (dBFS) on the left and the GR scale on the right in the GR colour, the GR now as a big number with its amber unit (small capitals, MD1's M1) and the most in the last 4 s under it, a small IN OUT GR legend. One point per device pixel column (highest input and output, deepest reduction), so a narrow display does not draw hundreds of points.
  - **Compressor** (`vizComp`, now one call to `ingComp`): its history beside the curve, scale 0 to −30 dBFS (deeper when the threshold is lower), the threshold as an amber line. The output is the input plus the reduction plus **Chromium's own make-up** (the DynamicsCompressor adds 0.6 x the reduction at 0 dBFS; measured: the drawn output is within 0.33 dB of the real one) plus Make-up. In the device panel the history is a narrow strip, so the numbers sit in the curve's empty top-left corner there.
  - **Limiter**: on its own −30 to +3 dB scale (the ceiling handle and the input and release dots keep their places), dB scales on both sides, the numbers in the right margin; the GR and OUT bars without numbers are gone (G1 replaces them). Its history already held 5.5 s.
  - **Gate**: on its −80 to 0 dB scale; the green open shading, the open and close lines, the OPEN mark and the envelope panel stay. The output is the level plus the gate's gain.
  - **Ducker** (`abxPaint`, also the Auto gain display while live): the trigger stays a filled area in its track's colour; the reduction is now in dB in red on the trigger's 60 dB scale (it was the linear gain as a line), with the GR scale on the right and the 4 s maximum under the existing read-out.
- **G3, the compressor's transfer curve, calibrated:** −60 to 0 dBFS both ways, a line every 6 dB, labels every 12 with real minus signs, IN dBFS, the 1:1 line dashed, the threshold dashed red. **The curve is the one Chromium's compressor really computes** (`ingCK`, `ingRed`, a port of DynamicsCompressorKernel: an exponential knee in linear amplitude starting at the threshold, its constant found so the slope at threshold + 6 dB is 1/ratio, then the ratio; the old drawing had no knee). The signal rides it as a white dot at the input's peak (the compressor's detector reads the peak; measured) and the reduction the compressor reports, with a 30-point trail (none at the Light level) and an **amber caliper** to the 1:1 line with the reduction's number. The curve is computed once per setting.
- **G4, `ingBar`**: a bar per band falling from the top on the studio scale 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 20, 30 dB (square-root spacing: the first dB gets 18 % of the bar), falling 25 dB/s with a white tick held 2 s (`INS.peak` from IN-A), the number under it, the band's edges:
  - **OTT**: each band's level block stays (narrower) with its bar beside it, the edges "< 120 Hz", "120 Hz to 2.5 kHz", "> 2.5 kHz" (the fixed crossovers);
  - **Multiband Dynamics**: the right-hand GR meter (a linear 18 dB bar) becomes three G4 bars with the edges from its crossovers ("<150", "150-3k", ">3k"), or mid and side;
  - **De-Esser**: the reduction panel becomes the history on the same scale with a G4 bar, and the band's real edges (the worklet's band-pass: Q 1.5 at 6.5 kHz is 4.7 to 9.0 kHz).
- **Display history kept 4 s:** the gate's, the de-esser's and the ducker's message lists keep 400 messages of 512 samples instead of 200 (display arrays only; the ducker's ring is in the AB code, a one-number change).
- **Not changed:** the audio path (no node made or connected; the values are the reductions and worklet messages the devices already post); the hit tests and handles; the Transient Shaper (not in the picks). The compressor's GR bar beside the curve stays as it was.

## 27 November 2026, v0.277: step sequencer clips, part 1 (task FT-F9a, lane C)
Step FT-F9a of `docs/features-build.md` (starred card F9 of `docs/research-features-gap.md`, section 4 "RF-F9 Step sequencer clips"). Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ft/ftF9a.py` with `ftF9a_block.js` (two asserted anchors: the end of FT-F2's block and the `dup` entry of `SCA`), test `tools/ui-tests/taskFT_F9a.py` (44 checks).

### Built
- **The clip**: a MIDI clip can carry `clip.steps` (optional, `v:1`; older songs have none): 16, 32 or 64 steps of 1/8, 1/16 or 1/32 over rows that are the drum kit's 16 pads (named and coloured as the pads) or 8 notes of the key (the piano roll's key and scale, A minor when none is set; `FT_HOOKS.projectKey` from FT-F11 is used when it exists), with octave up and down and Follow key. Each step has a **level**, **accent** (+25 % level), **slide** (the note holds into the next step, marked `sl` for F9b's Acid and Psy Bass glide), **chance** and **ratchet** (1 to 4 hits in the step).
- **It writes ordinary notes**: the pattern is written into the clip's notes, repeated over the clip's length (a clip made longer keeps repeating it). Playback, export, bounce, freeze, linked copies (they share the pattern too: `steps` joined `LK.MIDI`) and older AudioLab versions all play plain notes, so a step clip renders bit-identical to a plain clip with the same notes. Only **chance** is decided while playing: a note with `ch` < 1 plays with that chance each time (one roll for all hits of a ratcheted step); this is one wrapper on `ccSus`, which every playing path already uses, and it returns the very same array for every clip without steps, so nothing else changes.
- **The editor**: a window of its own (double-click a step clip, clip menu **Edit steps…**, command `clip.editSteps`): a grid (click a step to turn it on or off, drag to paint, one undo step per click or drag), and under it the selected row's five lanes (Level and Chance bars to drag, Accent and Slide dots to click, Ratchet to click through 1 to 4 or drag); Steps, Step size, Rows (Drum pads or Notes in key), Oct − and Oct +, Follow key, Clear row, Piano roll. The step that plays is lit while the song plays (drawn at most 30 times a second, only while the editor is open and playing; a 4 Hz check while it is open, nothing when closed). Tooltips on every control and on the grid, no em dashes; Esc closes; the title bar moves it.
- **Making one**: track menu **Add step sequencer clip here** on instrument tracks (a one-bar, 16-step clip: drum pads on a drum kit, notes in key on other instruments) and the command `clip.newSteps` (on the selected instrument track at the playhead).
- **Piano roll**: Open in piano roll from the clip menu still opens the notes there. If they were changed, the step editor says so ("Editing a step here writes the pattern again and replaces those changes") and offers **Use the steps**.
- Hooks: `FT_HOOKS.stepClip(clip)` gives `{n, res, mode, edited}` or null, for lane A to mark step clips in the arrangement (a small step badge beside the name; this step does not touch clip drawing); `FT_HOOKS.stepEditor` = `{open(clipId), close(), paint(), add(trackId, beat), gen(clipId)}` for Push 1's step lane (F9b) and DL2. No settings rows.

### Tested (`tools/ui-tests/taskFT_F9a.py`, headless Chromium, 44 checks, all pass)
- Fractals has no step clips and every ordinary clip gets the same notes array back from the chance step. Track menu entry with tooltip; a new clip on a drum kit: 16 steps of 1/16 over the 16 pads, one bar, the editor opens; the real mouse: four kicks on 1, 5, 9, 13 write four notes (one undo step each), a drag paints 8 steps in one undo step, undo is followed by the open editor; in the lanes accent (full level), ratchet 2 (two hits, 1/32 apart), chance and level. Chance over 2000 rolls plays about as often as set, both ratchet hits always together, steps without chance always. On a Saw: 8 notes of A minor from A3 (command `clip.newSteps`), five steps and a slide; **the step clip renders bit-identical to a plain clip with the same notes**. 32 steps (2 bars, pattern repeated), 1/8 steps, a longer clip, Oct +, a piano roll edit and Use the steps, double-click opens the step editor, the clip menu's two entries (Open in piano roll still works), a linked copy follows, saved with the song, no animation frame unless playing, tooltips on every control, no console errors.
- Screenshots looked at: the drum editor (pad colours, lanes with accent, ratchet 2, a lower chance bar), the key editor (root rows in amber, the slide arrow), playing, and with the Light glass level.
- Also: `taskFT_F2.py` 50/50, `taskFT_F1.py` 29/29, `taskFT_C2b.py`, `taskAI.py`; start-up smoke test (`tools/release-gate/smoke_electron.js`, 14 of 14 MIDI scenarios clean at 30 s each, run on this step before the last rebase onto v0.276; after the rebase the lint and this step's test again); **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB.

### Only the user can test
- Right-click an instrument track's lane, Add step sequencer clip here (on a Drum kit you get its pads), click steps and press play; under the grid set an accent, a ratchet and a chance below 100 % and hear the step come and go. On a synth the rows are notes of the piano roll's key.

## 27 November 2026: task NB-N1c (the deepest integer format on the wire)

Fired by the scheduler with a chain-check note (read as data) pointing at the user's reports 6 and 7: the iFi Gryphon ran at 16-bit integer on the wire. N3e had just finished in this session, so this run took that report fix (stage N1's "the real format", the plan's N8 kind of work) before the next device family. `index.html`, `desktop/`, `native/host/` and `native/testapp/` (task NL7) untouched.

### Built
- `native/common/coreaudio.cpp` / `.h`: `deepestIntegerBits(dev, rate, mixable)` and `setIntegerFormat(...)`: integer formats only, rate ranges accepted (the older `setPhysicalFormat` matches bits alone and could pick float at 32 bits; kept as it was for the test app).
- `native/common/nulldevice.cpp`: the same two on the null device, which now also offers 16- and 24-bit integer formats the system mixes (as the Gryphon); setting one posts a format change, as the HAL would.
- `native/engine/engine_main.cpp`: `open` takes `"bits":"deepest"` (or `"deepest":true`), with or without `"integer":true`; the choice is kept and applied again by the format worker after a rate change from outside (event `deepest`); status `deepestIntegerBits`, `keepsDeepest`.
- `tools/native-lab/engine_deepest_test.py` (7 checks). `native-ci.yml`: runs it in Release, ASan+UBSan and TSan; the null-device steps use `pipefail`, so a failed check fails the job (it did not before).

### Proven
- Linux, this machine: 7 of 7 in Release, ASan+UBSan and TSan; `engine_null_test.py` 52 of 52.
- GitHub, native-ci run 46065297072: the Mac job green (the Core Audio side of `deepestIntegerBits` and `setIntegerFormat` compiles on Apple Silicon, and every earlier check still passes there, devices 289 of 289); Linux's null-device step with the new test (Release, ASan+UBSan) and the TSan job green.

### Left
- The Gryphon itself: its integer depths per rate and whether macOS keeps the format: only the user's Mac (test app 0.7's [format] line and its "Use the deepest format" menu, task NL7).
- The setting and the warning in the app: N2c.

### Assumptions
- The engine changes the DAC's format only when asked (`"bits":"deepest"`); a plain `open` leaves the device as it is, since the format is a system-wide setting other apps share. The settings page will offer it (on by default is a decision for N2c's pick page).
- "Deepest" means most bits among integer formats at the current rate, in the mixing mode asked; float formats are not considered, because the DAC receives integers.

Keys inside the open menu are taken before the app's shortcuts (before, Home ran Go to start and letters such as M could run their shortcut while a menu was open). ## 27 November 2026, v0.279: task NI-7, the level journey (lane D, idea I13)

Idea I13 is complete. Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ni/ni_7.py` (anchored; needs NI-6), test `tools/ui-tests/taskNI_7.py` (24 checks, all pass). The step was claimed in the plan before it started. (This run's trigger still named NI-5b as the last release; the plan's rule is the next step not yet logged, so this run did NI-7.)

### Built
- **A window "Level journey"** (the app's floating window: moves, resizes, remembers its place), from the main menu (right-click the logo: Level journey…) and the command `ni.levelJourney`. For the selected track, one row per step, top to bottom:
  - the clips (audio) or the instrument
  - each device (a switched-off device is shown struck through and "off", not measured)
  - the fader and pan
  - "Into Master" or "Into <group>"
- **Each row**: a level bar on a dBFS scale (-60 to +6, a graticule every 6 dB, 0 dBFS marked) in the track's colour, RMS as the bar and the peak as a tick, the level and the peak in dB, and the change from the step before. The biggest rise (amber ▲) and the biggest drop (cyan ▼) of 3 dB or more are marked; a peak above 0 dBFS is shown in amber with a tooltip.
- **How it is measured**: its own offline render of that one track, with the same steps as the app's one-track render (clips with their gain and fades, the instrument, the devices, the fader with its automation, pan, Vector Map). Every step's output also goes to its own pair of output channels, so **nothing is added to the live path or to exports**. Up to 15 steps per render, more in further renders. Over the loop when it is on, otherwise the 8 bars around the playhead (at most 16 bars), with up to 2 bars of pre-roll so tails are in it.
- **It follows** the selected track ("Follow the selection", on by default). It measures again 0.8 s after an edit or a move of the playhead settles, only while the song is stopped. A 300 ms check runs only while the window is open, and does work only when the track, the range or the project changed. Closing stops it.
- Groups and returns are not measured (their sound comes from other tracks; the window says so). The master chain, sends and sidechains are not in it (said under the rows).
- `NI_HOOKS.levelJourney` (`open(id)`, `measure(id, b0, b1)`) for a button on a mixer strip or the device frame (lanes A, I).

### Checked
- **Test song** (audio, 120 BPM): Tone, a 0.25 sine at 1 kHz, with a Pro EQ at Output +6 dB, a switched-off Pro EQ and its fader at 0.5.
  - Clips -15.05 dB RMS, -12.04 dB peak.
  - Pro EQ **+6.00 dB** (marked as the biggest rise); the switched-off EQ shown as off with no change.
  - Fader **-6.02 dB** (marked as the biggest drop); Into Master equal to the fader's level.
  - Range bars 3 to 10 at beat 24; the loop (beats 32 to 48) when it is on.
- **Selection and edits**:
  - selecting Other measures it (Clips, Fader and pan, Into Bus)
  - selecting the group says to pick one of its tracks
  - an EQ edit to +3 dB is not measured for 0.4 s, then shows +3.00
  - with Follow off another selection keeps Tone
  - idle for 2 s: nothing measured
- **Final rebase** onto v0.278 (lane C's step sequencer clips, lane F's right-click menus OV2a): the edit script re-run, lint clean, `taskNI_7.py` 24 of 24 again; the gate was not run a third time on this last file, main moved faster than one gate run.
- **Live path and exports**: a render of Tone is bit-identical before and after the journey measured it. **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py` on this build after the rebase onto v0.271, and the gate's export step again on the final v0.277 file): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; -9.75669 (0496bb147f6c) and -25.48699 dB (09e0415bec5e) at 0 dB.
- **Also**: `taskNI_6.py` 33 of 33. After the rebase onto v0.276 (lane E's dynamics displays, lane B's S8, lane I's device frame DV-1, lane H's commands registry) the edit script re-run: `taskNI_7.py` 24 of 24, `taskNI_6.py` 33 of 33 again, and the release gate on that working copy (`gate.py --here --skip-ui --quick`, never promotes) passes every step it ran: lint; the start-up smoke test (14 scenarios, every one clean); frame times idle with Fractals (p50 16.7 ms, p95 50.0 ms, as the reference); windows (19 checks); Fractals levels and exports (the 9 repeatable lines bit-identical to v0.250). Tooltips on every control, step and column; no em dashes; no console errors.
- **Screenshots looked at**: the test song, and the Fractals Kick (normal and Light level). The Kick reads instrument -16.1 dB, Pro EQ +4.3 dB with its peak at +3.2 dBFS (amber), fader -1.9 dB, into the Kick & Bass group.

### Limits and what only the user can judge
- RMS over the whole range treats quiet gaps as part of the level, so a sparse part reads lower than it sounds. The peak is the sample peak (no oversampling).
- What to try: select a bass or a lead in a drop, open Level journey and look for a device that adds or takes away a lot. On the Fractals Kick the Pro EQ adds 4.3 dB and peaks at +3.2 dBFS inside the track, which the master's -10 dB hides.
