## 27 November 2026, v0.281: task SND-0, the shared DSP kit (built-in sounds, lane L, first step)

The user's AE4 picks (27 Nov, 21:13 Brussels): everything, B1 to B37 and N1 to N6. Plan: `docs/sounds-build.md` (from section 7 of `docs/research-built-in-sounds.md`). This step builds the shared pieces the later steps use (N5's filter set, the oversampling and ADAA for B12, B19, B28, B36 and N2). **No device uses the kit yet: no sound changes.**

### Built
- `sndKitCore()` in `index.html` (before `askChoice`): one plain-arithmetic core. `wlLoad` appends `sndWL()` to the worklet module, so every processor can use it as `SNDK`; on the main thread `sndKitCore()` gives the same object for tests and offline work. `SND_HOOKS` (empty for now, `kit:1`) is where other lanes will find lane L's hooks.
- Blocks: `Smooth` (one-pole, time constant in ms, snaps to the target) and `Ramp` (linear, lands exactly) for parameters; `OnePole` (TPT lp, hp, ap); `Svf` (TPT, 7 outputs: lp, unity band-pass, hp, notch, peak, all-pass, band-pass); `Ladder` (4-pole Moog, TPT cascade with the feedback solved, res 1 = self-oscillation at the cutoff, outputs 1 to 4 poles; driven mode: tanh(d x)/d on the solved input and every stage input); `Diode` (the linearised equal-capacitor diode ladder as a state-space system solved by the trapezoidal rule, cutoff = the resonance pitch, self-oscillation at k = 901/49, w = sqrt(10/7); driven mode: the solved input saturated); `SallenKey` (MS-20 style 2-pole, LP 1/(s^2+(2-k)s+1), driven mode saturates the feedback); `Comb` (feedback with a damping one-pole or feed-forward, fractional delay by 4-point Hermite); `Formant` (five unity band-passes per vowel, a e i o u morph, Csound bass-voice table, a shift factor); `Adaa` (first-order antiderivative antialiasing for tanh, hard clip and a triangle fold, half a sample of delay); `Os2`, `Os4` (polyphase IIR halfbands, 12 coefficients for the steep 2x stage, 6 for the 4x stage); `Shaper` (any shaper at 1x, 2x or 4x with or without ADAA); `make(name, params, sr)`, one factory for the tests and the probe processor `al-snd-kit` (tests only; no device creates it).
- Licences: everything is my own implementation from the papers (Zavalishin's VA filter book, Huovilainen DAFx-04, Parker/Zavalishin/Le Bivic DAFx-16, Bilbao et al. 2017, Valenzuela and Constantinides 1983). The halfband design formulas follow HIIR by Laurent de Soras (WTFPL); no HIIR code was copied; `tools/engine-lab/snd/halfband_design.py` computes and checks the coefficients. The formant table is the Csound manual's data.

### Measured (`tools/engine-lab/snd/kit_test.py`, 43 of 43; numbers in `tools/engine-lab/snd/results_snd0.json`)
- Filters against their analog prototypes through the prewarped bilinear transform (5 cutoffs from 50 Hz to 20 kHz, 3 Q or resonance settings): SVF (all 7 outputs), one-pole, ladder, diode ladder and Sallen-Key all within 1e-10 dB. Driven modes equal the linear filter for quiet signals (under 0.0001 dB), stay bounded with full-scale noise at res 1.1 and drive 4, self-oscillate at 1000.0 Hz for a 1000 Hz cutoff. Resonance peak for a 2000 Hz cutoff at res 0.995: ladder 1997.5, diode 1996.4, Sallen-Key 1999.9 Hz.
- Halfbands: 2x and 4x round trip flat to 20 kHz at 44.1 kHz (under 1e-11 dB); images of a 15 kHz tone -131.0 dB (2x) and -118.7 dB (4x); a 30 kHz tone at the high rate -141.7 dB after down-sampling.
- Aliasing of a 4.5 kHz sine at drive 4 at 48 kHz (dB against the harmonics), plain / ADAA: tanh 1x -40.8 / -49.8, 2x -103.4 / -117.5, 4x -147.1 / -147.1; hard clip 1x -31.5 / -40.5, 2x -43.3 / -62.6, 4x -54.5 / -78.3; triangle fold 1x -20.5 / -29.3, 2x -32.4 / -51.6, 4x -43.6 / -67.3.
- Cost (Node, one block, ns per sample at 48 kHz; 1000 ns per sample is about 4.8 % of a core): SVF 27, ladder 62 (driven 236), diode 33 (driven 90), Sallen-Key driven 86, comb 28, formant 45, tanh ADAA 104 (2x 200, 4x 358), Os2 83, Os4 126. The driven ladder's five tanh calls dominate; SND-6 measures it inside Psy Bass's voice and may use a portable rational tanh if a voice gets too expensive.
- In the app (`tools/ui-tests/taskSND_0.py`, 9 of 9): the worklet module carries the kit once; all 18 probe cases give the same bits in the worklet as on the main thread; the other processors still load; nothing of the kit runs at start, with a song or while playing; no console errors.
- Old projects: Fractals Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) at master -10 dB, measured on main v0.277 and on this build (v0.278 before the last rebase; the file only gained other lanes' work since) with `tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`: every repeatable line the same hash (Saw, Pad, Acid, Wavetable, Venom and the four Fractals lines); Plant, Sampler, Sampler grains and Drum kit move between two renders of one build too (release gate, section e). Found: the extra line 'Fractals Bass, master put back to 0 dB' takes one of two exact values from run to run (-25.48699 dB 09e0415bec5e or -26.74483 dB a6774faed0a9), on v0.273 before the kit existed as well as after; the two master -10 dB lines the gate checks never moved. For whoever owns `export_same.py`'s master-0 pass (lane K or the gate): probably the master change is still settling when the render starts. `measure.py` (AE4) was not re-run: no device changed, so its numbers are those of `results.json`; each later step runs it before and after for its own device.
- A/B renders for listening, `tools/engine-lab/snd/renders/` (44.1 kHz, peaks at -6 dBFS): `sweep_tanh_plain_1x` against `sweep_tanh_adaa_2x` (a 1 to 8 kHz sweep into hard tanh: the whistling falling tones of the plain one are gone), `bass_ladder_linear` against `bass_ladder_driven_2x` (a K-B-B-B F1 line at 145 BPM), `acid_diode_linear` against `acid_diode_driven_2x`, `formant_morph` (a e i o u and back), `comb_plucks` (noise bursts tuned to A2, C3, E3, A3).
- Release gate: lint clean; the start-up smoke test in the desktop app clean in all 14 MIDI scenarios (20 s idle each, no state change, no console error, no command).

### For NB (native port)
Port `sndKitCore` statement by statement as `native/engine/core/snd_kit.h`: doubles throughout, `-ffp-contract=off`, no flush to zero (states below 1e-30 are zeroed by `flush()`, which the devices call), `ieee754::tan`, `exp`, `log1p`, `tanh` from `native/third_party/fdlibm` for `Math.tan`, `Math.exp`, `Math.log1p`, `Math.tanh`, `std::floor` for `Math.floor`. The Gauss-Jordan inversion in `invert` must keep its pivot order and loop order. Test: the 18 probe cases of `taskSND_0.py` (noise seed 777, 8192 samples) bit for bit. Nothing to port for sound yet, since no device uses it; port it with SND-1's Filter v2.

### Left
SND-1 (Filter v2 and Auto Filter models, B37) next; then SND-2 to SND-19 as `docs/sounds-build.md` lists. Then "built-in sounds complete". The user's AE1 picks (recorded while this step ran) are folded into the plan: Q1, Q6 with SND-12, Q2 with SND-7, Q3 with SND-8 and Growl, Q4, Q5 with SND-16, Q7, Q8 with SND-4; the v1/v2 modes use lane N's Quality field `q:'classic'|'clean'`; B30 (true peak) moves to lane N's SQ4.

## 27 November 2026, v0.283: Learn, the lesson runner and the four lessons (task LM-4a, lane M)
Step LM4a of task LM (the user's Learn picks N5 H1 P1 W1 L1 G1, `docs/research-learn-mode.md` 4.5 to 4.7 and section 6; the prototype `tools/design-lab/ux3/learn.html` is the reference for the lessons and checks). Edit script `tools/design-lab/lm/lm4a.py` (anchors: before `function askChoice(title,text,btns,icon){` and `.dacv{display:flex;`, the block between `/* ==LM4a-js== */` markers so a re-run replaces it), test `tools/ui-tests/taskLM_4a.py` (124 checks).

### Built
- **`LM_LESSONS`**, the four psytrance lessons as data, 4 to 6 steps each, on the user's own song: *A rolling bass* (tempo 143 to 147, Play, the three 16ths after each kick in the first bar of the Bass clip under the playhead, Decay shorter than a 16th, Cutoff moved more than 0.4 octave ending in 300 Hz to 2 kHz), *Sidechain kick and bass* (Play, pump on, Depth 50 to 80 %, release near a 16th: ratio 0.6 to 1.5, off and on again), *A build with a filter sweep* (loop the Build, Cutoff under 200 Hz, write on, Play, a written line over at least 40 % of the Build moving at least 35 % of the knob, write off with the line kept), *Mixing a drop* (loop the Drop and play, solo the kick, master peak -8 to -4 dBFS over a 1.5 s hold, unsolo, bass at least 2 dB under the kick with the peak under -1 dBFS, pump on with Depth 30 % or more). The level targets are written as starting points that leave room, not rules.
- Every step names a **released control id** (`data-al`: `transport.tempo`, `transport.play`, `transport.loop`, `track.name`, `track.edit`, `track.solo`, `track.volume`, `track.writeAutomation` with `track.recordAutomation` as an alternative) and, for controls that repeat per track, which track (`kick`, `bass`, found by name: a track called Kick or Bass, else one whose name or instrument says so). Device steps also name the device control id they will point at once lane H gives device knobs ids (`want`, DL7: `device.instrument.decay`, `device.instrument.cutoff`, `device.sidechain.power/depth/release`); until then they point at the Bass track's Edit channel button. Play goes through the command id `transport.play` (`runCommand`). No positions or selectors.
- **The runner** (`lmLs*`, `LM_RUN`): a step waits for a **state**, never a click (a key, a MIDI controller, the Assistant all count). A step already true says "Already done ✓ · moving on" and passes after 1.3 s; the two `mustAct` steps (Cutoff moved, pump switched twice) always wait for a fresh move. A reached state ticks ✓ and moves on after 1 s (1.4 s with reduced motion). Back, Skip step, **Do it for me** (where it helps) and End · Esc on every step. "Do it for me" (`LM_FIX`) is one undo step each (tempo, bass notes, Decay, pump, Depth, release, Cutoff, solo, unsolo); looping a section and switching automation write are not part of undo, as by hand. Filling the bass notes also writes the clip's linked copies; a step sequencer clip (FT-F9a) is left to its step editor.
- **Pointing** goes through **`LM_HOOKS.point(id, card)`**: lane F's `ovGuide(id, card)` when it exists (task LM1), else the stand-in `lmLsPoint`: one card (T3 look with the overlay tokens: amber label line, live value with amber units, step dots), one 1 px amber ring and one hairline leader with a dot at each end; only the card takes the pointer, it is placed on the side with room so it never covers its control or the controls the step asks you to watch (the master peak and meter in the mixing lesson), and it stays in the window. `card` = `{html, el, avoid, track, onAct, label}`; the handle is `{update(html), place(el), close()}`.
- **Cost**: no lesson, nothing: no element, timer or listener (one 12 s timeout at start for the first-run offer). While a lesson runs: one 150 ms timer reads the step's check (a few reads of the song) and re-places the card only when the text or the target's place changed; Esc and resize listeners only while a lesson runs.
- **Progress** (G1, quiet): `UI.lm = {p: {lessonId: steps passed or 'done'}, o: 1}`; a finished lesson shows "A rolling bass: done ✓ (1 of 4 lessons done)" as a toast (the N1 notification log is lane F's).
- **First-run offer**: once, 12 s after start, a small card at the bottom left lists the four lessons with their steps, minutes and ticks ("0 of 4 done"); a click starts one, Not now closes it. Never shown under automation (`navigator.webdriver`), with Settings, the mixer or a dialog open, or while a lesson runs.
- **For other lanes**: `LM_HOOKS.lessons()`, `start(id, step)`, `end()`, `active()`, `progress()` ("2 of 4 done"), `offer()` for lane F's Help menu (LM2) and the Assistant (LM6).

### Getters (LM_G) and what LM5 asks of other lanes
The checks read the song (`S`) and, for the master peak, the master meter's numbers read only (`MT2.l/r`, a 1.5 s hold kept by the lesson's own timer). Task LM5 moves these onto getters from their lanes; asked for here:
- **lane E (IN)**: `INS.masterPeak()` (the master's sample peak now, dBFS) or better `INS.masterPeakHold(ms)`; LM_G already uses `INS.masterPeak` when it exists.
- **lane K (MX)**: `MX_HOOKS.pump(trackId)` = `{on, depth (%), releaseMs, kind}` for the track's Sidechain or Ducker, so the lessons need not read device parameters.
- **lane C (FT)** or the automation owner: `FT_HOOKS.autoWrite(trackId)` (is write on for this track) and `FT_HOOKS.autoLine(trackId, a, b)` (cover and span of the written line in a range).
- **lane H (XT)**: device knob ids (DL7) for the `want` ids above, and a command id for automation write (`track.recordAutomation` has a button but no command).
- **lane F (OV)**: `ovGuide(id, card)` (LM1) with the card shape above; LM4b wires the lessons into the Help menu (LM2).

### Tested (`tools/ui-tests/taskLM_4a.py`, headless Chromium, 124 checks, all pass)
- The data: four lessons, 4 to 6 steps, every id in `CONTROLS`, every check, fix and live line present, commands resolve, no em dash, two mustAct steps.

## 27 November 2026, v0.284: task IN-O follow-up, the phase angle of the value shown (lane E, instruments)

Two IN runs built step IN-O at the same time: this one claimed it at 20:36 UTC (`ccf50b6`); a parallel run that had started before the claim released it as v0.280 at 21:05. This run's own version (24 checks passing, kept out of the repository so `INO` is not built twice) was dropped; nothing of it is in main. Comparing the two with known signals found one thing to fix in the released code:

- **The phase angle now matches the value it stands beside.** `inoCorr` (the strips' phase bar) and `inoMaster` (the master's Stereo box) took the angle from the unrounded correlation; arccos is steep near the ends, so a smoothed anti-phase pair read "−1.00  175°" and a mono pair "+1.00  6°". The angle is now taken from the two-decimal value shown: −1.00 is 180°, +1.00 is 0°, 0.00 is 90°. Edit script `tools/design-lab/in/in_o_fix1.py` (edits index.html and `in_o_block.js`, so `in_o.py` re-applies the same code; anchors asserted unique).
- **Tested:** `tools/ui-tests/taskIN_O.py` 28 of 28 (three new checks: the bar at ±0.996, the master box at −0.996, +0.996 and 0.004). No audio code; **Fractals levels unchanged**, measured on this file (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`): Kick −19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass −35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) at master −10 dB; at 0 dB Kick −9.75669 (0496bb147f6c), Bass −25.48699 (09e0415bec5e), as in the newest entries. Lint clean. The start-up smoke test of the release gate cannot run on the cloud machine (the gate stops before it: no release commit for its reference v0.250 here, and the Electron download is blocked), as in the earlier IN entries.
- **Noted from the comparison, for the scheduling chat** (not changed; v0.280 already does them): the afterglow layer at one pixel per CSS pixel is the right call; at full device resolution the layers cost about 2 ms a frame on the cloud machine with every strip on the stereo view (`frame0_cost.py` with `INVIEW=stereo`, five pairs: 17.8 against 20.2 ms), within the noise at one pixel per CSS pixel. `frame0_cost.py` in this run's copy took an `INVIEW` variable for that; v0.280 has `stereo_cost_o.py` for the same.
- **To avoid a second collision:** a run should check `git log origin/main` for a release of its step, not only the claim line, before releasing.

## 27 November 2026, v0.287: task SC-A, the science look's shared drawing module (lane G)
Step SC-A of `docs/science-look-round-2.md` ("Implementation order"), after the user's picks `W1 normal, W2 faint, W3 off, W4 faint, W5 normal, W6 normal, W7 normal, W8 normal, W9 faint, W10 faint, W11 faint, W12 faint, W13 faint, W14 off | X1 X2 X4 X5 X6 X7 X8 X9 X10 X11 X12 X14 X15 | Y1`. "task SC-A" was not in this log; claimed in "Where it stands" before the work. Invisible groundwork: no place shows a drawing yet. Edit script `tools/design-lab/sc/sc_a.py` with `sc_a_block.js` and `sc_a_css.txt` (two anchors, asserted unique: JS before `askChoice`, CSS before `.dacv`), test `tools/ui-tests/taskSC_A.py` (30 checks).

### Built
- **`SCI`** (block "v0.287 (task SC-A, lane G)"; named SCI because `SC` is a local name in older code): the drawings as plain functions that paint into any canvas context, ported from the round 2 pick page with today's colours: `SCI.D.orbits` (orbit chart S7: rings, tick ring, dashed cross, bodies; `o.ang` fixes each body's angle so W1 can lock them to the song position), `corner` (orbit corner B2), `field` (dipole field lines S1 and B3, optional surface and moving charges), `lissa` (Lissajous S4 with a moving dot), `harm` (string harmonics B4), `comb` (harmonic comb with the amber bracket that measures the pitch, W8), `spec` (a small spectrogram picture fed one column at a time by `push` or at a fixed column by `put`, drawn into a box with the amber line at the front, W6, W7, W12), `lab` (the small amber mono label) and `dot`. Each takes a strength k (faint 0.45, normal 1) and draws nothing at 0; labels only at normal.
- **Views and one timer**: `SCI.view({cv, place, paint, move})` sizes its canvas in device pixels (with the interface scale, up to 2x) and paints `paint(g,w,h,t,k,view)`. `move:false` (working surfaces) is one picture, painted again only when its size, level or the settings change. `move:true` (empty and waiting states) is painted by one shared timer at 30 pictures a second at most, only while its canvas is on screen; the timer stops by itself when no moving view is shown, `view.wake()` starts it again. Frames go through the app's frame gate, so the background freeze (task AO) holds them.
- **The rules in one place**: Motion other than Ambient (Appearance), "reduce motion" and Light mode make every view still; Light mode draws nothing (the user's W14 off; a canvas switched off is cleared once); `SCI_DEF` holds the user's strength per place (W3 and W14 off); `UI.scW` (hidden, no control) can override one place, e.g. `{W2:'off'}`. Without a view there is no timer, no class observer and no resize listener.
- **Setting**: Appearance, Density and motion, under Caliper while dragging: **Science drawings** (on; tooltip in plain language), in the settings table as `scOn` (`UI.scOn`). Off: no drawing anywhere, no timer.
- CSS: `.sciv`, a canvas that fills its place and takes no clicks (hidden in Light mode). Hooks for other lanes: `SCI_HOOKS.view`, `.level`, `.draw`, `.refresh`.

### Tested
- `tools/ui-tests/taskSC_A.py`, 30 of 30: the picks and levels; no view = no timer, observer or frames (counted over 1.5 s); the setting on its page, stored, off clears and stops; a test view: 26 to 28 pictures a second (SwiftShader), hidden = 0 frames and the timer stops, wake() resumes, faint without labels, Motion "Signal and transitions" one still picture and 0 frames, Light mode cleared and 0 frames, a still view drawn once and once more on resize, all views stopped = nothing left running; k 0 draws nothing; while playing the module draws nothing. ## 27 November 2026, v0.288: step sequencer clips, part 2 (task FT-F9b, lane C)
Step FT-F9b of `docs/features-build.md` (starred card F9 of `docs/research-features-gap.md`, section 4 "RF-F9 Step sequencer clips": the Roll preset, convert both ways, slide into Acid and Psy Bass). Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ft/ftF9b.py` with `ftF9b_block.js` (asserted anchors: three in F9a's own code, the end of F9a's block, the `clip.editSteps` command), test `tools/ui-tests/taskFT_F9b.py` (40 checks).

### Built
- **Pattern menu** in the step editor (beside Piano roll), one undo step, the menu goes back to Choose… afterwards. Note rows: **Roll (K B B B)**, the psytrance roll on the root: the bass on the three 16ths after each kick with the first of them lower (level 55 % against 75 %); **Gallop (K - B B)**; **Off-beat (K - B -)**; **Clear all**. Drum pads: **Four on the floor**; **Psy drums** (kick on every beat, clap on 2 and 4, closed hat on the off-beats at 60 %; the rows are found by the pads' types); **Clear all**. A pattern on 1/8 or 1/32 steps sets 1/16. Every entry has a tooltip.
- **Step clip to a normal MIDI clip**: clip menu **Make normal MIDI clip**, the editor's **Normal clip** button, command `clip.toNotes`. The notes stay exactly as they are; the steps are kept aside (`clip.stepsOld`) so turning it back is exact while the notes are unchanged; notes with a chance keep it (`clip.nch`: the chance roll of F9a now also runs for such a clip).
- **A MIDI clip to a step clip**: clip menu **Make step sequencer clip** (instrument tracks), command `clip.toSteps`. Exact when the clip was a step clip and its notes were not changed. Otherwise the notes are read: drum pads on a drum kit, otherwise 8 notes of the key in the octave that holds every note, or the clip's own notes as rows ("Notes of the clip", up to 16; Oct + and Oct − move them, Follow key gives the key's rows); the step size that fits (1/16 first, then 1/32, then 1/8); 2 to 4 even hits of one note in a step become a ratchet; a note longer than its step a slide; level, accent (on Acid a velocity over 0.88), chance; the gate from the median length. Notes off the steps move to the nearest one, and the toast says how many moved and how many lengths changed (Mod+Z undoes it). More than 16 different notes: refused with a message.
- **Accent and slide into Acid**: Acid takes an accent from a velocity over 0.88 and glides into a note that starts while the last one still sounds. An accented step now always writes at least 0.9, and on an Acid track a plain step at most 0.88, so level and accent no longer mix up; a slide step already writes a note 5 % longer than its step, so the next note glides (checked in a render through the voice engine: a glide into the note after the slide step and only there). Only new or edited step clips change; nothing else is touched.
- **Psy Bass**: its engine starts every note afresh (wave, filter and envelopes), so a slide there needs a change inside the engine, which is lane L's (`psbCore`, `psbPlay`; Psy Bass v2 is their SND-6). Not done here; the request is in the hook table of `docs/features-build.md`: a note that overlaps the next should glide into it, same rule as Acid. Step clips already write the notes that way.
- **Push 1's drum step lane** (C2b) on a step clip in drum mode: the top two rows show and edit the pattern steps of the selected pad under the playhead (one undo step a press, no new clip made over it); Delete + pad clears that pad's steps in the bar.
- Linked copies follow (`nch` and `stepsOld` joined `LK.MIDI`). Hook `FT_HOOKS.stepConvert`. No settings rows.

### Tested (`tools/ui-tests/taskFT_F9b.py`, headless Chromium, 40 checks, all pass)
- Fractals untouched (no step or converted clips, the same notes array). Roll on Psy Bass: steps 2, 3, 4 of every beat on the root A, first hit lower, one undo step; Psy drums on the kit's own kick, clap and closed hat pads. Acid: accent at level 60 % plays at 0.9, a plain full step at 0.88, the slide note overlaps, and the render glides into the next note only. To normal and back (menus with tooltips): the same notes, chance kept and rolled, the same steps back, undo. Reading notes: a pattern with ratchets 3 and 2, slide, accent, a low level and chance comes back as the same steps and the same notes; notes on 8ths, on 32nds (1/32 steps), off the grid (moved), outside the key (own rows, Oct +), 20 different notes (refused). Push 1 (fake): the lane shows the step clip's kicks, a press turns a pattern step on with its note, Delete + pad clears, undo. A linked copy becomes normal too; saved with the song; no em dash; no timer or frame when idle; no console errors.

## 27 November 2026, v0.289: task LT-1, the output check and the playing buffer (lane J, the user's AE2 picks L1 and L2)

Step LT-1 of `docs/latency-build.md` (research id AE2-1). Edit script `tools/engine-lab/lt/lt_1.py` (unique asserted anchors), test `tools/ui-tests/taskLT_1.py` (42 checks), measurement `tools/engine-lab/lt/lt1_measure.py` (the method of `latency_chain.py`; results in `lt1_measure_result.json`).

### Built
- **L1, the output check.** When the engine starts, when devices change and when the output is changed (events only, no timer), AudioLab looks at the output in use (lane B's device scan `adScan`, read only; on the Mac desktop app also the helper's transport and rate) and warns when it is Bluetooth, eqMac (labels ending in "(eqMac)"), a virtual device (Background Music, BlackHole, Soundflower, Loopback, an aggregate such as Cubase System Sound Link, call apps' devices), a device in call mode (16 or 8 kHz), or (desktop only) a device reporting more than 40 ms. The notice says why in plain words and has one button "Play through <wired device>": the wired output picked before (`UI.ltWired`), else a known DAC or interface (iFi, Zoom AMS-24, Focusrite, RME, MOTU, Apogee, Audient, SSL, UA), else any USB output that is not virtual. It sets the output through the Settings output select (lane B's handler: `setSinkId`, `UI.sink`). "Keep this output" stops warnings for that device (`UI.ltOkOut`); "Not now" for this session. Shown with `askChoice` (lane F has no notification API yet): `LT_HOOKS.notify` is the one place to switch to lane F's notice.
- **L2, the playing buffer.** While a track is armed or the computer keyboard plays notes and the song is stopped, the engine runs at 128 frames with 64-frame render blocks (Chromium 158 here gives 64; checked with `ctx.renderQuantumSize`). The switch happens only while stopped, 0.45 s after the last click or key, never while a key or note is held or while recording. A restart costs 115 to 145 ms on the main thread here (measured), too long to add to every Play, so **Play keeps the playing buffer**; if it crackles while the song plays, AudioLab goes to the mixing buffer at once (keeps playing, one message), and from then on in this session starts every Play on the mixing buffer and comes back to the playing buffer at Stop. The read-out under Output latency says "playing buffer 128 samples, blocks of 64".
- **Auto comes back down.** After a clean minute of playing on the mixing buffer, Auto marks one step down (2,048 to 1,024 to 512 to 256, never below 256), applied at the next Stop. Steps up and down are at least a minute apart; a step up within two minutes of a step down doubles the clean time needed (up to 8 minutes), so it cannot swing. Dropouts heard at the playing buffer never raise Auto.
- **Settings:** two rows under Render blocks: "Playing buffer" (128, 256, Off; default 128) and "Check the output device" (on), with tooltips, in the settings table (`STT`) and offered to lane B as `LT_HOOKS.audioRows`. The Auto option now reads "goes up when it hears dropouts, back down after a clean minute".
- Hooks in shared code: one line in `ensureCtx` (`LT_HOOKS.ctxOpts(o)`, sets the latency hint and render block); lane J's own `autoBufCheck` and the Auto interval ignore dropouts heard at the playing buffer. Wrappers on `ensureCtx`, `restartAudio`, `start`, `stop` and `latency` the way other lanes wrap them. New keys `UI.ltPlayBuf`, `UI.ltOutChk`, `UI.ltWired`, `UI.ltOkOut` are optional; `UI.buf`, `UI.abuf`, `UI.rq` keep their meaning.

### Measured (this build machine: headless Chromium 158, no sound card)
- Key press to the first heard sample, Lead armed, Auto 256, idle, 16 presses, two runs each: **before (v0.277) median 40.9 / 42.1 ms, worst 54.9 / 56.1 ms; after median 22.2 / 21.1 ms, worst 38.7 ms** (one press in the first run waited 198 ms on the main thread before the handler ran, a main-thread pause, not the buffer). The buffer part ("ahead") went from 34 to 35 ms to 9.2 ms; the render block from 128 to 64, base latency from 10 to 2.9 ms. The main-thread part rose a little (median 5 to 7 ms before, 10 ms after): twice as many render blocks also means more meter messages to the page; L6 (a lighter main thread, later) is where that is won back.
- **Exports unchanged**, measured with `tools/engine-tests/export_same.py` on this build and on v0.277: Fractals Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) at master -10 dB; -9.75669 (0496bb147f6c) and -25.48699 dB (09e0415bec5e) at 0 dB. Saw, Pad, Acid, Wavetable, Venom and the other repeatable lines identical; Plant, Sampler, Sampler grains and Drum kit differ from run to run on v0.277 itself (two runs of v0.277 differ the same way), so they are not compared.
- `taskLT_1.py` 42 of 42: rows, defaults, tooltips, search, no em dashes; arm while stopped gives 64-frame blocks; Play and Stop keep it; injected dropouts switch to the mixing buffer without raising Auto, then Play starts on the mixing buffer and Stop returns; Off; keyboard playing; no switch while a key is held; a clean minute takes Auto from 1,024 to 512 at Stop; dropouts at Stop still raise it and then two clean minutes are needed; never below 256; fake outputs: Bose via eqMac (eqMac and Bluetooth), Background Music, BlackHole, Cubase System Sound Link (virtual), the Bose by Bluetooth, 16 kHz call mode flagged, the iFi and the speakers not; the notice's button names the iFi and sets the output and remembers it; Keep this output silences it; the check off; no console errors. ## 27 November 2026, v0.291: task XT-DL12, the script sandbox spike (extensions and the Workshop, lane H, third step)
Row DL12 of docs/extensions-plan.md 9.7 (9.6 e, the sandbox of user scripts). Invisible groundwork: nothing calls it yet, nothing looks or behaves differently. Findings and the decision in **`docs/script-sandbox.md`**.

### Decided
- **A Worker inside a sandboxed iframe with its own content security policy**, not QuickJS. QuickJS (quickjs-emscripten 0.31, measured in Node) would add 692 kB of base64 to the single file and ran a 10-million-step loop in 1424 ms against 18 ms; its strengths (a hard memory limit, an interrupt) are matched by the frame's own process and by removing the frame. QuickJS stays the fallback if a future Chromium or Electron weakens a wall; the tests would notice.

### What was built
- `xtSandboxRun(code, {input, limit, onSlow, onLog})`, resolving to `{ok, value, changes, logs, error, line, stopped, ms}` and never rejecting; `xtSandboxStop(id)`; `XT_SBX` (limits). Each run: a hidden iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts"` only (opaque origin), a `srcdoc` with the policy `default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline' blob:; worker-src blob:`, a blob Worker that holds the user's code inside an async function with a prelude (`console`, `al.input` a frozen copy, `al.change`), one `MessageChannel` to the page (no listener on the page), every message checked and capped (200 log lines, 10,000 changes, 1 MB back, 256 kB of code).
- Time limit 2 s; `onSlow` is asked at each limit and may say wait (the user's K9b; the card is DL13's). A heartbeat from the frame: no beat for 1.5 s means its process died (memory). Stopping removes the frame, which ends the worker even in an endless loop. A finished run leaves no frame, worker, listener or timer; before the first run nothing exists.
- Code: block "SCRIPT SANDBOX (v0.291, task XT-DL12)" before `askChoice`; edit script `tools/edits/taskXT_DL12.py` with `taskXT_DL12_block.js`. No CSS. Names use the lane's `xt` prefix.
- `docs/commands.md`: three commands other lanes added were not listed (lane C v0.277 `clip.newSteps`, `clip.editSteps`, v0.288 `clip.toSteps`, `clip.toNotes`; lane D v0.279 `ni.levelJourney`), so `taskXT_DL2.py` failed (as it is meant to); listed now, 24 of 24 again. For lanes C and D (and every lane): a new `SCA` row needs a row in docs/commands.md.

### Tested
- `tools/ui-tests/taskXT_DL12.py`: 85 of 85 (two passes: the browser version, and cross-origin isolated as the desktop app serves it; Chromium with site isolation on). Escape attempts, each refused, with a local server that must see no request: fetch (cors and no-cors), XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, importScripts, import(), a worker from a URL, eval, new Function, setTimeout with a string, indexedDB, caches, a BroadcastChannel to the page, the page's globals and the desktop bridge, forged messages, breaking out of the wrapper; a worker from a blob is made but keeps the same walls. Two controls: the page itself reaches the server, and the same sandbox with its policy lifted reaches it, so the walls are the policy's. An endless loop stopped at the limit while the page kept drawing (57 frames in 1 s) and the sound kept playing; wait or stop; a 1.7 s wait finishes; the caps; error lines; a memory bomb dies in its own process (61 s) and the page lives.
- `tools/ui-tests/taskXT_DL12_electron.js`, the real desktop app (Electron 45.4.1, `audiolab://`, cross-origin isolated, the bridge present): 21 of 21. The sandbox frame has its own process (main 4823, frame 4880) and origin `null`; network, eval, the bridge, `audiolab://` refused; the server saw nothing; an endless loop stopped at 1005 ms with 63 frames drawn; a memory bomb died alone in 9.6 s and the next script ran. No switch is needed in `desktop/main.js` (site isolation is on by default).
- Without site isolation (Playwright's default, not Chrome's or Electron's) a memory bomb left running for about 45 s crashes the whole page; 8 s did not. DL13 should cap "wait" unless the frame is known to have its own process.
- Load time (3 runs to ready): before 1.89, 1.65, 1.78 s; after 1.57, 1.55, 1.57 s. Frame time with Fractals playing: before 18.1, 17.0, 17.5 ms; after 18.2, 17.2, 18.4 ms. Same within noise.
- **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`, measured on this file and on v0.290): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; Kick -9.75669 dB (0496bb147f6c), Bass -25.48699 dB (09e0415bec5e) at 0 dB, beats 64 to 96. Plant, Sampler grains, Sampler and Drum kit differ between two runs of the unchanged v0.278 file as well (not repeatable).
- taskXT_DL1 21/21, taskXT_DL2 24/24; lint clean; no console errors. Start-up smoke test (`tools/release-gate/smoke_electron.js`, the desktop app, 20 s each, scenarios real, none, keyboard, push1-loop, iac-push, noise): all clean, no state change, no console error. The full quick gate was started twice but main moved on (v0.278 to v0.287 in half an hour) before it finished, so the smoke test was run directly on the final rebase. ## 27 November 2026: task NB-N3f (the Compressor: Chromium's DynamicsCompressorNode, bit for bit)

Fired by the scheduler at about 21:35 UTC. N2c still waits for the design chain (the user's order: the design first; v0.287 SC-A was the last design release), so the next stage not done is stage 3's devices, in the order the built-in song needs them: after the Pro EQ (N3e) the compressor (Fractals: Kick & Bass, Drums and the master). No other NB run had pushed since 20:50. `index.html`, `desktop/` (also `desktop/app-version.json`), `native/host/` and `native/testapp/` (task NL8) untouched; no version.

### Built
- `native/engine/core/dyncomp.h`: Chromium 158.0.8127.36's DynamicsCompressor (platform/audio/dynamics_compressor.cc, which now holds the old kernel too), the handler's once-per-quantum parameters (dynamics_compressor_handler.cc) and audio_utilities' DecibelsToLinear, LinearToDecibels and DiscreteTimeConstantForSampleRate. Every maths call goes where Chromium's goes: `fdlibm::asinf` and `fdlibm::powf` where the source names fdlibm; the system's `powf` and `log10f` in audio_utilities (called unqualified there), the system's double `exp` in the knee and double `sin` in the gain warp. The 32-frame divisions sit on a fixed grid from the first frame, with the envelope of a division kept across calls, so any call size gives the same bits (Chromium starts them at each quantum, and 128 and 512 are multiples of 32). AudioParams: float, clamped to their ranges. Reusable for the Sidechain device's two compressors.
- `native/engine/core/dev_comp.h`: the app's `comp` (input GainNode at 1, the compressor with knee 6 dB, make-up GainNode at `Math.pow(10, makeup/20)` rounded to float); a mono input comes out with two channels, as from the browser node. Meters: reduction (dB) and latency (frames). Registered as `comp`.
- `make_ref_core.py`: `comp` in TYPES; extras: Fractals' three settings (`frx-kickbass`, `frx-drums`, `frx-master`, read from the song's own project in v0.287), the ends of every range, values past the AudioParams' ranges (`x-past-ranges`: the browser clamps them, and its own make-up at a -100 dB threshold gives a peak of 988, which the port matches), no compression, odd values; chains `chain-comp-bus` (EQ, compressor preset, limiter) and `chain-comp-crush` (two compressors around a Bitcrusher and a chorus). `make_bus_ref.py`: scenes `compbus` and `compbus128`; refs in `ref/bus` (made with app v0.287; the other scenes' entries kept).

### Proven (Linux, this machine, headless Chromium 158.0.8127.36)
- Devices: **49 of 49 compressor cases bit for bit** (every preset, the extras, the two chains) at 1, 7, 33, 64, 128, 512 and 4,096 frames per call; the first build matched at once.
- The export's quantum (512) references for comp, eq, limit, crush and chorus: **172 of 172** at 512, 128 and 7 frames per call.
- Buses: **18 of 18 identical** (new: the compressor on a group, on a mono source, on a return and on the master before its limiter, with 288 frames of compensation on the other tracks; at 512 and 128).
- Cost: 5.2 µs (Fractals' master setting) to 6.7 µs (hard settings) per 128 stereo frames, 400 to 510 times real time on one core.
- **GitHub, native-ci run 46072672120 (dispatched with the Mac job), every job green.** Apple Silicon (macos-latest, against the Mac's own Chromium, so Apple's powf, log10f, exp and sin on both sides): **340 of 340 device cases bit for bit** (every ported device and preset, the 49 compressor cases among them), **18 of 18 bus scenes** with the Mac's own references (compbus and compbus128 included), N3b's mixer identical. Linux: 340 of 340 in Release and under ASan+UBSan at 128 frames, 339 of 340 at 7 frames (the known two-random-device chain, review A2); buses, mixer, the engine on the null device, the edit protocol, TSan, the bridge, the Electron feeder: all green.

### Found on the way (for lane K, mixing engine)
- At 44.1 kHz the app's `fxLat` says the compressor is `Math.round(.006 * 44100)` = 265 frames late, but Chromium's pre-delay is `unsigned(0.006f * 44100.f)` = 264 (truncated). So at 44.1 kHz the web engine's delay compensation puts a track with a compressor (and OTT, whose dry path is built the same way) one frame off against the others. At 48 kHz both are 288. The native engine will compensate with the compressor's own figure (`latencyFrames`); lane K may want `Math.floor(Math.fround(.006) * sr)` in `fxLat`. Not changed here (not this lane's code).

### Left
- The rest of Fractals' devices: the sidechain pump (two of these compressors, a sawtooth OscillatorNode synced to the beat, a WaveShaperNode without oversampling, a ConstantSourceNode), the clipper (WaveShaperNode at 4x: Chromium's up and down samplers, a DelayNode, a highpass biquad), the tempo delay, the plate reverb (ConvolverNode: measure).
- The compressor's parameters automated, and its tail after the input is disconnected (it matters with clips as sources).

### Assumptions
- The first call of a device is the start of its 32-frame grid (in the app the node starts at a quantum boundary, so the grid is the same).
- Chromium 158's source stands for the Electron the app ships for these files, as in N3e.

## 27 November 2026, v0.292: task NI-8, the mono-loss map (lane D, idea I4)

Idea I4 is complete. Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ni/ni_8.py` with `ni_8_block.js` (anchored; needs NI-7), test `tools/ui-tests/taskNI_8.py` (32 checks, all pass). The step was claimed in the plan before it started.

### Built
- **A window "Mono loss"** (the app's floating window: moves, resizes, remembers its place). It opens from:
  - the main menu (right-click the logo: Mono loss…)
  - the command `ni.monoLoss`
  - a small **Loss** button next to Mono, Dim and L↔R on the master strip
- **One row per track that plays** in the range (not groups, returns or muted tracks):
  - a band strip from 20 Hz to 20 kHz (1/6 octave, NI-3's bands), each band coloured by how much of that track's level is lost in mono there: cyan holds, grey −3 dB (wide or one-sided), amber −6 dB (partly cancels), red −12 dB and more (cancels); faint where the band is quiet for that track
  - the whole track's loss in dB (power over its bands)
  - the worst stretch in words, for example "−10.0 dB at 381 to 427 Hz" (amber from 3.5 dB, red from 6 dB), else "wide, nothing cancels" or "holds up in mono"
  - click a row to select the track
- **How the per-band loss is measured**: from NI-3's per-beat mid and side bands (the cache; nothing new is rendered for it): loss = mid / (mid + side) in power, summed over the beats where the track plays. A centred mono sound loses 0 dB, a hard-panned or uncorrelated wide sound 3 dB, out-of-phase content more.
- **Tracks that cancel each other in mono** are joined by a line beside their names, with a sentence under the rows: "Left and Right cancel at 143 to 180 Hz: they cancel out in mono, fine in stereo" (or "in stereo too (−x dB)").
  - Found on their own renders: the 8 loudest tracks of the range, each rendered offline on its own after its fader and pan (NI-7's one-track render, at 22.05 kHz, at most 8 bars).
  - Compared pair by pair per 1/3 octave in a worker: a pair is named where the two together lose at least 3 dB in mono against the sum of their powers, both are within 15 dB of each other, and the band matters for the pair.
- **Hear in mono**: the master strip's Mono switch, from the window.
- **Range**: the loop when it is on, else the 8 bars around the playhead (as the level journey), or the whole song (switch; the pairs are then still checked around the playhead, and the window says which bars).
- **When it runs**: it measures again 0.8 s after an edit or a move settles, only while the song is stopped. A 300 ms check runs only while the window is open. Closing stops it.
- **Hooks**:
  - `NI_HOOKS.monoLoss` (`open`, `measure`, `tracks`) for NI-11 Ask the mix.
  - `NI_HOOKS.mxMon(w)`, called by one added call in the mixer's render after `monPaint()`, adds the Loss button. Whoever rebuilds the master strip keeps that call.
  - NI-7's `NI_jourRender` (lane D's own) learned `taps.raw` and `taps.sr`. Its normal use is unchanged; the test checks this.

### Checked
- **Test song** (audio, 120 BPM, 32 beats):
  - **Pad**: a 100 Hz sine in both channels plus a 400 Hz sine at +1 left and −0.5 right. Its 400 Hz band loses **9.96 dB** (computed −10.0 dB) and its 100 Hz band 0.0 dB. The worst stretch reads "−10.0 dB at 381 to 427 Hz".
  - **Mono** (1 kHz, both channels): 0.0 dB in every band, "holds up in mono".
  - **Left** (150 Hz on the left only) and **Right** (the same sine inverted on the right only): **3.01 dB** each, not flagged. Together they are the **one pair**: they cancel completely in mono and lose 0 dB in stereo. The line joins exactly their two rows.
  - With Right muted, it has no row and there is no pair. With Right playing 2.5 kHz instead, there is no pair and the window says so.
- **Window and controls**:
  - Range: beats 0 to 32 at beat 12; the loop 8 to 24; whole song 0 to 32.
  - Hear in mono switches the master's Mono and back.
  - The Loss button on the master strip opens the window.
  - Idle for 2 s: nothing measured. Closing stops the check.
- **Live path and exports**: a render of Pad is bit-identical before and after the map measured it, and the level journey reads the same numbers before and after.
- **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py` on this build): Kick −19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass −35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at −10 dB; −9.75669 (0496bb147f6c) and −25.48699 dB (09e0415bec5e) at 0 dB; the other nine lines the same checksums.
- **Also**: `taskNI_7.py` 24 of 24. Lint clean. Rebased onto v0.291 (lanes C, L and others), the edit script re-run on the fresh file, `taskNI_8.py` 32 of 32 again. The release gate (`gate.py --here --skip-ui --quick`, never promotes) passed its export step (Fractals levels and the 9 repeatable lines bit-identical to v0.250); its start-up smoke test, frame times and windows steps could not run on this cloud machine (the Electron binary download is blocked here, as in earlier runs). The UI tests load the whole app in Chromium with no console errors.
- Tooltips on every control, row, column and line; no em dashes in the UI text; no console errors.
- **Screenshots looked at**: the test song; the master strip with the Loss button; Fractals at bars 29 to 36, normal and Light level. In that stretch of Fractals every track holds up in mono (0.0 to 0.4 dB), except the Pad: −2.0 dB, wide. No pair cancels among the 8 loudest.

### Limits and what only the user can judge
- The per-band numbers come from NI-3's renders, which go through the master chain, so a stereo widener on the master shows on every track. The pairs are measured without the master.
- The pairs are checked only among the 8 loudest tracks and only up to 11 kHz (the renders run at 22.05 kHz).
- A track with reverb or chorus reads as "wide" (about −3 dB in its upper bands). That is expected, not a fault.
- **What to try**: open Mono loss on a drop of your own song and look for amber or red stretches. A stereo bass or a doubled pad with a flipped copy shows up there. Then press Hear in mono to hear what the strip shows. Say whether the Loss button on the master strip is the right place, or whether a strip per mixer channel would help more.

### Left
Group U, next: NI-9, the harmonic ruler (I5).

## 27 November 2026, v0.293: Volume Shaper, part 1 (task FT-F16a, lane C)
Step FT-F16a of `docs/features-build.md` (starred card F16 of `docs/research-features-gap.md`, section 4 "RF-F16 Volume shaper"). Edit script `tools/feature-lab/ft/ftF16a.py` with `ftF16a_block.js` (one asserted anchor: the LFO Shaper's `shApply` line, after which `ND`, `ANOUT` and the shaper helpers are ready), test `tools/ui-tests/taskFT_F16a.py` (24 checks). Also in this run: the AE3 picks (FT-X8 with X9, FT-X10, FT-X11 after MX-1, FT-X20; X14, X15, X21, X22 and X26 into F27, F18b, F25b and F29) and the UX1 picks (FT-S1, FT-S2, FT-S4; S18 with FT-X8) are folded into the plan's order.

### Built
- **Volume Shaper**, a new effect in the Modulation group of the browser (type `ftvs`): the volume follows a drawn curve, one cycle per **1/4 note, 1/2 note, 1 bar or 2 bars**, the cycles starting on the song's bar lines. **Depth** (how far down the curve goes), **Smooth** (0 to 20 ms, default 1 ms, softens hard steps without moving them), **Offset** (shifts the curve in its cycle), **Snap** (dragged points land on the song's 16ths or 32nds, or anywhere; two points at the same place make a hard step), Smooth segments, and Add point, Remove point, Invert, Reverse, Double, Flat (each one undo step). The dots are dragged as in the LFO Shaper (white points, yellow bends).
- **Locked to the sample**: the gain is worked out for every sample in a small worklet of its own (`al-ftvs`) from the song's beat: the tempo map (jumps and ramps), the play start and every loop jump arrive as an anchor (a context time and the beat there) that takes over at its exact frame; a tempo edit while playing re-anchors it; while stopped it runs on in tempo. An export, bounce or freeze starts the curve at the render's first beat, so the result is the same as when playing. The LFO Shaper (an 8 kHz looped buffer) is unchanged.
- **15 presets**: Sidechain (Kickstart style): Kick duck 1/4, Short duck, Long pump, Gentle pump, Half-time pump, Psy roll gap (the first 16th of each beat off, for a rolling bass); Gates (LFOTool style): Gate 1/8, Gate 1/16, Off-beat 1/8, Trance 3-3-2; Swells: Swell 1 bar, Swell 2 bars, Tremolo 1/8.
- **The display**: the curve as a gain (depth applied) over a grid of the song's beats and 16ths (LOOK tokens), the signal of the last cycle folded over it (input grey, output green, from the worklet 20 times a second and only while there is sound; it fades after 1.5 s of silence), the song's place as a line with a dot on the curve, the cycle length and the dB range. Tooltips on Length, Snap, Smooth segments and every button.
- Not touched: the audio graph (lane K), lane L's worklet bundle (the shaper loads its own module beside it), the device frame (lane I). Hook `FT_HOOKS.volumeShaper` = `{type, beats(p), gainAt(p, beat)}` so lane A can draw the curve behind the track's waveform in the arrangement. No settings rows.

### Tested (`tools/ui-tests/taskFT_F16a.py`, headless Chromium, 24 checks, all pass)
- The device and its 15 presets; Fractals has none. In the worklet with a constant input: the Psy roll gap's point at 1/16 lands on frame 4966 at 145 BPM and 48 kHz (0.25 beat is 4965.5 frames: the first frame at or after it), frame 4563 at 44.1 kHz; the next beat's gap starts on frame 19863 and ends on 24828; a render starting at beat 0.125 keeps the curve on the song's grid; with a tempo change to 120 BPM at beat 1 the next step lands where the tempo map puts it (frame 15932); Smooth 1 ms rises from the same sample and is 63 % there after 1 ms.
- **Export**: a saw track with Kick duck 1/4 at 145 BPM, rendered with the device on and off: the shaped render is the dry render times the curve at the song's beat (4168 samples checked, worst difference 0.0145 of full scale, from the 1 ms smoothing), and it dips on every beat.
- Live: the worklet runs and sends the last cycle while playing; silent and stopped it sends nothing; a 4-beat loop with a 2-bar cycle: after the loop jump the curve is back where the song is. Add point and Flat are one undo step each; Snap 1/16 puts a dragged point on a 16th; saved with the song; tooltips; no em dash; no console errors. Screenshots looked at: playing (the duck curve with the saw's last cycle over it), and with a 2-bar cycle and the Light level.
- Also: `taskFT_F9b.py` 40/40; lint clean; start-up smoke test (`tools/release-gate/smoke_electron.js`, 14 of 14 MIDI scenarios clean at 30 s each, run on v0.290 before the last rebase onto v0.292; after the rebase the lint and this step's test again); **Fractals levels unchanged** (`tools/engine-tests/export_same.py`): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB.

### Only the user can test
- Put a Volume Shaper on the rolling bass (or any pad) and choose Kick duck 1/4 or Psy roll gap; play with the kick: the dip sits on the kick every beat, also after a loop jump and in an export. Drag a point; with Snap 1/16 it lands on the song's 16ths.

### Left
- FT-F16b: triggered by notes of another track (ghost kick) or by audio, up to three bands (only the lows duck). The curve behind the waveform in the arrangement: lane A through `FT_HOOKS.volumeShaper`. Lane E may restyle the display, lane L may move the processor into the shared bundle. Next in lane C: **FT-F16b**.

## 27 November 2026, v0.294: task MX-1, pre or post per send and output to any bus (lane K, mixing engine)
Step MX-1 of `docs/mixing-build.md` (the user's AE3 picks X12 and X13, `docs/research-mixing.md`). Edit script `tools/engine-lab/mx/mx1.py` with `mx1.js` (asserted unique anchors: `busRoute`, `abxReach`, three in `renderMix`, two in `mxSends`, two in `abxOpts`; new JS before `askChoice`, new CSS before `.dacv`), test `tools/ui-tests/taskMX_1.py` (49 checks).

### Built
- **X12 pre or post per send.** `t.sendPre = {returnId: true}` (optional; absent = after the fader and pan, as before). A pre send is taken after the track's effects, delay compensation, width, phase and trim and before the fader, through one gain per track (`N.mxPre`) that follows Mute and Solo; it sleeps with the track (lane J's sleeping tracks). In the mixer each send bar has a ring: **yellow after the fader, blue before it**; click to switch (one undo step, tooltip). Export builds the same.
- **X13 output to any bus.** `t.out` = id of a group, a return or another track, or `'master'` (optional; absent = its group, else the master, as before). `t.grp` stays the arrangement's folder: nothing is regrouped. An **Output** button under each strip's effects (not on the master) opens a menu: Master, Groups, Returns, Tracks; refused entries are greyed with the reason. Into a track, the sound plays through that track's devices and fader with its own clips (resampling; recording it is lane C's). The cable menu offers **Play into <return or track>** and, for a routed channel, **Play straight into the Master**. A group or return that is not its folder: its fader and effects apply.
- **One loop check** for outputs, sends and Ducker triggers (`abxReach` follows outputs now). A loop written into a file by hand: the output gives way (plays into its group or the master, the button outlined red) and the send stays; a send that would close a loop is greyed and silent with the reason as its tooltip.
- **Solo**: a soloed track keeps the track, group or return it plays into audible (as a soloed member keeps its group). **Sleeping tracks**: a track, group or return that an awake track plays into stays awake (a wrapper on `slpTick`, see Left).
- **Export now renders a track's width, phase and trim** (the live graph always had them; `renderMix` did not). Only for tracks where they are not neutral, so older projects that never touched them render bit-identically. Pre sends and Ducker triggers in export are taken after them, as live.
- Hooks `window.MX_HOOKS`: `links()` (every link `{k:'out'|'send'|'sc', a, b, pre, lv, tap, lat}`), `canLink(a,b,kind)` → `{ok, why}`, `outOf(t)`, `setOut(t,id)`, `outMenu(t,x,y)`, `isPre(t,rid)`, `setPre(t,rid,on)`, `tap(t,'in'|'fx'|'fader'|'group')`.

### Tested (`tools/ui-tests/taskMX_1.py`, headless Chromium, 49 checks, all pass)
- A 1 kHz tone, its direct sound sent into a muted track so only the return is heard: post send at half level -6.02 dB below the tone; fader -12 dB → return -12.000 dB (post), 0.000 dB (pre); pre equals post at 0 dB; Mute silences both. Output to a group, a return and a track: the tone arrives at 0.000 dB and muting that bus silences it (nothing reaches the master directly); a group's fader applies; Solo keeps the bus; loops refused with "Tone already plays into Resample, so this would make a loop."; a hand-written loop falls back and still renders. **Live equals export** in every scene (analyser on the live master against `renderMix`, within 0.001 dB), and trim -6 dB now -6.000 dB in both. UI: output button on every strip with tooltip, yellow ring, real click turns it blue, undo, the output menu by mouse routes the tone into Perc glue and the button says so; cable menu items; no console errors. Screenshots looked at (rings, output buttons, menu).
- **Fractals levels unchanged** (measured on this build): Kick -19.05560 dB (fb577dd5202b), Bass -35.48685 dB (392ec52590c7) with the master at -10 dB; the full mix beats 64 to 96 hashes the same before and after (a5d0e1bfe9bd). Beats 0 to 32 already differ from render to render on v0.277 itself (about 0.0001 dB), so they are not a reference. Fractals has no width, phase or trim set.
